# Coming from Laravel

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/concepts/coming-from-laravel/

# Coming from Laravel

This page is for Laravel developers: it shows the Laravel way and the Dox way side by side.

The Laravel code is Laravel 11. The biggest changes are in [What is different](#what-is-different).

## Routing

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `Route::get('/ping', fn () => 'pong');` | `Route.get('/ping', (DoxRequest req) => 'pong');` |
| `Route::post('/blogs', [BlogController::class, 'store']);` | `Route.post('/blogs', (BlogController c) => c.store);` |
| `Route::get('/blogs/{id}', ...)` and `function show(int $id)` | `Route.get('/blogs/{id}', ...)` and `show(int id)` |
| `Route::get('/posts/{page?}', ...)` | `Route.get('/posts/{page?}', (int? page) => ...)` |
| `->where('path', '.*')` | `Route.get('/docs/{page*}', (String page) => ...)` |
| `->where('id', '[0-9]+')` | `Route.get('/users/{id}', ...).where('id', '[0-9]+')` |
| `Route::match(['get', 'post'], '/contact', ...)` | `Route.match(<String>['GET', 'POST'], '/contact', ...)` |
| `Route::any('/webhook', ...)` | `Route.any('/webhook', ...)` |
| `Route::redirect('/here', '/there')` | `Route.redirect('/here', '/there')` |
| `Route::permanentRedirect('/here', '/there')` | `Route.permanentRedirect('/here', '/there')` |
| `Route::fallback(...)` | `Route.fallback(...)` |
| `Route::prefix('blogs')->group(function () { ... });` | `Route.group('/blogs', () { ... });` |
| `Route::middleware('auth')->group(...)` | `Route.middleware(<dynamic>[AuthMiddleware()], () { ... });` |
| `Route::domain('admin.app.test')->group(...)` | `Route.domain('admin.app.test', () { ... });` |
| `Route::resource('blogs', BlogController::class);` | `Route.resource('blogs', BlogController);` |
| `Route::view('/welcome', 'welcome')` | `Route.get('/welcome', (DoxRequest req) => view(req, 'welcome'))` with `view()` of `dox_view`. Dox `Route.view` is the WebDAV `VIEW` method, not a template. |
| `routes/api.php` with the `api` prefix | `lib/routes/api.dart`, a `Router` class with `prefix => 'api'` |

In Dox, the container makes the controller. Put `@Inject()` above the class. The route picks the method with a typed function.

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/blogs', (BlogController c) => c.index);
    Route.resource('users', UserController);
  }
}
```

## Controllers

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `php artisan make:controller BlogController` | `dox make:controller Blog` |
| `php artisan make:controller BlogController --resource` | `dox make:controller Blog -r` (or `--resource`) |
| `php artisan make:controller BlogController --api` | `dox make:controller Blog --api` |
| `php artisan make:controller BlogController --model=Blog` | `dox make:controller Blog --model=Blog` |
| `public function show(Request $request, int $id)` | `Future<Blog?> show(DoxRequest req, int id)` |
| `public function store(StoreBlogRequest $request)` | `Future<Blog> store(CreateBlog body)` |
| constructor injection by the service container | constructor injection by the container: `@Inject()` above the class |
| method injection | filled by type: `DoxRequest`, one `@Dto` class, path params, models, container classes |
| implicit route model binding | the same: a `User user` parameter loads `{user}` by its key |

Dox fills a parameter by its type, not by its name. Path params go by position.
The container is generated code, not reflection. See [Dependency injection](../the-basic/dependency-injection.md).
A controller can be a class method, a static method or a plain function.

## Middleware

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `php artisan make:middleware Logger` | `dox make:middleware Logger` |
| `public function handle(Request $request, Closure $next)` | `dynamic handle(IDoxRequest req)` |
| `return $next($request);` | `return req;` |
| `return response('no', 401);` | `return response('no').statusCode(401);` |
| `abort(404);` | `abort(404);` |
| `$middleware->append(LogMiddleware::class)` in `bootstrap/app.php` | `AppConfig(globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[LogMiddleware()])` |

```dart title="lib/app/http/middleware/logger.middleware.dart"
class LoggerMiddleware implements IDoxMiddleware {
  @override
  dynamic handle(IDoxRequest req) {
    print('${req.method} ${req.uri.path}');
    return req; // go on. anything else is the response.
  }
}
```

A plain function `dynamic apiKey(DoxRequest req)` also works as middleware.
Dox middleware runs before the controller only. There is no "after" step; use a `responseHandler` for that.

## Requests and validation

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `php artisan make:request StoreBlogRequest` | `dox make:dto CreateBlog` |
| `class StoreBlogRequest extends FormRequest` with `rules()` | `@Dto() class CreateBlog` with annotations on `final` fields |
| `'title' => ['required', 'string', 'max:50']` | `@MaxLength(50) final String title;` |
| `'age' => ['nullable', 'integer', 'min:18']` | `@Min(18) final int? age;` |
| `'email' => ['required', 'email', 'unique:users']` | `@Email() @Unique('users') final String email;` |
| `'password' => ['required', 'confirmed', Password::min(8)->mixedCase()]` | `@Confirmed() @Password(mixedCase: true) final String password;` |
| `'company' => 'required_if:type,company'` | `@RequiredIf('type', 'company') final String? company;` |
| `'pin' => 'digits:4'`, `'meta' => 'json'`, `'day' => 'date_format:Y-m-d'` | `@Digits(4)`, `@Json()`, `@DateFormatted('Y-m-d')` on `String` fields |
| `'role' => Rule::in(['admin', 'user'])` | `final Role role;` (a Dart enum) |
| `'tags' => ['array', 'max:5']`, `'tags.*' => 'string'` | `@MaxItems(5) final List<String> tags;` |
| `$request->validated()` | the DTO object itself, already typed |
| `$request->validate([...])` inside a method | `await req.validate<CreateBlog>()` |
| `$request->input('name')` | `req.input('name')` |
| `$request->file('avatar')` | a `RequestFile` field in the DTO, or `req.input('avatar')` |
| `$request->user()` | `req.auth?.user<User>()` |
| `422` with `{"errors": {...}}` | `422` with a flat map `{"email": "...", "items.1.quantity": "..."}` |

```dart title="lib/app/dtos/create_blog/create_blog.dto.dart"
@Dto()
class CreateBlog {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 50)
  final String title;

  @Min(18)
  final int? age; // nullable = optional

  const CreateBlog({required this.title, this.age});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateBlog> schema = $CreateBlogDto;
}
```

The rules are checked by generated Dart code, not by rule strings at run time.
See [Validation](../the-basic/validation.md).

## Responses

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `return 'pong';` | `return 'pong';` |
| `return ['a' => 1];` | `return <String, int>{'a': 1};` |
| `return $blog;` (JSON) | `return blog;` (JSON from `toJson()`) |
| `return response($data, 201)->header('X-A', 'b');` | `return response(data).statusCode(201).header('X-A', 'b');` |
| `return response()->json($data);` | `return data;` (a `Map` or `List` is JSON) |
| `return response()->file($path);` | `return File(path);` |
| `return response()->download($path);` | `return Storage().download(path);` |
| `->cookie('theme', 'dark')` | `.cookie(DoxCookie('theme', 'dark'))` |
| `abort(404, 'Not found');` | `abort(404, 'Not found');` |
| `new BlogResource($blog)` | `BlogSerializer(blog)` |

## Views

With [dox_view](../the-basic/views.md), templates end in `.dox.html`. Most Blade tags have the same name. A block ends with `@end`.

A Blade name that is not a Dox tag, like `@foreach` or `@endif`, is printed as text. Dox writes a warning to `stderr` that names the template, the line and the Dox way. See [Coming from Blade](../the-basic/views.md#coming-from-blade).

| Laravel Blade | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `{{ $user->name }}`, `{!! $html !!}` | `{{ user.name }}`, `{{{ html }}}` |
| `@if ... @endif`, `@foreach ($users as $user)` | `@if ... @end`, `@each(user in users) ... @end` |
| `@isset`, `@empty`, `@auth`, `@guest`, `@env`, `@production`, `@once`, `@verbatim` | the same names, closed with `@end` |
| `@class`, `@checked`, `@selected`, `@disabled` | the same |
| `@include('nav')`, `@include('card', ['title' => 'Hi'])` | `@include('nav')`, `@include('card', { title: 'Hi' })` |
| `@includeWhen($user, 'account')` | `@includeWhen(user, 'account')` |
| `$loop->iteration`, `$loop->remaining`, `$loop->even`, `$loop->parent` | `$loop.iteration`, `$loop.remaining`, `$loop.even`, `$loop.parent` |
| `@json($data)`, `Js::from($data)` | `@json(data)`, `{{ json(data) }}` |
| `@error('email') {{ $message }} @enderror` | `@error('email') {{ message }} @end` |
| `<x-button>`, `$attributes->merge([...])`, `$slot` | `@button(...) ... @end`, `$attributes.merge({...})`, `$slot` |
| `@extends('layouts.app')`, `@section ... @endsection`, `@yield('content')` | `@extends('layouts/app')`, `@section ... @end`, `@yield('content')` |
| `@stack('scripts')`, `@push ... @endpush`, `@prepend ... @endprepend` | `@stack('scripts')`, `@push ... @end`, `@prepend ... @end` |
| `@csrf`, `@method('PUT')`, `old('email')` | `@csrf`, `@method('PUT')`, `old('email')` |
| `Blade::directive('datetime', ...)` | `View.directive('datetime', DateTimeDirective())` |

Three things are not the same as in Blade:

- `@includeIf(condition, 'name')` in Dox takes a condition first. It does not check if the template exists.
- `{{ true }}` prints `true`, a variable that does not exist prints nothing, and the text `'0'` is true. Turn on the `bladeOutput`, `strictVariables` and `stringZeroIsFalse` options to work like Blade. See [Strict options](../the-basic/views.md#strict-options).
- `@json` is safe in a `<script>` block and in an attribute in single quotes, not in an attribute in double quotes.

## Eloquent vs Dox Model

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `php artisan make:model Blog -m` | `dox make:model Blog -m` |
| `php artisan make:model Blog -mcr` | `dox make:model Blog -mcr` |
| `php artisan make:model Blog -a` | `dox make:model Blog -a` (migration, factory, seeder, resource controller) |
| `class Blog extends Model` | `@DoxModel() class Blog extends BlogGenerator` |
| `protected $table = 'blogs';` | `@DoxModel(table: 'blogs')` |
| `protected $primaryKey = 'uid';` | `@DoxModel(primaryKey: 'uid')` |
| `use SoftDeletes;` | `@DoxModel(softDelete: true)` |
| `public $timestamps = false;` | `@DoxModel(timestamps: false)` |
| `protected $hidden = ['password'];` | `List<String> get hidden => <String>['password'];` |
| `protected $fillable = [...]` | `List<String> get fillable => <String>[...];` |
| `$user->forceFill([...])` | `user.forceFill(<String, dynamic>{...})` |
| `User::forceCreate([...])` | `await User().forceCreate(<String, dynamic>{...})` |
| `Model::unguarded(fn () => ...)` | `await Model.unguarded(() async { ... })` |
| `protected $casts = ['meta' => 'array'];` | the field type: `Map<String, dynamic>? meta;` |
| mutator `setSlugAttribute()` | `@Column(beforeSave: makeSlug)` |
| accessor `getStatusAttribute()` | `@Column(beforeGet: readStatus)` |
| `$appends` with an accessor | `@Computed() String get fullName => ...;` |
| `Blog::find(1)` | `await Blog().find(1)` |
| `Blog::findOrFail(1)` | `await Blog().findOrFail(1)` (throws `ModelNotFoundException`) |
| `->firstOrFail()` | `.firstOrFail()` |
| `Blog::where('age', '>', 18)->get()` | `await Blog().where('age', '>', 18).get()` |
| `Blog::create([...])` | `await Blog().create(<String, dynamic>{...})` |
| `Blog::firstOrCreate([...], [...])` | `await Blog().firstOrCreate(<String, dynamic>{...}, <String, dynamic>{...})` |
| `Blog::firstOrNew([...])` | `await Blog().firstOrNew(<String, dynamic>{...})` |
| `Blog::updateOrCreate([...], [...])` | `await Blog().updateOrCreate(<String, dynamic>{...}, <String, dynamic>{...})` |
| `$blog->save()` | `await blog.save()` |
| `$blog->delete()` | `await blog.delete()` (returns the deleted rows as an `int`) |
| `$blog->increment('views')` | `await blog.increment('views')` |
| `$blog->update([...])` | `await blog.update(<String, dynamic>{...})` (only that row, sets `updated_at`, no model events) |
| `Blog::withTrashed()` | `Blog().withTrash()` |
| `Blog::onlyTrashed()` | `Blog().onlyTrashed()` |
| `$blog->touch()` | `await blog.touch()` |
| `$blog->replicate()` | `blog.replicate()` |
| `$blog->restore()` | `await blog.restore()` |
| `Blog::with('posts')->get()` | `await Blog().preload('posts').get()` |
| `$blog->load('posts')` | `await blog.$getRelation('posts')` |
| `$user->posts()->where(...)->get()` | `user.related<Post>('posts')?.where(...).get()` |
| `User::whereHas('posts', fn ($q) => ...)` | `User().whereHas('posts', (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) { ... })` |
| `orWhereHas`, `whereDoesntHave`, `orWhereDoesntHave` | the same names |
| `User::has('posts', '>=', 3)` | `User().has('posts', '>=', 3)` |
| `whereHas('posts.comments')` | `whereHas('posts.comments')` |
| `$with = ['posts']` | `@HasMany(Post, eager: true)` |
| `hasOne`, `hasMany`, `belongsTo`, `belongsToMany` | `@HasOne`, `@HasMany`, `@BelongsTo`, `@ManyToMany` |
| local scope `scopeActive()` | a static method with `@Scope()`, then `Blog().active()` |
| global scope | `@Scope(global: true)` |
| `creating`, `saved`, `deleting` events | `onCreating()`, `onSaved()`, `onDeleting()` hooks in the model |
| `Blog::observe(BlogObserver::class)` | `Model.observe<Blog>(BlogObserver())` |
| `$blog->saveQuietly()` | `await blog.saveQuietly()` |
| `Model::withoutEvents(fn)` | `Model.withoutEvents(() async { ... })` |

```dart title="lib/app/models/blog/blog.model.dart"
@DoxModel(table: 'blogs', softDelete: true)
class Blog extends BlogGenerator {
  @Column()
  String? title;

  @Column(name: 'user_id')
  int? userId;

  @BelongsTo(User)
  User? user;

  @override
  Future<void> onCreating() async {
    title = title?.trim();
  }
}
```

Every column field is nullable, because a new model has no values yet.
Dox has no `$casts` list. Use the field type, a [cast](../database/model/casts.md), `beforeSave` or `beforeGet`.
For scopes, see [Scopes](../database/model/scopes.md).
See [Model](../database/model/index.md).

## Query builder

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `DB::table('users')->get()` | `await QueryBuilder.table('users').get()` |
| `->where('a', 1)->orWhere('b', 2)` | `.where('a', 1).orWhere('b', 2)` |
| `->whereIn('id', [1, 2])` | `.whereIn('id', <int>[1, 2])` |
| `->whereIn('id', $subQuery)` | `.whereIn('id', subQuery)` |
| `->whereNull('deleted_at')` | `.whereNull('deleted_at')` |
| `->where(fn ($q) => $q->where(...)->orWhere(...))` | `.whereGroup((QueryBuilder<Blog> q) { q.where(...).orWhere(...); })` |
| `->orWhere(fn ($q) => ...)` | `.orWhereGroup((QueryBuilder<Blog> q) { ... })` |
| `->whereNot(fn ($q) => ...)` | `.whereNot((QueryBuilder<Blog> q) { ... })` |
| `->whereBetween('age', [18, 60])` | `.whereBetween('age', <int>[18, 60])` |
| `->whereColumn('a', '>', 'b')` | `.whereColumn('a', '>', 'b')` |
| `->whereLike('name', '%a%')` | `.whereLike('name', '%a%')` |
| `->whereExists(fn ($q) => $q->from('post')->...)` | `.whereExists('post', (QueryBuilder<Map<String, dynamic>> q) { ... })` |
| `->whereDate('created_at', '2024-05-01')`, `->whereYear(...)` | `.whereDate('created_at', '2024-05-01')`, `.whereYear(...)` |
| `->whereJsonContains('tags', 'a')` | `.whereJsonContains('tags', 'a')` |
| `->when($cond, fn ($q) => ...)` | `.when(cond, (QueryBuilder<Blog> q) { ... })` |
| `->whereRaw('lower(name) = ?', [$n])` | `.whereRaw('lower(name) = @n', <String, dynamic>{'n': n})` |
| `->select('id', 'name')` | `.select(<String>['id', 'name'])` |
| `->orderBy('name', 'desc')->limit(10)->offset(20)` | `.orderBy('name', 'desc').limit(10).offset(20)` |
| `->latest()`, `->oldest()`, `->inRandomOrder()` | `.latest()`, `.oldest()`, `.inRandomOrder()` |
| `->distinct()` | `.distinct()` |
| `->having('a', '>', 1)`, `->havingRaw(...)` | `.having('a', '>', 1)`, `.havingRaw(...)` |
| `->join('posts', 'posts.user_id', '=', 'users.id')` | `.join('posts', 'posts.user_id', 'users.id')` |
| `->joinSub($q, 'alias', 'alias.id', '=', 'users.id')` | `.joinSub(q, 'alias', 'alias.id', 'users.id')` |
| `->fromSub($q, 'alias')` | `.fromSub(q, 'alias')` |
| `->union($q)`, `->unionAll($q)` | `.union(q)`, `.unionAll(q)` |
| `->groupBy('age')` | `.groupBy('age')` on `QueryBuilder.table()` (returns maps) |
| `->count()` | `await ....count()` |
| `->sum('a')`, `->avg('a')`, `->min('a')`, `->max('a')` | `.sum('a')`, `.avg('a')`, `.min('a')`, `.max('a')` |
| `->exists()`, `->doesntExist()` | `.hasRows()`, `.hasNoRows()` |
| `->pluck('name')` | `.pluck('name')` |
| `->pluck('name', 'id')` | `.pluckMap('name', 'id')` |
| `->value('email')` | `.valueOf('email')` |
| `->chunk(100, fn)`, `->chunkById(100, fn)` | `.chunk(100, (rows) { ... })`, `.chunkById(100, (rows) { ... })` |
| `->paginate(10)` | `.paginate(currentPage: 1, perPage: 10)` |
| `->simplePaginate(10)` | `.simplePaginate(currentPage: 1, perPage: 10)` |
| `->cursorPaginate(10)` | `.cursorPaginate(perPage: 10, cursor: cursor)` |
| `->insert([...])` | `.insertMultiple(<Map<String, dynamic>>[...])` |
| `->update([...])` | `.update(<String, dynamic>{...})` (returns the changed rows as an `int`; on a model it keeps `fillable`, use `.forceUpdate()` to skip it) |
| `->increment('views', 5)`, `->decrement(...)` | `.increment('views', 5)`, `.decrement(...)` |
| `->insertOrIgnore([...])` | `.insertOrIgnore(<Map<String, dynamic>>[...])` |
| `->upsert([...], ['email'], ['name'])` | `.upsert(<Map<String, dynamic>>[...], <String>['email'], <String>['name'])` |
| `->delete()` | `.delete()` (returns the deleted rows as an `int`) |
| `Blog::query()->delete()` (every row) | `await Blog().whereRaw('1 = 1').delete()`. With no `where`, `Blog().delete()` throws a `StateError`. |
| `->lockForUpdate()`, `->sharedLock()` | `.lockForUpdate()`, `.sharedLock()` |
| `DB::select('select ...', [$id])` | `QueryBuilder.query('select ... @id', substitutionValues: {'id': id})` |
| `DB::transaction(fn)` | `QueryBuilder.transaction(() async { ... })` |
| `->toSql()` | `.toSql()` |
| `DB::connection('mysql')` | `.withConnection('mysql')` |

Values are always bound parameters. Names you pass are quoted. Do not pass user input as a column name or an operator.

`exists` and `value` are other names in Dox, because a model already has an `exists` getter, and `value` is a common column name.

## Migrations and schema

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `php artisan make:migration create_users_table` | `dox make:migration create_users_table` |
| `database/migrations/` | `db/migration/` |
| `Schema::create('users', function (Blueprint $table) {...})` | `await schema.create('users', (Table table) {...})` |
| `$table->id();` | `table.id();` |
| `$table->string('email')->unique();` | `table.string('email').unique();` |
| `$table->foreignId('user_id')->constrained()->cascadeOnDelete();` | `table.foreignId('user_id').constrained().cascadeOnDelete();` |
| `$table->timestamps();` | `table.timestamps();` |
| `$table->softDeletes();` | `table.softDeletes();` |
| `$table->string('name', 100)->nullable()->change();` | `table.string('name', 100).nullable().change();` |
| `Schema::dropIfExists('users');` | `await schema.dropIfExists('users');` |
| `php artisan migrate` | `dox migrate` (or `dox migration:run`) |
| `php artisan migrate:rollback --step=2` | `dox migration:rollback --step=2` |
| `php artisan migrate:reset`, `migrate:refresh`, `migrate:status` | `dox migration:reset`, `migration:refresh`, `migration:status` |
| `php artisan migrate:fresh --seed` | `dox migrate:fresh --seed` |
| `php artisan db:seed --class=UserSeeder` | `dox db:seed --class=UserSeeder` |
| `php artisan make:factory`, `make:seeder` | `dox make:factory`, `dox make:seeder` |

```dart title="db/migration/2026_10_21_120000_create_users_table.dart"
class CreateUsersTable extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.create('users', (Table table) {
      table.id();
      table.string('email').unique();
      table.timestamps();
    });
  }

  @override
  Future<void> down(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.dropIfExists('users');
  }
}
```

Dart can not load files at run time in an AOT binary. So the CLI keeps a list of your migrations in `db/migration/migrations.dart`. You do not edit it.
The server can run the migrations at start. See [Migration](../database/migration.md).

## Artisan vs the dox CLI

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `laravel new blog` | `dox create blog` |
| `php artisan serve` | `dox serve` (or `dox s`), with hot restart and `build_runner watch` |
| `php artisan make:resource` | `dox make:serializer` |
| `php artisan key:generate` | `dox key:generate` |
| `php artisan route:list` | `dox route:list` (also `--json`) |
| `php artisan tinker` | not there |
| `php artisan optimize` | `dox build` (one native binary in `build/bundle`) |
| `php artisan queue:work` | `dox queue:work` |
| `php artisan schedule:work` | `dox schedule:work` |
| `php artisan schedule:clear-cache` | `dox schedule:clear-cache` |

The `make:*` and `migrate` commands are in the tables above. Two commands have no Laravel twin: `dox build_runner:build` makes the generated code, and `dox env:generate` makes the typed env class.
See [Dox CLI](../digging-deeper/dox-cli.md).

## Auth

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `config/auth.php` guards and providers | `Auth.initialize(AuthConfig(guards: ...))` in a provider |
| `Auth::attempt(['email' => $e, 'password' => $p])` | `await Auth().attempt(<String, dynamic>{'email': e, 'password': p})` gives a token (an access token or a JWT, by the guard), or `null` |
| `Auth::login($user)` | `Auth().login(user)` gives a JWT. With access tokens, use `Auth().createAccessToken(user)` |
| `Auth::user()` | `req.auth?.user<User>()` |
| `Auth::id()` | `req.auth?.id()` |
| `Auth::guest()` | `req.auth == null` |
| `Auth::check()` | `Auth().check()` (the same as `isLoggedIn()`) |
| `Auth::once($credentials)` | `await Auth().once(credentials)` gives `true` or `false`, with no token and no session |
| `Auth::attempt(...)` for a web page (session) | `await Auth().attemptSession(req, <String, dynamic>{...})` gives `true` or `false` |
| `Auth::logout()` | `Auth().logout(req)` for a session. For a token: `await Auth().revokeToken(req)` |
| `->middleware('auth:sanctum')` | `AuthMiddleware()` from `dox_auth` |
| `->middleware('auth:web,api')` | `AuthMiddleware(guards: <String>['web', 'api'])` |
| `->middleware('guest')` | `GuestMiddleware(redirectTo: '/dashboard')` |
| `Crypt::encryptString($v)`, `Crypt::decryptString($v)` | `Crypt.encryptString(v)`, `Crypt.decryptString(v)` |
| `Hash::make($p)`, `Hash::check($p, $hash)` | `Hash.make(p)`, `Hash.check(p, hash)` (or `Hash.verify`) |

For an API, use access tokens (`AccessTokenAuthDriver`), like Sanctum. JWT is also available. `dox auth:tokens-table` makes the `auth_access_tokens` table. `$user->createToken('cli', ['posts:read'])` is `Auth().createAccessToken(user, name: 'cli', abilities: <String>['posts:read'])`, and `$request->user()->tokenCan('posts:read')` is `(req.auth as Auth).tokenCan('posts:read')`. To renew a token, use `rotateAccessToken`.
For web pages, a guard with `SessionAuthDriver` keeps the login in the session cookie.
See [Authentication](../security/authentication.md).

## Cache

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `config/cache.php` | `lib/config/cache.dart`, `CacheConfig(defaultStore:, stores:)` |
| `Cache::put('k', $v, 600)` | `await Cache().put('k', v, duration: Duration(minutes: 10))`. The time is a named `duration:`, not the third value. |
| `Cache::many(['a', 'b'])`, `Cache::putMany([...], 600)` | `await Cache().many(<String>['a', 'b'])`, `await Cache().putMany(<String, Object?>{...}, duration: ...)` |
| `Cache::get('k', 'default')` | `await Cache().get('k', 'default')` |
| `Cache::remember('k', 600, fn)` | `await Cache().remember('k', Duration(minutes: 10), fn)` |
| `Cache::forget('k')` | `await Cache().forget('k')` |
| `Cache::store('redis')` | `Cache().store('redis')` |
| `Cache::tags(['a'])` | `Cache().tags(<String>['a'])` |
| `Cache::lock('k', 10)` | `Cache().lock('k', Duration(seconds: 10))` |
| drivers: file, redis, memcached, database, array | drivers: `file`, `redis`, `memory`, `null` |

A value must be a JSON type. The `memory` store is per isolate. See [Cache](../digging-deeper/cache.md).

## Storage

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `config/filesystems.php` disks | `lib/config/storage.dart`, `StorageConfig(defaultDisk:, disks:)`, passed to a `StorageProvider` (`dox_storage`) |
| `Storage::put('a.txt', $bytes)` | `await Storage().put('a.txt', bytes, exact: true)` |
| `Storage::putFile('avatars', $file)` | `await Storage().putFile('avatars', file)` |
| `Storage::putFileAs('avatars', $file, 'u1.png')` | `await Storage().putFileAs('avatars', file, 'u1.png')` |
| `$request->file('f')->store('avatars')` | `await file.store('avatars')` |
| `$request->file('f')->storeAs('avatars', 'u1.png')` | `await file.storeAs('avatars', 'u1.png')` |
| `Storage::get($path)` | `await Storage().get(path)` |
| `Storage::exists($path)` / `missing($path)` | `await Storage().exists(path)` / `missing(path)` |
| `Storage::delete($path)` | `await Storage().delete(path)` |
| `Storage::copy($from, $to)` / `move($from, $to)` | `await Storage().copy(from, to)` / `move(from, to)` |
| `Storage::files($dir)` / `allFiles($dir)` | `await Storage().files(dir)` / `allFiles(dir)` |
| `Storage::directories($dir)` / `deleteDirectory($dir)` | `await Storage().directories(dir)` / `deleteDirectory(dir)` |
| `Storage::setVisibility($path, 'private')` | `await Storage().setVisibility(path, Visibility.private)` |
| `Storage::url($path)` | `await Storage().url(path)` |
| `Storage::temporaryUrl($path, now()->addMinutes(10))` | `await Storage().signedUrl(path, expiresIn: Duration(minutes: 10))` |
| `Storage::disk('s3')` | `Storage().disk('s3')` |
| `Storage::download($path, $name)` | `return Storage().download(path, name: name);` |
| drivers: local, s3, ftp, sftp | drivers: `local`, `s3` (also R2, MinIO, Spaces), `memory` |

Three things are different from Laravel:

- `setVisibility()` and `getVisibility()` on a local disk change and read the file mode only when the disk has `'permissions': true`. Without it, `setVisibility()` does nothing on a local disk, and `getVisibility()` gives the disk `visibility` (`public` by default). Laravel always runs `chmod`. So a file you made private is not private on disk until you turn this on.
- Paths that Dox gives you start with `/`. This is true for `putFile`, `store`, `files`, `allFiles` and `directories`.
- `put()` returns nothing. `download()` takes `name:` but no headers. For headers, use `response(await Storage().download(path)).header('Cache-Control', 'no-store')`.

See [File Storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md).

## Config and `.env`

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `config/*.php` files | `lib/config/*.dart` files, put together in `AppConfig` |
| `env('APP_KEY')` | `env.appKey` (a getter in `lib/config/env.dart`) |
| `env('APP_PORT', 3000)` | `env.appPort` (the default is in the getter: `int get appPort => 3000;`) |
| `config('app.name')` | `env.appName` from the typed env class (`@DoxEnv()`) |
| `php artisan config:cache` | not needed. The typed env is read once, at start. |

The typed env class gives you an `int` for `APP_PORT` and a build error for a bad type.
A missing key stops the app at start, with a list of every missing key. See [Environment Variables](../digging-deeper/env.md).

## Testing

| Laravel | Dox |
| --- | --- |
| `php artisan test` | `dart test` |
| `$this->get('/api/ping')->assertStatus(200)` | `(await client.get('/api/ping')).expectStatus(200)` with `DoxTestClient` |
| `RefreshDatabase` | run the migrations in `setUpAll`, then `setUp(refreshDatabase)` from `package:dox_orm/testing.dart` |
| `Storage::fake('s3')` | `Storage.manager.fake('s3')` |
| `Mail::fake()` | `Mail.fake()`, then `mail.assertSent()` and `mail.assertQueued()` |
| `Queue::fake()` | `Queue.fake()`, then `queue.assertPushed<T>()` |
| `Cache::fake()` | `Dox().cache = CacheManager(CacheConfig(...))` with a `memory` store |
| `$this->actingAs($user)` | `client.withToken(token)` with a token from `Auth().createAccessToken(user)` (access tokens) or `Auth().login(user)` (JWT) |

Dox has no fake HTTP kernel. `DoxTestClient.start(appConfig)` starts the real server inside the test, on a free port, and sends real requests.
See [Testing](../digging-deeper/testing.md).

## What is different

- **A generated container.** Like Laravel, Dox makes your controllers and injects what the constructor asks for.
  You add `@Inject()` to the class. `build_runner` writes `lib/generated/container.g.dart` with every registration. You do not register classes by hand in a provider.
  A singleton is one instance per isolate, not one per request.
- **Isolates, not PHP-FPM workers.** One process runs one isolate per CPU core. Each isolate runs your whole app and has its own memory.
  A static value or a singleton lives once per isolate. A PHP worker starts from zero on each request. A Dox isolate keeps its state between requests, so a memory leak stays.
  Anything that must be shared goes to the database, Redis or files. See [How Dox works](how-dox-works.md#isolates).
- **Code generation, not reflection.** Laravel reads your classes at run time. Dart has no usable reflection in a compiled app.
  So `build_runner` with `dox_builder` writes the model code, the DTO checks, the env class and the OpenAPI docs into `.g.dart` files.
  Run `dox build_runner:build` after a change, or let `dox serve` watch for you.
- **One native binary.** `dox build` makes an AOT binary in `build/bundle`. There is no interpreter, no `vendor/` folder and no `composer install` on the server.
  The Docker image is about 11 MB.
- **A native HTTP server and native database drivers.** Rust parses HTTP and talks to Postgres and MySQL. Your code stays in Dart. They come ready-built, so you do not need Rust.
- **Types everywhere.** A DTO is a class with typed fields. A path param is an `int`. A model field is a `String?`. The compiler finds many mistakes before you run the app.
- **Async is explicit.** Database calls return a `Future`. You write `await`. One isolate serves many requests at the same time while it waits for the database.
- **JSON API first.** Dox returns text, JSON, files and streams. For HTML pages, add [views](../the-basic/views.md) (`dox_view`) or [Inertia](../the-basic/inertia.md) (`dox_inertia`).

## What is missing today

Dox does not have these Laravel features yet:

- events and listeners (model events are there)
- password reset

See [What Dox does not have yet](status-and-roadmap.md#what-dox-does-not-have-yet) for what to use today.

What is there, as separate packages: [validation](../packages/validation.md), [OpenAPI docs](../packages/openapi.md),
[storage](../packages/storage.md), [cache](../packages/cache.md), [Socket.IO](../packages/socketio.md),
[auth](../security/authentication.md), [queues](../digging-deeper/queue.md), the [scheduler](../digging-deeper/scheduler.md),
[mail](../digging-deeper/mail.md), [views](../the-basic/views.md) and [Inertia](../the-basic/inertia.md).
[Sessions](../the-basic/session.md) are in `dox_core`.

# Dox and the other Dart backends

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/concepts/dart-frameworks/

# Dox and the other Dart backends

This page compares Dox with four other ways to build a backend in Dart: Dart Frog, Serverpod, Shelf (with `shelf_router`) and Alfred.

It lists facts only.
Each project is good at different things.

!!! note "Facts can change"
    The facts about the other projects come from their own docs, READMEs and pub.dev pages, read on 2026-10-22.
    Projects change. Check their docs before you decide.
    Where this page is not sure, the table says "see their docs".

## What each one is for

- **Dox** is a full backend framework, in the style of Laravel. It has routes, controllers, typed DTOs, an ORM, migrations, auth, cache, storage and a CLI.
- **Dart Frog** is a small backend framework. It is built on Shelf. Routes come from the files in the `routes/` folder.
  It describes itself as "a fast, minimalistic backend framework for Dart".
- **Serverpod** is a full-stack framework for Flutter. You write endpoint methods on the server. Serverpod generates a typed Dart client for the Flutter app.
  It has an ORM, auth, streaming and a hosted service (Serverpod Cloud).
- **Shelf** is the request and middleware model from the Dart team. It is a library, not a framework.
  `shelf_router` adds a router. You pick every other part yourself.
- **Alfred** is a small server in the style of Express.js. Routes, middleware, WebSocket and static files are built in.

## Feature table

"Not built in" means the project does not ship it. You can still add a package for it.

| Feature | Dox | Dart Frog | Serverpod | Shelf + shelf_router | Alfred |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Routing | Route classes: `Route.get(...)`, groups, resources, domain routes | Routes from files in `routes/`, dynamic and nested routes | Endpoint classes become typed client methods. A separate web server (Relic) has its own routing. | `Router()` with `<param>` patterns, nested routers | Express-like, `:id:int` params with types or regex |
| Typed request validation | `@Dto` classes, checks generated at build time, `422` with errors | Not in their feature list (see their docs) | Typed, generated parameters for endpoints. Rules: see their docs. | Not built in | Route params only (type or regex) |
| ORM and relations | `dox_orm`: models, has one, has many, belongs to, many to many | Not built in | Built in: filters, joins, one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many | Not built in | Not built in |
| Migrations | `dox migrate` (SQL or Dart files) | Not built in | Built in, versioned migrations | Not built in | Not built in |
| Auth | `dox_auth`: JWT and session guards. Password hashing (`Hash`) is in `dox_core`. | `dart_frog_auth`: Basic, Bearer and Cookie middleware | Built in: email and password, Google, Apple, GitHub, passkeys and more | Not built in | See their docs |
| WebSocket | A Socket.IO v4 server (`dox_socketio`) and raw `Route.websocket` | `dart_frog_web_socket` (`webSocketHandler`) | Streaming methods over a managed WebSocket | `shelf_web_socket` | Built in |
| OpenAPI | Generated OpenAPI 3.1 (JSON, YAML) and a docs page | On their roadmap, not done | See their docs | See their docs | See their docs |
| CLI and code generation | `dox` CLI, `build_runner` for DTOs, models and OpenAPI | `dart_frog` CLI: `create`, `dev` (hot reload), `build` | `serverpod` CLI, generates server and client code | No CLI (`shelf_router_generator` for routes from annotations) | No CLI |
| Native binary | `dox build` makes an AOT binary | `dart_frog build` makes a production build with a Dockerfile | Deploy to Serverpod Cloud, Docker or Terraform. Binary: see their docs. | Your app is plain Dart. Compile it like any Dart program. | Your app is plain Dart. Compile it like any Dart program. |
| Multi-core | One isolate per CPU core by default | See their docs | One isolate per process. Scale with more processes and server roles. | `serve(..., shared: true)` and your own isolates | Yes, a multi-isolate mode is in their README |
| HTTP server | Native server in Rust, also for WebSocket | Shelf on `dart:io` | Relic (their own) for the web server. API server: see their docs. | `dart:io` `HttpServer` (`shelf_io`) | `dart:io` |
| Databases | Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite | Not built in | Postgres, SQLite (also SQLite on the device). Redis for cache. | Not built in | Not built in |
| Code sharing with Flutter | `@Dto` classes in a pure Dart package, see [Share code with Flutter](../guides/share-code-with-flutter.md) | Plain Dart packages. A generated client is marked "in progress" in their feature list. | Generated client package, and shared packages for models | Plain Dart packages | Plain Dart packages |
| License | MIT | MIT | BSD-3 for most packages. The main `serverpod` package is SSPL. | BSD-3-Clause | MIT for the core. Some parts BSD. |
| First release and maturity | New (2026) | First on pub.dev in 2022, 1.0 about three years ago | First on pub.dev in 2021, now 4.x | First on pub.dev in 2014, 1.0 in 2021 | First on pub.dev in 2021, 1.x |
| Maintenance (on 2026-10-22) | Active | Active. Moved to the `dart-frog-dev` group in 2025. Last `dart_frog` release: 1.2.6 (November 2025). | Active. Release 4.0.4 in October 2026. | Active. Published by `tools.dart.dev` (the Dart team). | Last release 1.1.3, about 17 months ago. Unverified uploader. |

Sources (checked on 2026-10-22):

- Dart Frog: [dart-frog.dev](https://dart-frog.dev), [github.com/dart-frog-dev/dart_frog](https://github.com/dart-frog-dev/dart_frog) (docs in `docs/src/content/docs`, the roadmap and "The Future of Dart Frog"), [pub.dev/packages/dart_frog](https://pub.dev/packages/dart_frog)
- Serverpod: [docs.serverpod.dev](https://docs.serverpod.dev), [github.com/serverpod/serverpod](https://github.com/serverpod/serverpod), [github.com/serverpod/serverpod_docs](https://github.com/serverpod/serverpod_docs) (scalability, streaming, shared packages, database connection), [pub.dev/packages/serverpod](https://pub.dev/packages/serverpod)
- Shelf: [pub.dev/packages/shelf](https://pub.dev/packages/shelf), [pub.dev/packages/shelf_router](https://pub.dev/packages/shelf_router), [github.com/dart-lang/shelf](https://github.com/dart-lang/shelf), [`serve` API docs](https://pub.dev/documentation/shelf/latest/shelf_io/serve.html)
- Alfred: [pub.dev/packages/alfred](https://pub.dev/packages/alfred), [github.com/rknell/alfred](https://github.com/rknell/alfred)

## Speed

This page does not compare speed. Dox's own numbers (hello world and a `/db` read) are on [Performance](../digging-deeper/performance.md).
To compare, run the same test on your own machine, with each server on the same number of cores.

## When to pick Dox

- You want a full framework in one place: routes, typed input, ORM, migrations, auth, cache, storage and OpenAPI docs.
- You know Laravel. See [Coming from Laravel](coming-from-laravel.md).
- You need MySQL or MariaDB, not only Postgres.
- You want typed DTOs with the same rules on the server and in a Dart or Flutter client. See [Share code with Flutter](../guides/share-code-with-flutter.md).
- You want an OpenAPI document made from your code, for clients that are not written in Dart.

## When to pick something else

- **You want a framework with many years of use.** Dart Frog, Serverpod and Shelf have been out for years. Dox is new.
- **You want a hosted service.** Serverpod has Serverpod Cloud. Dox has no hosted service. You deploy it yourself (a binary or Docker).
- **Your app is Flutter only, and you want the client made for you.** Serverpod generates a typed client for every endpoint. Dox does not generate a Dart client. It generates an OpenAPI document.
- **You want a small tool with few parts.** Dart Frog is simpler. You add only what you need.
- **You want to build your own stack.** Shelf gives you the base parts, and the Dart team publishes it.
- **You need features Dox does not have yet**, like events and listeners. See [What Dox does not have yet](status-and-roadmap.md#what-dox-does-not-have-yet).

# Status and roadmap

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/concepts/status-and-roadmap/

# Status and roadmap

This page shows what works in Dox today, what is missing and what is planned.

## Packages

What the states mean:

- **Stable**: works, has tests and has had real use.
- **New**: works and has tests, but it is newer and has had less real use.

All packages follow semantic versioning: a breaking change only comes in a new major version.

Each package has its own version number. Some packages live in their own repos. See [Contribute](../community/contribute.md#packages-in-other-repos).

| Package | What it does | State | Tests |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dox_core` | Routes, middleware, controllers, request and response, isolates, config, the IoC container, exception handler, sessions, CSRF, rate limit, security headers, health check, test client | Stable | 528 tests in 61 files. CI runs them on the native server. |
| `dox_orm` | Query builder, models, relations, `whereHas`, scopes, casts, `withCount`, transactions, row locks, many to many writes, polymorphic relations, factories, seeders | Stable | 549 tests in 51 files. CI runs them on Postgres, MariaDB, MySQL 8.4 and SQLite. |
| `dox_validation` | `@Dto` rules, fluent schemas, JSON Schema, Standard Schema | Stable | 149 tests in 8 files |
| `dox_builder` | Code generator for models, DTOs, env classes, the container and OpenAPI | Stable | 86 tests in 5 files |
| `dox_annotation` | Annotations used by the generator | Stable | 6 tests in 1 file. Mostly tested through `dox_builder`. |
| `dox` (CLI) | `dox create`, `dox serve`, `dox build`, `make:*`, `migration:*`, `db:seed`, `queue:*`, `schedule:*`, package commands | Stable | 132 tests in 12 files |
| `dox_migration` | Migrations for Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite | Stable | 36 tests in 5 files. CI runs them on each database. |
| `dox_auth` | JWT and session auth guards and middleware, access tokens you can revoke, gates and policies | Stable | 201 tests in 8 files |
| `dox_cache` | Memory, file and Redis cache, tags, locks, encryption | Stable | 126 tests in 7 files, with Redis in CI |
| `dox_cache_database` | The database cache store, for `dox_cache` | New | 78 tests in 4 files, with SQLite, Postgres, MariaDB and MySQL in CI |
| `dox_storage` | Local disk and S3 (and S3-compatible) storage | Stable | 153 tests in 10 files, with MinIO in CI |
| `dox_openapi` | OpenAPI 3.1 document and a docs page | Stable | 63 tests in 4 files |
| `dox_socketio` | Socket.IO v4 server with a Redis adapter | Stable | 119 tests in 11 files, with Redis and the real `socket.io-client` in CI |
| `dox_queue` | Queues and jobs, the Redis and sync drivers, chains, batches, workers | New | 46 tests in 7 files. Most queue tests run in `dox_queue_database`, on every store. |
| `dox_queue_database` | The database queue driver, the batch store and `afterCommit` for `dox_queue` | New | 234 tests in 16 files, with SQLite, Postgres, MariaDB and Redis in CI |
| `dox_scheduler` | Run tasks on a schedule | New | 106 tests in 6 files, with Redis in CI |
| [`dox_mcp`](../packages/mcp.md) | MCP server: tools for AI clients over Streamable HTTP, signed sessions | New | 15 tests in 1 file |
| `dox_view` | [Views](../the-basic/views.md): `.dox.html` templates with layouts and components | New | 40 tests in 2 files |
| [`dox_inertia`](../the-basic/inertia.md) | Inertia.js server side: single page apps with React, Vue or Svelte and Dox controllers | New | 34 tests in 2 files |
| `dox_mailer` | Email with SMTP, Amazon SES, Azure, Resend, Mailgun, Postmark and sendmail, mailables, Markdown mail, notifications | New | 168 tests in 16 files, with a fake SMTP server |
| `dox_http_native` | Native HTTP/1.1 and WebSocket server in Rust, on the isolate's own thread. Dox has no other server. | New | 65 Dart tests in 4 files, and 32 Rust tests |
| `dox_postgres_native` | Native Postgres client (Rust tokio-postgres), the Postgres driver. Has TLS (`sslmode`, `sslRootCert`). | New | 41 tests in 7 files, plus the `dox_orm` tests |
| `dox_mysql_native` | Native MySQL and MariaDB client (Rust mysql_async), the MySQL driver. Has TLS. | New | 30 tests in 2 files, plus the `dox_orm` tests |

`Hash` (bcrypt password hashing) is in `dox_core`.

!!! note "About test coverage"
    The repos do not measure line coverage. Counts are `test(` calls in each package's `test/` folder.
    A test inside a loop counts once, so `dart test` can report more tests.
    The CI setup of the main repo is in `.github/workflows/test.yaml`. The packages in their own repos have their own CI.

## What Dox does not have yet

| Feature | Status | What to do today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Events and listeners | Not there | Model events are there. See [Model events](../database/model/events.md). |
| Password reset | Not there | Make a signed, short-lived token, send it with [Mail](../digging-deeper/mail.md) and check it in a controller. |
| Localization | Partly | Validation messages can follow the request locale (`req.locale`). There is no general translation helper. Keep your own message maps. |

## Planned

### Later

- Localization

The package CHANGELOGs have an `Unreleased` section when changes wait for the next version.

## How to help

- Try Dox and open an issue when something breaks or is missing.
- Pick an item above and open an issue first, so the design can be discussed.
- See [Contribute](../community/contribute.md) to set up the repo and run the tests.

# Contribute

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/community/contribute/

# Contribute

This page shows how to work on Dox: set up the repo, run the tests, release packages and update the docs.

To send a change, fork the repo and open a pull request.

## Setting up local development

### 1. Clone the repo

```bash
git clone git@github.com:dartondox/dox.git
```

### 2. Install melos

The repo is a [Dart pub workspace](https://dart.dev/tools/pub/workspaces).
The melos config is in the root `pubspec.yaml` (under `melos:`). Use Dart 3.13 or newer.

```bash
dart pub global activate melos
```

### 3. Run melos bootstrap

It runs one `dart pub get` at the root. All local packages are linked.
There is one `pubspec.lock` for the whole repo.

```bash
melos bs
```

### 4. Useful commands

```bash
# Run all tests.
# Use `melos run test`. `melos test` is a built-in melos command.
melos run test

# Analyze and check format (same as CI)
melos run analyze
melos run format_check
```

### If the project does not run

1. Remove `pubspec.lock` and `.dart_tool` at the root.
2. Remove any old `pubspec_overrides.yaml` and `pubspec.lock` in `packages/*` (left from melos 3).
3. Run `melos bs` again.

## Release (maintainers)

The `Release` GitHub workflow (`.github/workflows/publish.yaml`) publishes one package to pub.dev.
Each package has its own version and its own tag, like `dox_builder-v3.1.4` (`<package>-v<version>`).
It uses pub.dev automated publishing, so it needs no token or secret.

### Steps

The full guide is [RELEASING.md](https://github.com/dartondox/dox/blob/main/RELEASING.md) in the repo. In short, for each package that changed:

1. Run `bin/bump.sh <package> <version>`. It sets the version of that package only.
   If the package needs a newer sibling, raise that constraint by hand.
   Close the `## Unreleased` section of its `CHANGELOG.md`.
2. Merge the release PR, then push the tag `<package>-v<version>`. This publishes that package to pub.dev.
   Release in dependency order: `dox_annotation`, `dox_cache`, `dox_builder`, `dox_core`.
3. Release the matching `dox-sample` template.

A builder-only fix needs a `dox_builder` release only. It does not need a `dox_core` release.

The native packages (`dox_http_native`, `dox_postgres_native`, `dox_mysql_native`) are not in this repo.
See [Native packages](#native-packages) below.
`dox_orm`, `dox_migration`, `dox_socketio`, `dox_storage`, `dox_queue`, `dox_queue_database`, `dox_scheduler`, `dox_inertia`, `dox_view` and `dox_mailer` are not in this repo either.
See [Packages in other repos](#packages-in-other-repos).

**New package only:** turn on pub.dev automated publishing for it first. See [One-time setup](#one-time-setup).
A new package must first exist on pub.dev, so publish its first version by hand with `dart pub publish`.

### What the workflow does

1. It reads the package name and the version from the tag.
   It stops with an error for an unknown package or a bad version.
2. It checks that the version in `packages/<folder>/pubspec.yaml` is the tag version.
   If not, it stops. Run `bin/bump.sh <package> <version>` and try again.
3. It runs the tests. They must pass.
   Then it checks that the sibling packages it needs are on pub.dev. If not, it stops: "release <dep> first".
4. It checks that one package with a dry run, then publishes it.

A tag for a version that is already on pub.dev is skipped.
So if a run fails, fix the problem and click "Re-run jobs".

To see the packages in publish order on your machine:

```bash
python3 bin/publish_order.py
```

### Dry run

Open Actions > Release > "Run workflow".
Pick one package, or `all`. It runs `dart pub publish --dry-run` and publishes nothing.
Warnings (for example a missing CHANGELOG entry) show as yellow warnings. They do not fail the run.

### One-time setup

Do this once for each published package, and for every new package before its first tag.
The list of packages is the output of `python3 bin/publish_order.py`.

On pub.dev:

1. Open `https://pub.dev/packages/<name>/admin`.
2. Under "Automated publishing", click "Enable publishing from GitHub Actions".
3. Repository: `dartondox/dox`.
4. Tag pattern: `<package>-v{{version}}`, like `dox_core-v{{version}}`. Each package has its own pattern.
5. Tick "Require GitHub Actions environment" and set the environment to `pub.dev`.
6. Save.

On GitHub, in `dartondox/dox` > Settings > Environments, there must be an environment named `pub.dev`.
The publish job runs in it.
Optional: add yourself as a required reviewer, and allow only the tags `dox_annotation-v*`, `dox_builder-v*`, `dox_cache-v*` and `dox_core-v*`.

## Packages in other repos

| Package | Repo |
| --- | --- |
| `dox` (the CLI) | [dartondox/dox-cli](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-cli) |
| `dox_orm`, `dox_migration`, `dox_cache_database` | [dartondox/dox-orm](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-orm) |
| `dox_auth` | [dartondox/dox-auth](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-auth) |
| `dox_openapi` | [dartondox/dox-openapi](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-openapi) |
| `dox_validation` | [dartondox/dox-validation](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-validation) |
| `dox_socketio` | [dartondox/dox-socketio](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-socketio) |
| `dox_storage` | [dartondox/dox-storage](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-storage) |
| `dox_queue`, `dox_queue_database` | [dartondox/dox-queue](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-queue) |
| `dox_scheduler` | [dartondox/dox-scheduler](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-scheduler) |
| `dox_inertia` | [dartondox/dox-inertia](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-inertia) |
| `dox_view` | [dartondox/dox-view](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-view) |
| `dox_mailer` | [dartondox/dox-mailer](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-mailer) |

The packages here use them from pub.dev. The database tests (Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite) run in `dox-orm`.
`dox_core` uses `dox_openapi` and `dox_validation`.
CI in this repo uses their newest code: `ci/clone-siblings.sh`, then `ci/use-siblings.sh`.

To work on one of them and Dox together:

1. Clone the repos next to the Dox repo, like `../dox-orm`.
   `ci/clone-siblings.sh` clones `dox-orm`, `dox-auth`, `dox-openapi`, `dox-validation`, `dox-socketio`, `dox-storage`, `dox-queue`, `dox-scheduler` and `dox-cli`.
   Clone `dox-mailer`, `dox-view` and `dox-inertia` by hand when you need them.
2. Add them to the root `pubspec_overrides.yaml` of the Dox repo. Git ignores this file.
   For `dox_openapi` and `dox_validation`, `ci/use-siblings.sh` writes this file for you.

    ```yaml
    dependency_overrides:
      dox_openapi:
        path: ../dox-openapi
      dox_validation:
        path: ../dox-validation
    ```

3. Run `dart pub get`.

The apps in `examples/` already use these clones (their `pubspec_overrides.yaml`), so clone them before you run an example.
In the other repo, a `pubspec_overrides.yaml` that points to `../dox/packages/...` uses your local Dox packages.

Each repo has its own version. Push a `v<version>` tag in that repo to release it.

## Native packages

The three native packages live in their own repos:

| Package | Repo |
| --- | --- |
| `dox_http_native` | [dartondox/dox-http-native](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-http-native) |
| `dox_postgres_native` | [dartondox/dox-postgres-native](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-postgres-native) |
| `dox_mysql_native` | [dartondox/dox-mysql-native](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-mysql-native) |

Dox uses them from pub.dev. Their build hooks download ready-built libraries, so you do not need Rust to work on Dox.

To work on a native package and Dox together:

1. Clone the package next to the Dox repo, like `../dox-http-native`.
2. Add it to the root `pubspec_overrides.yaml` of the Dox repo. Git ignores this file.

    ```yaml
    dependency_overrides:
      dox_http_native:
        path: ../dox-http-native
    ```

3. Run `dart pub get`.

Each native package is released from its own repo, with its own version.
Push a `v<version>` tag in that repo.
Its CI builds the libraries, uploads them, fills the hashes and publishes the package to pub.dev.
Then raise the version constraint in the Dox packages that use it.

## Docs

The docs site is https://dartondox.dev. It is built with MkDocs Material and
[mike](https://github.com/jimporter/mike). mike keeps one folder per version on the `gh-pages` branch.

| URL | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `/3.x/...` | 3.x docs, built from `main` |
| `/latest/...` | a copy of the newest version (now 3.x) |
| `/` | redirects to `/latest/` |
| old links like `/the-basic/routing/` | redirect to `/latest/the-basic/routing/` |

### Write and preview

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
.venv/bin/mkdocs serve           # live preview of this branch
.venv/bin/mkdocs build --strict  # the same build as CI. Broken links fail.
```

`hooks/docs_hooks.py` runs during the build. It makes the changelog page from `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md`, and writes `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`.

The `Docs check` workflow (`.github/workflows/docs-check.yaml`) runs on every pull request that changes the docs. It runs three checks:

- `mkdocs build --strict`
- a spell check: `codespell docs --skip "*.svg,*.png,*.ico,*.css,*.js" --ignore-words .codespell-ignore`
- `ci/check-no-tabs.sh`: the docs must not use content tabs

### Deploy

- 3.x deploys with each release. The `Docs` workflow (`.github/workflows/docs.yaml`) runs on a
  `dox_core-v<version>` tag, the same tag that publishes `dox_core`. So docs for a feature that is not released yet stay off the site.
  It runs `mike deploy --update-aliases 3.x latest`.
- To deploy the docs only (a typo fix, or the docs of a package from another repo that was just released),
  push a `docs-v<version>` tag on `main`, like `git tag docs-v3.0.1-1 && git push origin docs-v3.0.1-1`.
  It publishes no package and runs no tests.
- After each deploy, the workflow writes small redirect pages for the old root links,
  the root `index.html`, a `404.html` and the `CNAME` file. So `dartondox.dev` and old links keep working.
- The workflow pushes with the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN`. This works because `gh-pages` is not a protected branch.

### New major version

When 4.x starts, deploy 4.x with `mike deploy --update-aliases 4.x latest`. Keep a `v3.x`
branch, and add `3.x` to the workflow input, so 3.x can still be fixed.

# Showcase

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/community/showcase/

# Showcase

This page lists real open source apps built with Dox that you can read, run and copy from.

## Monthly Expense

[Monthly Expense](https://github.com/necessarylion/monthly-expense) is an expense tracker for you and the people you share money with. You log expenses, track wallets in many currencies and keep a shopping list. An AI assistant like Claude can add expenses and read summaries for you over MCP.

| Part | What it uses |
| --- | --- |
| API | Dox, with SQLite or Postgres |
| Web app | React, Vite, Tailwind and shadcn/ui |
| Sign-in | Firebase (Google), checked on every API request |
| AI | An MCP server with OAuth sign-in, 44 tools |
| Deploy | One Docker image with the web app and a native API binary |

What you can learn from it:

- **ORM and migrations.** Groups, members, categories, expenses, wallets and budgets as models. The app runs the migrations when it starts. See [Model](../database/model/index.md) and [Migration](../database/migration.md).
- **Token auth from another service.** The API checks a Firebase ID token in middleware. It makes the user on the first sign-in. See [Middleware](../the-basic/middleware.md).
- **MCP for AI clients.** Each HTTP route has a matching MCP tool with the same input. See [MCP](../packages/mcp.md).
- **Scheduled jobs.** See [Scheduler](../digging-deeper/scheduler.md).
- **One container in production.** The API serves the built web app and compiles to a native binary. CI runs the tests on SQLite and Postgres, then pushes the image. See [Docker](../guides/docker.md).

Run it on your machine:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/necessarylion/monthly-expense.git
cd monthly-expense
./dev.sh
```

The [README](https://github.com/necessarylion/monthly-expense#readme) lists the Firebase settings and env vars you need first.

## Add your app

Built something with Dox? Open a pull request that adds it to this page. Your app must be open source, so readers can see the code.

# Meet Doxie

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/community/mascot/

# Meet Doxie

![Doxie, the Dox mascot](../assets/mascot.png){ width="260" }

Doxie is the official mascot of Dox. Doxie is a blue dachshund.

## Why a dachshund

"Doxie" is a common nickname for a dachshund. It sounds like Dox, so the name came first.

A dachshund is small, fast and full of energy. Dox tries to be the same: a small native binary that serves a lot of requests.

## Logo and mascot

Dox has a logo and a mascot. They have different jobs.

| | Logo | Mascot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What | A hexagon with a "D" cut out | Doxie, the blue dachshund |
| Where | The docs header, the favicon, the README, pub.dev | The home page, social cards, talks, stickers |
| Files | [`logo.svg`](../assets/logo.svg) (white, for dark backgrounds) | [`mascot.png`](../assets/mascot.png) (transparent background) |

Use the logo when the space is small, like an icon or an avatar. Doxie has too much detail to read well at 16 or 32 pixels.

## Colors

| Name | Hex | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sky blue | `#5CC6FF` | Doxie's body, links in dark mode |
| Dart blue | `#0A5FC2` | Doxie's ears and collar, links in light mode |
| Navy | `#0B1B36` | The docs header, outlines |

## Use Doxie

You are welcome to use Doxie when you write or talk about Dox: blog posts, slides, videos and stickers.
Please do not change Doxie's colors, and do not use Doxie to brand another product.
