- Three [opt-in flags](../packages/validation.md#opt-in-flags) change how DTOs are checked: get all errors at once, reject `[]` in a required list, and reject `""` in a `Maybe` field.

### Missing or `null`? (for PATCH)

A `T?` field gives `null` for both. To know the difference, use `Maybe<T>`:

```dart
@Length(max: 500)
final Maybe<String?> bio; // default: const Maybe.missing()

// in the controller
if (body.bio.isPresent) {
  user.bio = body.bio.value; // can be null: the client cleared it
}
```

## Types

| Dart type | JSON | Query and form data |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `String`, `int`, `double`, `num`, `bool` | the same JSON type | text, converted |
| `DateTime` | an ISO 8601 string | the same |
| an `enum` | the name, like `"admin"` | the same |
| `RequestFile` | not allowed | a file part |
| a `@Dto` class | an object | bracket keys: `address[city]` |
| `List<T>` | an array | `tags=a&tags=b` or `tags[]=a` |
| `Map<String, T>` | an object | bracket keys: `meta[color]` |

JSON is strict: `"18"` is not an `int`. Query and form data are text, so Dox converts them.
To accept text in a JSON body too, use `@Dto(coerce: true)`. Then `"18"` is read as `18`, `"4.5"` as `4.5`, and `"true"`, `"1"`, `"yes"`, `"on"` (and the opposites) as a bool. A `bool` also takes the numbers `1` and `0`. A nested DTO uses its own `@Dto(coerce:)`.

```dart
@Dto(coerce: true)
class UpdateStock {
  final int count; // {"count": "18"} gives 18
  final bool active; // {"active": 1} gives true

  const UpdateStock({required this.count, required this.active});
}
```
Every detail is in [Types in detail](validation-rules.md#types-in-detail).

## Where the data comes from

| Request | Dox reads |
| --- | --- |
| `GET`, `HEAD`, `DELETE` | the query string |
| `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` | the body (JSON, form or multipart) |

Dox reads **one** source. It never mixes the query and the body.
To choose the source yourself:

```dart
@Dto(source: Source.query) // on the DTO
class SearchUsers { ... }

await req.validate<SearchUsers>(source: Source.query); // for one call
```

Path params are not part of a DTO. Ask for them as controller parameters, like `int id`.

## Keys

The input key is the field name in snake_case: `firstName` reads `first_name`.

```dart
final String firstName; // key: first_name

@Name('emailAddress')
final String email; // key: emailAddress
```

- `@Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field)` uses the field names as they are.
- Unknown keys are dropped. With `@Dto(strict: true)`, an unknown key is an error.

## Rules

Put rules on a field as annotations. They run from top to bottom. The first rule that fails gives the error.

```dart
@Trim()
@Lowercase()
@Email()
@MaxLength(255)
final String email;
```

| Kind | Annotations |
| --- | --- |
| Text | `@Length`, `@MinLength`, `@MaxLength`, `@Email`, `@Url`, `@Uuid`, `@Ulid`, `@Ip`, `@Regex`, `@In`, `@NotIn`, `@StartsWith`, `@EndsWith`, `@Alpha`, `@AlphaNumeric`, `@AlphaDash` |
| Change text | `@Trim`, `@Lowercase`, `@Uppercase`, `@AllowEmpty` |
| Numbers | `@Min`, `@Max`, `@Range`, `@Positive`, `@GreaterThan`, `@LessThan`, `@In`, `@NotIn` |
| Lists | `@MinItems`, `@MaxItems`, `@UniqueItems` |
| Dates | `@After`, `@Before`, `@AfterOrEqual`, `@BeforeOrEqual` |
| Other fields | `@Same`, `@Confirmed`, `@Different`, `@GreaterThanField`, `@GreaterThanOrEqualField`, `@LessThanField`, `@LessThanOrEqualField`, `@ProhibitedIf` |
| Present or missing | `@RequiredIf`, `@RequiredUnless`, `@RequiredWith`, `@RequiredWithout`, `@RequiredWithoutAll`, `@Filled`, `@Present`, `@Prohibited`, `@Accepted`, `@Declined` |
| Skip a field | `@ExcludeIf`, `@ExcludeUnless` |
| Files | `@MaxSize`, `@MinSize`, `@Mimes`, `@MimeTypes`, `@Image`, `@Dimensions` |
| Database | `@Unique`, `@Exists` |

Every rule, with its error code and message, is in [Validation rules](validation-rules.md).

- A rule on a list checks each item: `@Email()` on a `List<String>`. Only the list rules check the list itself.
- For a few allowed values, use a Dart `enum`, or `@In(<String>['draft', 'published'])`.

## Nested objects and lists

A field can be another `@Dto` class, or a list of them.

```dart
@Dto()
class CreateOrder {
  final Address address;

  @MinItems(1)
  final List<OrderItem> items;

  const CreateOrder({required this.address, required this.items});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateOrder> schema = $CreateOrderDto;
}
```

`Address` and `OrderItem` are `@Dto` classes too. An error in a nested value has a path key, like `items.1.quantity`.

## Files

A `RequestFile` field reads a file from `multipart/form-data`.

```dart
@Image()
@MaxSize('2MB')
@Dimensions(minWidth: 100, maxWidth: 2000)
final RequestFile avatar;

@Mimes(<String>['pdf', 'docx'])
final List<RequestFile> documents;
```

Dox checks the real file type from its first bytes. It does not trust the file name or the client.
To save the file, see [File upload](../guides/file-upload.md).

## Checks across fields: `validate()`

Add a `validate(DtoErrors errors)` method to the DTO. Dox calls it after all field rules passed.

```dart
void validate(DtoErrors errors) {
  if (password != passwordConfirmation) {
    errors.add('password_confirmation', 'The passwords do not match');
  }
}
```

- The key is the input key (snake_case). Use `_root` for an error about the whole body.
- `errors.has(key)` tells you if a key already has an error.
- The method can be `async`. Do not throw for bad input. Add an error.

## Database rules: `@Unique` and `@Exists`

These read the database, so they run last.
They come from `dox_orm`. Add `import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';` to the DTO file.

```dart
@Unique('users', column: 'email')
final String email;

@Exists('teams') // column defaults to id
final int teamId;
```

For an update, skip the row you are updating with `ignoreParam`:

```dart
// PUT /users/{id}
@Unique('users', column: 'email', ignoreParam: 'id')
final String email;
```

All options are in [Validation rules: database](validation-rules.md#database).
The full order of checks is in [The order of checks](validation-rules.md#the-order-of-checks).

## The error response

When a check fails, Dox answers `422` with one message per field:

```json
{
  "email": "The email is not a valid email",
  "tags.0": "The tags may not be greater than 20 characters",
  "items.1.quantity": "The quantity must be greater than 0"
}
```

The key is the path to the value, with the input keys. List items use the index.

The flag `laravelErrors` sends `{"message": "...", "errors": {"field": ["..."]}}` instead. See [Core flags](../reference/app-config.md#core-flags).

For another error shape, read `error.issues` of the `ValidationException` in your `ExceptionHandler`. Each issue has its `dottedPath`, its rule `code` (like `min_length`), its `message` and its `params`.

## Messages

Change a message in one of these places. The first one wins.

1. On the rule: `@Email(message: 'Please check your email')`.
2. On the DTO, by code or by `key.code`. A full dotted path works too, like `'address.city.required'` (it also reaches a nested DTO). A message in the nested DTO itself, like `'city.required'`, wins over it. Use `*` for list items, like `'tags.*.required'`:

```dart
@Dto(messages: <String, String>{
  'email.required': 'We need your email',
  'integer': 'The {field} must be a number',
})
```

3. For the whole app, with a `MessageResolver`. Use it for other languages:

```dart
class AppMessages extends MessageResolver {
  static const Map<String, Map<String, String>> _texts = <String, Map<String, String>>{
    'th': <String, String>{'required': 'กรุณากรอก {field}'},
  };

  @override
  String resolve(MessageRequest request) {
    String? template = _texts[request.locale]?[request.code]; // locale from Accept-Language
    if (template == null) {
      return super.resolve(request);
    }
    return format(template, request.params);
  }
}

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  validationMessages: AppMessages(),
  // ...
);
```

Placeholders: `{field}` (the last key), `{value}`, and rule values like `{min}` and `{max}`.

### Names for `{field}`

By default `{field}` is the key, like `The first_name is required`.
To show another name, give attribute names.
A key with no name still shows the key.

On the DTO:

```dart
@Dto(attributes: <String, String>{'first_name': 'first name'})
class CreateUser { ... }
// The first name is required
```

For the whole app (and for fluent schemas), in the `MessageResolver`:

```dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  validationMessages: MessageResolver(
    attributes: <String, String>{'first_name': 'first name'},
  ),
  // ...
);
```

- A name is looked up by the dotted path (`address.city`), then with `*` for list items (`items.*.qty`), then by the field name (`city`).
- The names of the DTO win over the names of the `MessageResolver`. A nested DTO uses its own names first, then the names of the outer DTO.
- `MessageResolver.setAttributes(...)` adds names to a resolver. A custom resolver can override `attributeName(path)`.
- `{other}` and `{others}` (the other keys of rules like `@RequiredIf` and `@Same`) show their names too.
- The error path and the key in the error response do not change. Only the text does.
- `@Dto(attributes:)` needs one `build_runner` run.

### Laravel rule names in message keys

Some Dox codes have another name in Laravel. With the opt-in flag `laravelMessageKeys`, a message key can use the Laravel name too. So `'name.min'` gives the message for the `min_length` error of `name`. Without the flag, only the Dox codes match.

```dart
Validator.flags = const ValidationFlags(laravelMessageKeys: true);
```

Set it in a provider's `setup()`, like the [other flags](../packages/validation.md#opt-in-flags).
The error code in the response does not change: it is still `min_length`.

At each step of the lookup, the Dox code is tried first, then the Laravel name. So `'name.min_length'` wins over `'name.min'`. A key with a path still wins over a key with only a code: `'name.min'` wins over `'min_length'`.

| Dox code | Laravel name |
| --- | --- |
| `min_length` | `min` |
| `max_length` | `max` |
| `length` | `size` |
| `length_between` | `between` |
| `start_with` | `starts_with` |
| `end_with` | `ends_with` |
| `alpha_numeric` | `alpha_num` |
| `greater_than` | `gt` |
| `less_than` | `lt` |
| `min_items` | `min` |
| `max_items` | `max` |
| `unique_items` | `distinct` |
| `min_size` | `min` |
| `max_size` | `max` |
| `mime_types` | `mimetypes` |
| `datetime` | `date` |

This works in `@Dto(messages:)` and in a `MessageResolver`. A code with the same name in both (like `email` or `required`) needs nothing.
With the flag on, a message key `min` or `max` with no path fits text, list and file errors too, not only numbers.

## Custom rules

Extend `Rule<T>`. `T` is the field type (or the item type, for a list).

```dart
class Slug extends Rule<String> {
  const Slug({super.message});

  @override
  String get name {
    return 'slug'; // the error code
  }

  @override
  String get defaultMessage {
    return 'The {field} must be a slug';
  }

  @override
  bool check(String value, RuleContext context) {
    return _pattern.hasMatch(value);
  }

  static final RegExp _pattern = RegExp(r'^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$');
}

// use it
@Slug()
final String slug;
```

- A rule with values: add `final` fields and override `params`. They become placeholders.
- `context.lookup('other.key')` reads another input value.
- `context.sibling('key')` reads the raw input of a field next to this one, in the same object. For example, `context.sibling('password_confirmation')` in a rule on `password`. It gives `undefined` when the field is missing.
- A rule that needs the database: extend `AsyncRule<T>` and write `checkAsync`.

## Dynamic input

When the shape is known only at runtime (like form fields from the database), use a fluent schema:

```dart
Map<String, dynamic> data = await req.validateSchema(v.object(fields));
```

See [Fluent schemas](../packages/validation.md#fluent-schemas-for-dynamic-input). Use a DTO for everything else.

## Testing

A DTO is a normal Dart class. Make one directly to skip the checks:

```dart
CreateUser input = const CreateUser(
  name: 'Ann',
  email: 'ann@dox.dev',
  password: 'secret123',
);
```

To test the checks, use `safeValidateMap`. It never throws:

```dart
ParseResult<CreateUser> result = await CreateUser.schema.safeValidateMap(<String, dynamic>{
  'name': 'A',
  'email': 'not-an-email',
  'password': 'secret123',
});

expect(result.success, isFalse);
expect(result.errors['email'], 'The email is not a valid email');
```

- `validateMap` does the same, but returns the object or throws.
- `source: Source.query` reads the map like a query string. `params: {'id': '5'}` gives path params.
- `@Unique` and `@Exists` need a test database.


---

# Validation rules

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/the-basic/validation-rules/

# Validation rules

This page lists every annotation you can put on a `@Dto` field.

See [Validation](validation.md) for how DTOs work.

How to read the tables:

- **Code** is the error code. Use it in `@Dto(messages: ...)` and in a `MessageResolver`.
- **Message** is the default English text. `{field}` is the last key of the path.
- Every annotation also takes `message:`. It wins over every other message.
- All limits include the limit itself, unless the table says "exclusive".
- On a `List<T>` field, a value rule checks each item. Only the list rules check the list itself.

## Type errors

These have no annotation. They come from the field type.

| Code | When | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `required` | a required field is missing, `null`, or `""` | `The {field} is required` |
| `string` | not a string | `The {field} must be a string` |
| `integer` | not a whole number | `The {field} must be an integer` |
| `numeric` | not a number (`double`, `num`) | `The {field} must be a number` |
| `boolean` | not a bool | `The {field} must be a boolean` |
| `date` | not an ISO 8601 date | `The {field} must be a date` |
| `in` | not a name of the enum | `The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values}` |
| `array` | not a list | `The {field} must be an array` |
| `object` | not an object (nested DTO, `Map`) | `The {field} must be an object` |
| `file` | not a file | `The {field} must be a file` |
| `unrecognized_keys` | unknown key, with `@Dto(strict: true)` | `The {field} field is not allowed` |

## Text

For `String` fields (and `List<String>` items).

| Annotation | Code | Message | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@Length(min: 3, max: 50)` | `length_between` | `The {field} must be between {min} and {max} characters` | `minLength`, `maxLength` |
| `@Length(min: 6, max: 6)` | `length` | `The {field} must be exactly {length} characters` | `minLength`, `maxLength` |
| `@MinLength(3)` | `min_length` | `The {field} must be at least {min} characters` | `minLength` |
| `@MaxLength(50)` | `max_length` | `The {field} may not be greater than {max} characters` | `maxLength` |
| `@Email()` | `email` | `The {field} is not a valid email` | `format: email` |
| `@Url()` | `url` | `The {field} must be a url` | `format: uri` |
| `@Uuid()` | `uuid` | `The {field} is invalid uuid` | `format: uuid` |
| `@Ulid()` | `ulid` | `The {field} must be a valid ULID` | `pattern` |
| `@Ip()` | `ip` | `The {field} must be an ip address` | `anyOf` `ipv4` / `ipv6` |
| `@Regex(r'[a-z]+')` | `regex` | `The {field} format is invalid` | `pattern` |
| `@In(['a', 'b'])` | `in` | `The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values}` | `enum` |
| `@NotIn(['root'])` | `not_in` | `The {field} field cannot be {value}` | `not: {enum}` |
| `@StartsWith('dox')` | `start_with` | `The {field} must start with {prefix}` | `pattern` |
| `@EndsWith('.dev')` | `end_with` | `The {field} must end with {suffix}` | `pattern` |
| `@Alpha()` | `alpha` | `The {field} must be an alphabetic` | `pattern` |
| `@AlphaNumeric()` | `alpha_numeric` | `The {field} must be only alphabetic and number` | `pattern` |
| `@AlphaDash()` | `alpha_dash` | `The {field} must be only alphabetic, number, dash and underscore` | `pattern` |

Details:

- `@Length` has `min:` and `max:`. Both are optional, but you must give one.
  With only `min:` it acts like `@MinLength`, with only `max:` like `@MaxLength`.
- Length counts characters (Unicode code points). `é` counts as 1.
- `@Url()` needs `http` or `https` and a host.
- `@Uuid()` takes any version. Upper or lower case.
- `@Ulid()` takes 26 Crockford base32 characters, upper or lower case. The first one is `0` to `7`.
- `@Regex(pattern, {message})` must match the **whole** value. You do not need `^` and `$`.
  The regex is checked when the generator runs. A bad regex stops the build.
- `@Alpha()`, `@AlphaNumeric()` and `@AlphaDash()` use ASCII letters `a-z`, `A-Z`. `@AlphaDash()` also allows digits `0-9`, `-` and `_`.
- `@In` and `@NotIn` compare exactly (case matters).

## More text rules

For `String` fields.

| Annotation | Code | Message | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@Json()` | `json` | `The {field} is not a valid json` | `contentMediaType: application/json` |
| `@Digits(6)` | `digits` | `The {field} must be {digits} digits` | `pattern` |
| `@DigitsBetween(4, 6)` | `digits_between` | `The {field} must be between {min} and {max} digits` | `pattern` |
| `@DateFormatted('Y-m-d')` | `date_format` | `The {field} must match the format {format}` | |
| `@HexColor()`, `@HexColor(short: true)` | `hex_color` | `The {field} must be a hex color like #1a2b3c` | `pattern` |
| `@Password(min: 8, ...)` | `password` | `The {field} must have {rules}` | `minLength` |

- `@HexColor()` takes `#` and 6 hex digits, in any case. `@HexColor(short: true)` also takes 3 digits, like `#abc`.
- `@Digits` and `@DigitsBetween` take only `0-9`. No sign, no dot. Use a `String` field, so leading zeros stay.
- `@DateFormatted` uses the PHP `date()` letters:
  day `d`, `j`, `D` (`Mon`), `l` (`Monday`), `N`, `w`, `S` (`st`), `z`;
  month `m`, `n`, `M` (`Jan`), `F` (`January`), `t`;
  year `Y`, `y`, `L`;
  time `a`, `A`, `g`, `h`, `G`, `H`, `i`, `s`, `v`, `u`;
  time zone `e`, `T`, `P`, `p`, `O`, `Z`, `I`;
  full `U`, `c`, `r`.
  Put `\` before a letter to use it as text, like `Y-m-d\TH:i`. Any other letter stops the build (and throws an `ArgumentError` in `v.string().dateFormat()`). Other characters must be there as they are.
  `j`, `n`, `g`, `G`, `z` and `U` take no leading zero: `j/n/Y` rejects `01/02/2024`.
  `e` and `T` take any name that looks like a time zone. They do not check that it is a real one.
  The date must exist: `2023-02-29` fails. Names need the case shown (`Jan`, not `jan`). A day name must fit the date. The field stays a `String`. Use a `DateTime` field for ISO 8601 dates.
- `@Password` options: `min` (default 8), `letters`, `mixedCase` (one upper and one lower case letter), `numbers`, `symbols`. They are all off by default.
  Letters, numbers and symbols are Unicode, so `é` is a letter. `{rules}` lists the options you set, like `at least 8 characters, one number, and one symbol`, or `at least 8 characters and one number`.
  It does not check leaked passwords.

## Other fields

These read another key of the same object. The other key is the input key, like `account_type`, not the Dart name `accountType`. If you give the Dart name of a field with another key, the build stops. `@Confirmed` and `@Same` compare the raw input of both keys. So `@Trim` does not change the compare.

| Annotation | Code | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@Confirmed()` | `confirmed` | `The {field} confirmation does not match` |
| `@Same('email')` | `same` | `The {field} must match {other}` |
| `@RequiredIf('type', 'company')` | `required_if` | `The {field} is required when {other} is {values}` |
| `@RequiredWith(['phone'])` | `required_with` | `The {field} is required when {others} is present` |
| `@RequiredUnless('type', 'guest')` | `required_unless` | `The {field} is required unless {other} is {values}` |
| `@RequiredWithout(['email'])` | `required_without` | `The {field} is required when {others} is not present` |
| `@RequiredWithoutAll(['email', 'phone'])` | `required_without_all` | `The {field} is required when none of {others} are present` |
| `@Different('old_password')` | `different` | `The {field} and {other} must be different` |
| `@ProhibitedIf('type', 'guest')` | `prohibited_if` | `The {field} is prohibited when {other} is {values}` |
| `@GreaterThanField('min_price')` | `greater_than` | `The {field} must be greater than {min}` |
| `@GreaterThanOrEqualField('min_price')` | `min` | `The {field} must be greater than or equal {min}` |
| `@LessThanField('max_price')` | `less_than` | `The {field} must be less than {max}` |
| `@LessThanOrEqualField('max_price')` | `max` | `The {field} must be less than or equal {max}` |

- `@Confirmed()` on `password` needs the key `password_confirmation` with the same value. The error is on `password`. Use `@Confirmed(other: 'password_again')` for another key.
  The DTO does not need a field for the confirmation key.
- Text and numbers match by text, both ways: `1234` matches `"1234"`, and `"1234"` matches `1234`.
- `@RequiredIf` and `@RequiredWith` work on a nullable field, a `Maybe` field or a field with a default. On an always-required field the build stops.
- `@RequiredIf('type', ['company', 'shop'])` takes a list: any of the values makes the field required. `"true"` matches `true`, `"1"` matches `1`. An enum value matches its name: `@RequiredIf('role', Role.admin)` matches `"admin"`.
- `@RequiredWith(['phone', 'email'])`: the field is required when any of the keys is there and not empty.
- `@RequiredUnless('type', 'guest')` makes the field required unless `type` is `guest`. A missing `type` counts as `null`, so the field is required then. It takes a list of values like `@RequiredIf`.
- `@RequiredWithout(['email'])`: the field is required when any of the keys is missing or empty. `@RequiredWithoutAll(['email', 'phone'])`: when all of them are missing or empty.
- `@RequiredUnless`, `@RequiredWithout` and `@RequiredWithoutAll` follow the same rules as `@RequiredIf`: a nullable, `Maybe` or default field, and input keys.
- `@Different('old_password')` needs a value that is not the same as the other key. It compares the raw input like `@Same`. A missing other key passes.
- `@ProhibitedIf('type', 'guest')` means: when `type` is `guest`, the field must be missing or empty. Empty is `null`, blank text, an empty list or an empty map. `0` and `false` fail. This is not the same as `@Prohibited()`, which fails on `null` and `[]`. It reads `type` and matches like `@RequiredIf`.
- `@GreaterThanField`, `@GreaterThanOrEqualField`, `@LessThanField` and `@LessThanOrEqualField` compare a value with another field. They are for `int`, `double` and `num` fields. They read the raw input of the other key: a number, or number text from a form. A missing other key (or one that is not a number) fails.
  `{min}` and `{max}` in the message are the other key. They use the codes of `@GreaterThan`, `@Min`, `@LessThan` and `@Max`.
- On a `List<T>` field, `@Different` checks the whole list, not each item. The field compare rules do not fit a list.
- Missing means: not there, `null`, blank text, an empty list or an empty map.
- They run in step 1, with the other "required" checks. `@Confirmed` and `@Same` run in step 2.

## Present or missing

These check if a key is sent and has a value.

| Annotation | Code | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@Filled()` | `filled` | `The {field} must have a value` |
| `@Present()` | `present` | `The {field} must be present` |
| `@Prohibited()` | `prohibited` | `The {field} is prohibited` |
| `@Accepted()` | `accepted` | `The {field} must be accepted` |
| `@Declined()` | `declined` | `The {field} must be declined` |

- `@Filled()`: a missing key passes. A key that is sent must have a value: not `null`, not blank text, not an empty list.
- `@Present()`: the key must be sent. Its value may be `null` or empty.
- `@Filled()` and `@Present()` are for a nullable, `Maybe` or default field, like `@RequiredIf`. They run in step 1.
- `@Prohibited()`: the key must be missing, or blank text like `""` or `"  "`. Any other sent value fails, also `null`, `[]`, `{}`, `0` and `false`. It reads the raw input, so it runs before the type check, in step 1. It is for a nullable, `Maybe` or default field.
- `@Accepted()` takes `true`, `1`, `"1"`, `"true"`, `"yes"` and `"on"`. `@Declined()` takes `false`, `0`, `"0"`, `"false"`, `"no"` and `"off"`. The text is case sensitive.
  Use them on a `bool` field with no default. Then a missing value fails with `required`. In a form, `yes` and `on` turn into `true` first. In a JSON body a `bool` field takes only `true` and `false`, unless the DTO has `@Dto(coerce: true)`.

```dart
@Accepted()
final bool terms;

@Present()
final String? note; // the key must be there, null is fine
```

## Skip a field

| Annotation | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `@ExcludeIf('type', 'person')` | when `type` is `person`, the field is skipped |
| `@ExcludeUnless('type', 'company')` | unless `type` is `company`, the field is skipped |

- A skipped field is not read and not checked. It gets its default, `null` or `Maybe.missing()`, as if it was not sent. The field is left out of the validated data.
- They read the raw input of the other key, and match like `@RequiredIf` (also with a list of values).
- `@ExcludeIf`: a missing other key does not skip. `@ExcludeUnless`: a missing other key counts as `null`, so the field is skipped.
- They are for a nullable, `Maybe` or default field. On an always-required field the build stops.
- The fluent schemas have `.excludeIf()` and `.excludeUnless()`. There the key is left out of the output. See [Skip a field](../packages/validation.md#skip-a-field).

```dart
final String type;

@ExcludeIf('type', 'person')
@MinLength(5)
final String? vatNumber; // not checked for a person
```

## Change text

These change the value before the rules run. They always run in this order, wherever you put them:
`@Trim`, then `@Lowercase` or `@Uppercase`, then the "empty string is missing" check.

| Annotation | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `@Trim()` | removes spaces at the start and the end |
| `@Lowercase()` | makes the text lower case |
| `@Uppercase()` | makes the text upper case |
| `@AllowEmpty()` | keeps `""` as a value. Without it, `""` counts as missing. |

They have no error and no JSON Schema output. `@Lowercase()` and `@Uppercase()` together stop the build.

## Bad value to default

| Annotation | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `@OrDefault()` | a bad value gives the default of the field (or `null`, or `Maybe.missing()`), not an error. |

- It drops type errors and the errors of the normal rules of the field.
- Errors from async rules (`@Unique`, `@Exists`, your `AsyncRule`) and from `validate()` are not dropped. They still give `422`.
- The field needs a default, a nullable type or a `Maybe` type. Else the build stops.

## Numbers

For `int`, `double` and `num` fields (and list items).

| Annotation | Code | Message | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@Min(18)` | `min` | `The {field} must be greater than or equal {min}` | `minimum` |
| `@Max(100)` | `max` | `The {field} must be less than or equal {max}` | `maximum` |
| `@Range(1, 10)` | `between` | `The {field} must be between {min} and {max}` | `minimum`, `maximum` |
| `@Positive()` | `greater_than` | `The {field} must be greater than 0` | `exclusiveMinimum: 0` |
| `@GreaterThan(0.5)` | `greater_than` | `The {field} must be greater than {min}` (exclusive) | `exclusiveMinimum` |
| `@LessThan(100)` | `less_than` | `The {field} must be less than {max}` (exclusive) | `exclusiveMaximum` |
| `@In([1, 2, 3])` | `in` | `The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values}` | `enum` |
| `@NotIn([0])` | `not_in` | `The {field} field cannot be {value}` | `not: {enum}` |

The values are `num`. `@Min(1.5)` on an `int` field stops the build. `@Range` checks that a number is between two values.

## Lists

For `List<T>` fields. These check the list, not the items.

| Annotation | Code | Message | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@MinItems(1)` | `min_items` | `The {field} must have at least {min} items` | `minItems` |
| `@MaxItems(5)` | `max_items` | `The {field} may not have more than {max} items` | `maxItems` |
| `@UniqueItems()` | `unique_items` | `The {field} must not have duplicate items` | `uniqueItems: true` |

`@UniqueItems()` works for `String`, numbers, `bool`, enums and `DateTime`. On a list of DTOs it stops the build.

## Dates

For `DateTime` fields.

| Annotation | Code | Message | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@After('2000-01-01')` | `after` | `The {field} must be a date after {date}` | `format: date-time` |
| `@Before('now')` | `before` | `The {field} must be a date before {date}` | `format: date-time` |
| `@AfterOrEqual('today')` | `after_or_equal` | `The {field} must be a date after or equal to {date}` | `format: date-time` |
| `@BeforeOrEqual('end_date')` | `before_or_equal` | `The {field} must be a date before or equal to {date}` | `format: date-time` |

- The value is one of:
    - an ISO 8601 date, like `'2000-01-01'`,
    - a word: `'now'` (the time of the request), `'today'`, `'tomorrow'` or `'yesterday'`. These are in UTC, and `'today'` is the start of the day,
    - the input key of another `DateTime` field of the same DTO, like `'start_date'`.
- With another field, the check uses its converted value. When that field has no value, the check passes.
- A text that is not a date, a word or a `DateTime` field stops the build.
- `@After` and `@Before` are exclusive: `@After('2000-01-01')` does not accept `2000-01-01T00:00:00Z`. `@AfterOrEqual` and `@BeforeOrEqual` accept the same time.
- Words and other fields need one `build_runner` run.

```dart
final DateTime startDate;

@After('start_date')
@BeforeOrEqual('tomorrow')
final DateTime endDate;
```

## Files

For `RequestFile` and `List<RequestFile>` fields.

| Annotation | Code | Message | JSON Schema |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `@MaxSize('2MB')` | `max_size` | `The {field} may not be larger than {max}` | `maxLength` (bytes) |
| `@Mimes(['pdf', 'png'])` | `mimes` | `The {field} must be a file of type: {types}` | `contentMediaType` |
| `@Image()` | `image` | `The {field} must be an image` | `contentMediaType: image/*` |
| `@MinSize('10KB')` | `min_size` | `The {field} must be at least {min}` | `minLength` (bytes) |
| `@MimeTypes(['image/png', 'image/*'])` | `mime_types` | `The {field} must be a file of type: {types}` | `contentMediaType` |
| `@Dimensions(minWidth: 100, ratio: 3 / 2)` | `dimensions` | `The {field} has invalid image dimensions` | `contentMediaType: image/*` |

- `@MaxSize` and `@MinSize` units: `B`, `KB`, `MB`, `GB`. `1KB` = 1024 bytes. A bad size text stops the build.
- `@Mimes` takes file extensions. Dox finds the real type from the first bytes of the file.
  The file name extension must not name another type, or a type a browser runs (like `html` or `svg`).
  So `x.html` with GIF bytes does not pass. An empty or unknown extension is fine.
  For zip based types (like `docx` or `xlsx`), the file name extension must match too.
  For types without a byte signature (like `txt` or `csv`), it uses the file name extension.
- `@Image()` is `@Mimes(['jpg', 'jpeg', 'png', 'gif', 'webp', 'bmp'])`. No `svg`.
- `@MimeTypes` takes MIME types. Dox turns each one into file extensions, then checks the real bytes like `@Mimes`.
  It does not trust the content type the client sent.
  `image/*` means: jpg, jpeg, png, gif, webp, bmp, tif, tiff, ico, heic, heif, avif and psd. No `svg`.
  This is wider than `@Image()`, and browsers can not show most of the extra types.
  For images that browsers can show, use `@Image()` or list the MIME types.
  Write `image/jpeg`, not `image/jpg`. `image/jpg` is not a real MIME type, so it never matches.
  An unknown MIME type never matches.
- `@Dimensions` checks the width and height in pixels. Limits: `width`, `height` (exact), `minWidth`, `maxWidth`, `minHeight`, `maxHeight` and `ratio` (width / height, like `3 / 2`).
  Give at least one limit, or the build stops.
  It reads only the image header of PNG, GIF, WebP and JPEG files, never the whole file.
  Any other file, or a broken or cut short header, fails.
  For a JPEG over 1 MB, Dox reads the first 128 KB. A JPEG with more photo metadata than that before its size fails.
  A `ratio` passes when it is off by less than one pixel.
- The JSON Schema of a file is `{"type": "string", "format": "binary"}`, plus the keys above.

With fluent schemas, the same rules are on `v.file()`. Sizes there are in bytes, not text:

```dart
v.file()
    .maxSize(2 * 1024 * 1024) // 2 MB
    .mimeTypes(<String>['image/jpeg', 'image/png'])
    .dimensions(minWidth: 100, maxWidth: 2000);
```

The fluent methods are `maxSize(bytes)`, `minSize(bytes)`, `mimes(types)`, `mimeTypes(types)`, `dimensions(...)`, `image()` and `extensions(types)`.

## Database

From `dox_orm`. Async: they run after all other checks passed.

| Annotation | Code | Message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@Unique(table, {column, ignoreParam, ignoreColumn, connection})` | `unique` | `The {field} has already been taken` |
| `@Exists(table, {column, connection})` | `exists` | `The selected {field} is invalid` |

- `@Unique` column default: the input key. `@Exists` column default: `id`.
- They read the table, not the model. So soft-deleted rows count too.
- `ignoreParam: 'id'` skips the row where `ignoreColumn` (default `id`) equals the path param `{id}`.
- They add nothing to the JSON Schema.

See [Database rules](validation.md#database-rules-unique-and-exists).

In a fluent schema, use `v.string().unique('users', column: 'email')` and `v.int().exists('teams')`. See [Fluent schemas](../packages/validation.md#more-rules).

## Keys and DTO options

| Annotation | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `@Name('emailAddress')` | the input key for this field. Default: the field name in snake_case. |
| `@Dto()` | marks the class. |
| `@Dto(source: Source.query)` | where to read: `Source.auto` (default), `Source.query`, `Source.body`. |
| `@Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field)` | keys: `KeyCase.snake` (default) or `KeyCase.field` (the Dart name as is). |
| `@Dto(strict: true)` | unknown keys are errors. Default `false`: they are dropped. |
| `@Dto(emptyStringsToNull: true)` | `""` is read as `null`, not as missing. Default `false`. |
| `@Dto(trim: true)` | trims every `String` field and text item, like `@Trim()` on each. Default `false`. |
| `@Dto(coerce: true)` | a JSON body may send text for numbers and bools, like a form. Default `false`. |
| `@Dto(messages: {...})` | messages by `code` or `key.code`. A dotted path like `address.city.required` or `tags.*.required` works too. A Laravel rule name works too, like `name.min`. See [Messages](validation.md#laravel-rule-names-in-message-keys). |
| `@Dto(attributes: {...})` | the names shown for `{field}`, by key, like `{'first_name': 'first name'}`. See [Names for `{field}`](validation.md#names-for-field). |
| `@Describe('...')` | on a field: a short text for the `description` of the field in the JSON Schema. It does not change the checks. |

A `///` doc comment on a field becomes its `description` in the JSON Schema.
`@Describe` wins over the `///` comment. Use it when the text is for API users and MCP clients, not for the code.
The OpenAPI docs and MCP tools (`McpDtoTool`) show it.

```dart
@Describe('Category ID (see list_categories).') final int categoryId;
```

## Types in detail

How each field type reads input. The short table is in [Types](validation.md#types).

- **JSON is strict.** In a JSON body, `"18"` is not an `int`. You get the error `integer`. With `@Dto(coerce: true)`, JSON is read like form text for `int`, `double`, `num` and `bool`, and a `bool` also takes `1` and `0`.
- **Query and form data are text.** Dox turns the text into the field type first. If it can not, you get the type error.
- `int` takes `18` or `18.0`, never a fraction. `"4.5"` or `4.5` gives `integer`.
- `bool` in text takes `true`, `1`, `yes`, `on` and `false`, `0`, `no`, `off` (any case).
- `DateTime` takes `2024-01-31` or `2024-01-31T10:00:00Z`. A value without a time zone is read as UTC.
  The result is always UTC (`isUtc == true`). A number (timestamp) is not allowed.
- An `enum` matches the Dart name exactly. `"Admin"` does not match `Role.admin`. Custom wire values (like `"ADMIN"`) are not supported.
- `Object?` and `dynamic` take any value. They are not checked.
- `Map<String, dynamic>` must be an object. Its values are not checked.
- In query and form data, one value for a `List<T>` field gives a list with one item.
- In bracket keys, list indexes are sorted and packed: `items[3]` alone gives a list with one item.
- In query and form data, a list can have at most 1000 items, and keys can nest at most 10 levels. More gives `422` with the key `_root`.

## Body types

| Body | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `application/json` (or any `+json` type) | read with strict JSON types |
| `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `multipart/form-data` | read as text, then converted |
| any other content type | `415 Unsupported Media Type` |
| JSON that is not valid | `400 Bad Request` |
| JSON that is not an object (like `[1, 2]`) | `422` with the key `_root` |

## The order of checks

1. Read the input and convert types. Change text (`@Trim`, `@Lowercase`, `@Uppercase`). Find missing required fields.
2. The field rules, top to bottom. The first rule that fails stops the other rules of that field. So there is no `@Bail`. A fluent schema runs all rules, unless you add `.bail()`. See [Stop at the first error](../packages/validation.md#stop-at-the-first-error).
3. The `validate()` method (nested DTOs first, then the parent).
4. Async rules (`@Unique`, `@Exists`, your `AsyncRule`), one at a time, in field order.

Each step runs only when the step before it had no errors. So the database is never asked about input that is already wrong.

- Steps 1 and 2 run per DTO. So one answer can have a type error in `address` and a rule error in `items.1`.
- Inside one step, Dox collects the errors of all fields.
- A default value is not checked by the field rules. Async rules check the final value.

## What the generator checks

The build stops with a clear error when:

- a field is not `final`, or is not a parameter of the unnamed constructor,
- a field type is not supported (see [Types](validation.md#types)),
- a rule does not fit the field type (like `@Email()` on an `int`),
- a `Maybe<T>` field has no `const Maybe.missing()` default,
- `@RequiredIf`, `@RequiredWith`, `@RequiredUnless`, `@RequiredWithout`, `@RequiredWithoutAll`, `@Filled`, `@Present`, `@Prohibited`, `@ProhibitedIf`, `@ExcludeIf` or `@ExcludeUnless` is on a field that is always required,
- `@OrDefault()` is on a field that is always required (no default, not nullable and not a `Maybe`),
- a rule that reads another key (like `@RequiredIf`, `@Same`, `@Different`, `@ExcludeIf` or `@GreaterThanField`) names a Dart field (like `accountType`) instead of its input key (`account_type`),
- `@After`, `@Before`, `@AfterOrEqual` or `@BeforeOrEqual` has a text that is not a date, a word or another `DateTime` field,
- `@DateFormatted` has a letter it does not know,
- two `@Dto` classes in the app have the same name,
- the class is generic, or extends another class (other than `Object`).


---

# Cache

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/digging-deeper/cache/

# Cache

`Cache()` keeps data that is slow to make, so the next request can read it fast.

It runs on [`dox_cache`](../packages/cache.md), which is built into `dox_core`.

## Drivers

| Driver | Where the data is | Shared between isolates | Locks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | files in a folder (default `storage/cache`) | yes, on the same machine | yes, on the same machine |
| `memory` | a map inside the isolate | no | yes |
| `redis` | a Redis server | yes, also between machines | yes |
| `null` | nowhere. It stores nothing | - | no |
| `database` | a table in your database, from [`dox_cache_database`](../packages/cache.md#database-store) | yes, also between machines | yes |

!!! warning "Many isolates"
    Dox runs one isolate per CPU core. Each isolate has its own `memory` store.
    So a value you put in one isolate is missing in the others.
    Use `redis` or `database` when all isolates and servers must see the same data.

## Install

```bash
dox add cache
```

Add `--store=redis` (or `memory`, `database`) to pick the default store. `file` is the default.
It writes `lib/config/cache.dart`, adds it to `lib/config/app.dart` and adds the `CACHE_STORE` key. `redis` also adds the `REDIS_*` keys.
`database` also adds `dox_cache_database`, its provider and the cache table migration. It needs `dox add orm` first.
It never overwrites a file, so it is safe to run twice.
A new app already has it. To set it up by hand, follow [Config](#config).

## Config

A new project already has `lib/config/cache.dart`, with a `file` store and a `memory` store.
`CACHE_STORE` in `.env` picks the default store (`file` when it is not set).
To add a store, edit the file. This example adds a `redis` store:

```dart title="lib/config/cache.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

CacheConfig cache = CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: env.cacheStore,
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 10000},
    'redis': <String, dynamic>{
      'driver': 'redis',
      'host': env.redisHost,
      'port': env.redisPort,
      'prefix': 'app_cache:',
    },
  },
);
```

Redis needs two keys that a new project does not have yet. Add them to
`lib/config/env.dart` and run `dart run build_runner build`:

```dart title="lib/config/env.dart"
  String get redisHost => '127.0.0.1';

  int get redisPort => 6379;
```

`lib/config/app.dart` already passes it to `AppConfig(cache: cache)`.
Each store is made once per isolate, the first time you use it.

### Store options

| Driver | Options |
| --- | --- |
| `file` | `path` (default `storage/cache`), `prefix` |
| `memory` | `max_size`: the most items. When it is full, the item that was used least recently is removed. No limit by default. Expired items are removed when read, and by a sweep after many writes (at least 1000). Also `prefix`. |
| `redis` | `host` (default `127.0.0.1`), `port` (default `6379`), `username`, `password`, `db` (default `0`), `tls` (`true`/`false`), `pool_size` (default 10), `max_value_bytes` (no limit by default), `prefix` |

A `redis` store with no `prefix` gets `<app name>_cache:` from `APP_NAME`, like `my_shop_cache:`. So two apps on one Redis do not share keys. The other drivers use `dox_cache:`.
You rarely need `pool_size`: the cache sends no blocking commands, so each isolate uses about one Redis connection.

## Encrypt the cache

By default the cache keeps plain JSON. Anyone who can read the cache file or the Redis database can read the values.
To hide them, add `'encrypt': true` to a `file` or `redis` store:

```dart
'file': {'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache', 'encrypt': true},
```

- It is off by default. A store without the option is not changed.
- The normal `Dox().cache` has the encrypter set for you, and values are encrypted with your `APP_KEY`. A `CacheManager` you build yourself needs `encrypter:` (for example `const CryptCacheEncrypter()`). Old keys in `previousKeys` can still read old entries.
- When the key changes, the old entries cannot be read. They count as a miss. The cache then fills again.
- On a `file` store, the whole file is encrypted, also the expiry time. Lock files are not encrypted. They hold no values.
- On a `redis` store, a plain `int` stays plain text, so `increment` and `decrement` still work. Every other value is encrypted. Tag counters are `int` values, so they stay plain too. To keep a secret number encrypted, store it as a `String`.
- A `memory` or `null` store does not encrypt. Its values never leave the process. The option still needs an encrypter, or building the store throws.
- The option must be `true` or `false`. Any other type, like `'true'`, throws an `ArgumentError`.
- Old plain values read as a miss after you turn the option on. The one exception is an `int` on Redis, which is plain by design and still reads as a value.
- On a `file` store, `prune` deletes files that cannot be decrypted. After a key change with no previous keys, or in a folder that apps with different keys share, `prune` removes those files.
- Cache keys and tag names are not encrypted. A value is not tied to its key, so someone who can write to Redis or the cache folder can copy an encrypted value to another key. Encryption protects against reading only.
- `maxValueBytes` is checked on the plain JSON size. The stored encrypted text is about a third bigger.

## Values are JSON

A value must be a JSON type: `Map`, `List`, `String`, `num`, `bool` or `null`.
A `Map` comes back as `Map<String, dynamic>`. A `List` comes back as `List<dynamic>`.

## Usage

```dart
// no duration: the value stays forever
await Cache().put('foo', 'bar');
await Cache().put('foo', 'bar', duration: Duration(minutes: 10));

await Cache().get('foo');             // 'bar', or null when missing
await Cache().get('foo', 'default');  // 'default' when missing
await Cache().has('foo');             // true
await Cache().forget('foo');          // remove one key
await Cache().forever('settings', <String, dynamic>{'theme': 'dark'});
await Cache().flush();                // remove all items of the store

await Cache().putMany(<String, Object?>{'a': 1, 'b': 2}); // many at once
await Cache().many(<String>['a', 'b', 'c']); // {a: 1, b: 2, c: null}
```

### `remember`

`remember` reads the value from the cache. When it is missing, the function runs and its result is stored.
The value is stored as JSON. Return maps, lists, strings and numbers, not models.

```dart
List<dynamic> posts = await Cache().remember(
  'posts',
  Duration(minutes: 5),
  () async => (await Post().all()).map((Post p) => p.toJson()).toList(),
);
```

`rememberForever(key, fn)` does the same with no expiry.

- `decode:` turns the stored JSON back into your type on a hit, like `decode: (j) => (j as List).cast<String>()`. Without it, use JSON types like `List<dynamic>`.
- `lock: true` lets only one caller on all isolates and servers run the function. The others wait for its value.

`flexible(key, fresh, stale, fn)` serves the value as it is for `fresh`. Then, until `stale` more has passed, it still serves the old value at once and runs `fn` once in the background:

```dart
Map<String, dynamic> stats = await Cache().flexible(
  'stats', Duration(minutes: 1), Duration(minutes: 5), loadStats,
);
```

After `fresh` + `stale`, the value is gone and the next call waits for `fn`.

Pass `null` as `stale` to keep the value until a refresh replaces it. Use it when an old value is better than no value, like rates from a service that can be down. When `fn` fails, callers still get the last good value:

```dart
Map<String, dynamic> rates = await Cache().flexible(
  'rates', Duration(minutes: 10), null, fetchRates,
);
```

### `getRaw`

`getRaw` gives the stored JSON text as it is. Send it as a response with no decode and no encode:

```dart
String? json = await Cache().getRaw('posts');
if (json != null) {
  return response(json).contentType(ContentType.json);
}
```

A missing key gives `null`. A stored `String` comes back as JSON, with its quotes: `"bar"`.
The `memory` driver also keeps JSON text, so `get` decodes on every hit there too.

### Another store

`store(name)` uses a store from the config instead of the default store:

```dart
await Cache().store('redis').put('foo', 'bar');
await Cache().store('memory').get('foo');
```

`store()` changes the `Cache` it is called on. The flag `cacheCopies` makes `store()` and `tags()` give a new `Cache`. See [Core flags](../reference/app-config.md#core-flags).

### Tags

Put items under a tag. Then you can remove only the items of that tag:

```dart
await Cache().tag('users').put('u1', 'Ann');
await Cache().tag('users').flush(); // removes only the items of this tag
```

`tags(['a', 'b'])` uses many tags.

### Locks

A lock makes sure only one request (or one server) runs some code at a time.
The `memory`, `file` and `redis` stores support locks. The `memory` lock works inside one isolate only. The `file` lock works for all isolates on one machine. Use `redis` when many servers must share the lock.

```dart
CacheLock lock = Cache().store('redis').lock('report', Duration(seconds: 30));
if (await lock.get()) {
  try {
    await buildReport();
  } finally {
    await lock.release();
  }
}
```

- `get()` tries once. It is `true` when you got the lock.
- `block(Duration(seconds: 5))` tries again and again until the time is over.
  It gives `false` when the time is over. With the flag `CacheFlags(lockThrows: true)` it throws `LockTimeoutException`. See [CacheConfig](../reference/app-config.md#cacheconfig).
- The lock is freed after its `ttl`, even if you never call `release()`.
- `block(timeout, callback)` runs the callback while it holds the lock, then frees it.
- `forceRelease()` frees the lock, whoever holds it.

### More methods

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `add(key, value, duration:)` | store only when the key is missing. `true` when it was stored |
| `pull(key)` | get the value and remove it, in one step |
| `increment(key, [by])` / `decrement(key, [by])` | change an integer. A missing key starts at 0 |
| `touch(key, duration:)` | give a key a new expiry. `false` when it is missing |
| `repository` | the `dox_cache` `CacheStore`, for everything else |

See [dox_cache](../packages/cache.md) for custom drivers.

## Tests

To use a memory store in tests, see [Testing](testing.md#test-the-cache).
