The generated method takes the same arguments, without the query.

!!! warning "Pick a free name"
    The scope name must not be a field or a method of the model.
    For example, a scope `active` next to a field `active` does not work.
    Use `isActive`. A scope named like a query method (`count`, `get`) is never called.

## Global scopes

`@Scope(global: true)` adds the scope to every query of the model.
This includes `get()`, `find()`, `all()`, `count()`, `paginate()`,
query updates and deletes, and relation queries.
A global scope counts as a `where`: `Post().delete()` deletes only the rows in the scope.
With `withoutGlobalScopes()` and no `where`, the write throws a `StateError`.

```dart
@DoxModel()
class Post extends PostGenerator {
  @Column()
  bool? archived;

  /// every query leaves out archived posts
  @Scope(global: true)
  static QueryBuilder<Post> notArchived(QueryBuilder<Post> q) {
    return q.where('archived', false);
  }
}

await Post().get(); // ... WHERE ("archived" = false)
```

The global scope goes in brackets, and your own conditions too.
So an `orWhere()` in your query can not skip the scope.

Remove a global scope for one query with `withoutGlobalScope()`,
or remove all of them with `withoutGlobalScopes()`:

```dart
await Post().withoutGlobalScope('notArchived').get();
await Post().withoutGlobalScopes().find(1);
```

The name of a global scope is the method name.

!!! info
    `save()`, `delete()` and `restore()` on a model instance work on that one row.
    They do not use the global scopes.
    Soft deletes are not a global scope. Use `withTrash()` for them.


---

# Attribute casts

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/database/model/casts/

# Attribute casts

A cast changes a column value between the database and Dart.

For example, it reads JSON text as a map, or saves an enum by its name.
Casts work the same on Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite.

Set a cast with `cast` on `@Column()`. Then run `dart run build_runner build`.

```dart
enum Status { draft, live }

enum Level { low, mid, high }

@DoxModel()
class Item extends ItemGenerator {
  @Column(cast: JsonCast())
  Map<String, dynamic>? meta;

  @Column(cast: ListCast<String>())
  List<String>? tags;

  @Column()
  bool? active; // gets BoolCast()

  @Column()
  Status? status; // gets EnumCast(Status.values)

  @Column(cast: EnumCast<Level>(Level.values, byIndex: true))
  Level? level;
}
```

The cast runs when a row is read (`get()`, `find()` and others),
when the model is saved, and in `toJson()`.

## Built-in casts

| Cast | Dart value | Database value |
|---|---|---|
| `JsonCast()` | a map or a list | JSON, or JSON in a text column |
| `ListCast<E>()` | a typed list, like `List<String>` | JSON, or JSON in a text column |
| `BoolCast()` | `bool` | boolean, or a number like `tinyint` (0 is false), or the text `1`, `0`, `true`, `false`, `t`, `f` |
| `EnumCast<E>(E.values)` | an enum | text with the enum name |
| `EnumCast<E>(E.values, byIndex: true)` | an enum | a number, the enum index |

You do not need `cast` for two field types:

- A `bool` field gets `BoolCast()`.
- An enum field gets `EnumCast(values)`, so it is saved by its name.

`DateTime` fields need no cast either. Dox reads them on every database.

!!! info
    A cast changes the values of a model. It does not change a `where()` value.
    Use the database value there, like `where('status', Status.live.name)`.

## Your own cast

Extend `Cast<T>`. `get()` gets the database value and returns the Dart value.
`set()` gets the Dart value and returns the value to save.
The class needs a const constructor.

```dart
class Money {
  final int cents;
  const Money(this.cents);
}

class MoneyCast extends Cast<Money> {
  const MoneyCast();

  @override
  Money? get(dynamic value) => value == null ? null : Money(value as int);

  @override
  dynamic set(Money? value) => value?.cents;
}

@DoxModel()
class Product extends ProductGenerator {
  @Column(cast: MoneyCast())
  Money? price;
}
```

A cast can take const arguments, like `EnumCast` does.
The generator copies the `cast` code into the generated file,
so the names in it must be imported in the model file.

A column with `beforeGet` does not use its cast.


---

# Counting relations

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/database/model/counting-relations/

# Counting relations

`withCount()` adds the number of related rows to each model.

It does not load the rows. It adds a subquery to the select,
so you get the counts with the same query.

It works with `hasOne`, `hasMany`, `hasOneThrough`, `hasManyThrough`, `manyToMany`, `morphOne` and `morphMany` relations.

```dart
@DoxModel()
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @HasMany(Post)
  List<Post> posts = <Post>[];
}

List<User> users = await User().withCount('posts').get();

users.first.countOf('posts'); // 3
users.first.toJson();         // {..., "posts_count": 3}
```

The key is the relation name in snake_case and `_count`, like `posts_count`.
Use the relation name (the field name) in `withCount()` and `countOf()`.

## Count only some rows

Give a function to add conditions to the related rows.
Use `as` to give the count its own key.

```dart
List<User> users = await User()
    .withCount('posts')
    .withCount('posts as published_count', (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
      q.where('published', true);
    })
    .get();

users.first.countOf('posts');               // all posts
users.first.aggregate('published_count');   // published posts
```

The global scopes and soft deletes of the related model are used in the count.

## With other query methods

`withCount()` works with `where()`, `orderBy()`, `find()`, `getFirst()`,
`paginate()` and with `preload()` or eager relations:

```dart
User? user = await User().preload('posts').withCount('posts').find(1);
user?.posts;              // the posts
user?.countOf('posts');   // the number of posts
```

## Sum, average, min and max

`withSum()`, `withAvg()`, `withMin()` and `withMax()` work the same way, on one column of the related rows.
The value is null when there is no related row.

```dart
User? user = await User()
    .withSum('posts', 'views')
    .withAvg('posts', 'views')
    .withMin('posts', 'views')
    .withMax('posts', 'views')
    .find(1);

user?.aggregate('posts_sum_views');
user?.aggregate('posts_avg_views');
user?.aggregate('posts_min_views');
user?.aggregate('posts_max_views');
```

## Exists

`withExists()` adds `<relation>_exists`. It is `true` when there is at least one related row.
It takes a function and `as`, like `withCount()`.

```dart
User? user = await User()
    .withExists('posts')
    .withExists('posts as has_published', (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
      q.where('published', true);
    })
    .find(1);

user?.aggregate('posts_exists');   // true or false
user?.aggregate('has_published');  // true or false
```

!!! info
    `withCount()` is not for `belongsTo` relations. It throws an `UnsupportedError`.
    It works for a relation to the same table, like the children of a category.

To keep only the rows that have related rows, use `whereHas()` or `has()`.
See [Query by relations](relation-queries.md).


---

# Query by relations

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/database/model/relation-queries/

# Query by relations

`whereHas()`, `whereDoesntHave()` and `has()` keep the rows of a query by their related rows.

For example: get the users that have a post.
These methods do not load the related rows.
They add a subquery to the `where` part, so it is still one query.
To load the related rows, use `preload()`. See [HasMany](relationship/has-many.md).

The examples on this page use these models:

```dart
@DoxModel()
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @HasMany(Post)
  List<Post> posts = <Post>[];
}

@DoxModel()
class Post extends PostGenerator {
  @Column()
  bool? published;

  @BelongsTo(User)
  User? user;

  @HasMany(Comment)
  List<Comment> comments = <Comment>[];
}
```

## `whereHas`

Keeps the rows that have at least one related row.
Use the relation name (the field name).

```dart
List<User> users = await User().whereHas('posts').get();
// WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM "post" WHERE ...)
```

Give a function to add conditions to the related rows.

```dart
List<User> users = await User().whereHas('posts', (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('published', true);
}).get();
```

This keeps the users that have at least one published post.

## `whereDoesntHave`

Keeps the rows that have no related row.

```dart
List<User> users = await User().whereDoesntHave('posts').get();
// WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM "post" WHERE ...)

List<User> noDrafts = await User().whereDoesntHave('posts', (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('published', false);
}).get();
```

## `orWhereHas` and `orWhereDoesntHave`

They are the same, but they join the condition with `OR`.

```dart
List<User> users = await User()
    .where('name', 'Ann')
    .orWhereHas('posts')
    .get();
// WHERE "name" = @name_p0 OR EXISTS (...)

await User().where('name', 'Ann').orWhereDoesntHave('posts').get();
```

## `has`

`has()` counts the related rows.
Give an operator and a number.

```dart
// at least one post
await User().has('posts').get();

// three posts or more
await User().has('posts', '>=', 3).get();

// no post
await User().has('posts', '=', 0).get();

// more than one published post
await User().has('posts', '>', 1, (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('published', true);
}).get();
```

- The default is `'>='` and `1`: at least one related row.
- The operator must be one of `=`, `!=`, `<>`, `<`, `>`, `<=` or `>=`.
  Any other operator throws an `ArgumentError`.

## Relations of relations

Use a dot to check a relation of a relation.

```dart
// users that have a post with a comment
await User().whereHas('posts.comments').get();

// users that have a post with a comment by user 1
await User().whereHas('posts.comments', (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('user_id', 1);
}).get();

// users that have no post with a comment
await User().whereDoesntHave('posts.comments').get();
```

The function is for the last relation (`comments`).

With `has()`, the count is for the last relation of one row.
`has('posts.comments', '>=', 2)` keeps the users that have a post with two comments or more.

## Rules

- It works with `hasOne`, `hasMany`, `hasOneThrough`, `hasManyThrough`, `belongsTo`, `manyToMany`, `morphOne` and `morphMany` relations.
  A `morphTo` relation throws an `UnsupportedError`.
- Soft deleted related rows do not count.
  To count them, set `q.withTrashed = true` in the function.
- The global scopes and the `onQuery` function of the relation are used.
- It works with `where()`, `count()`, `paginate()`, `withCount()` and the other query methods.
- Start the query with a model, like `User()`.
  On `QueryBuilder.table()` it throws a `StateError`.
- A name that is not a relation of the model throws an `ArgumentError`.
- It works for a relation to the same table, like a `Category` with a parent `Category`.

## A relation to the same table

The subquery gives the table its own name, so each row is not compared with itself.

```dart
// categories that have at least one child category
List<Category> parents = await Category().whereHas('children').get();

// categories whose parent is named 'Books'
List<Category> books = await Category()
    .whereHas('parent', (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
      q.where('name', 'Books');
    })
    .get();
```

!!! warning
    In the function, write the column without the table name: `name`, not `categories.name`.
    With the table name, the column points to the parent row, not to the related row.


---

# HasOne

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/database/model/relationship/has-one/

# HasOne

Use `HasOne` when one row of this table has one row in another table.

For example, a user has one user info row.
The other table keeps the foreign key (`user_info.user_id`).

## Define it

Add a field with `@HasOne(...)` to the model. The field type is the related model, nullable.

```dart title="lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

import '../user_info/user_info.model.dart';

part 'user.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel()
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @Column()
  String? name;

  @HasOne(UserInfo)
  UserInfo? userInfo;
}
```

```dart title="lib/app/models/user_info/user_info.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

part 'user_info.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel()
class UserInfo extends UserInfoGenerator {
  @Column()
  int? userId; // column user_id

  @Column()
  String? address;
}
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` after you add a relationship.

## Load it

The relation is not loaded by default. Load it in one of these ways.
Use the field name (`'userInfo'`) as the relation name.

### `preload`

Use it when you load the models with a query.

```dart
User? user = await User().preload('userInfo').find(1);
print(user?.userInfo?.address);
```

`preload` works with `find`, `get`, `all` and `getFirst`.
For a list of users, it runs one query for all of them.

### `$getRelation`

Use it when you already have the model.

```dart
User? user = await User().find(1);
await user?.$getRelation('userInfo');
print(user?.userInfo?.address);
```

### `related`

Use it when you need more conditions on the related row.

```dart
User? user = await User().find(1);
UserInfo? info = await user
    ?.related<UserInfo>('userInfo')
    ?.where('address', '!=', '')
    .getFirst();
```

It does not set `user.userInfo`.

### `eager`

Use it when every query of `User` should load the relation.

```dart
@HasOne(UserInfo, eager: true)
UserInfo? userInfo;
```

You do not call `preload`.

The load runs this SQL:

```sql
SELECT *, "user_id" as "_owner_id" FROM "user_info" WHERE "user_id" IN (@user_id_p0)
```

`reload()` and a preload set the relation fields again, also when there is no related row. See [Relationships](../index.md#relationships).

## Filter by it

`whereHas()` keeps the users that have a `user_info` row.
`whereDoesntHave()` keeps the users without one.
It does not load the `UserInfo`.

```dart
List<User> users = await User().whereHas('userInfo').get();

List<User> inParis = await User().whereHas('userInfo', (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('address', 'Paris');
}).get();

List<User> noInfo = await User().whereDoesntHave('userInfo').get();
```

See [Query by relations](../relation-queries.md).

## Options

| Option | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `foreignKey` | `{this model}_id`, like `user_id` | The column in the related table that points to this model. |
| `localKey` | the primary key of this model | The column in this table that `foreignKey` points to. |
| `onQuery` | none | A static function that changes the query. |
| `eager` | `false` | Load the relation on every query. |

The default `foreignKey` uses the class name in snake_case.
`User` gives `user_id`, also when the table is `users`.

### `foreignKey` and `localKey`

```dart
@HasOne(UserInfo, foreignKey: 'owner_id', localKey: 'id')
UserInfo? userInfo;
```

### `onQuery`

`onQuery` is a static function in the same model class.
It gets the query of the related model and returns it.

```dart
@DoxModel()
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @HasOne(UserInfo, onQuery: onlyActive)
  UserInfo? userInfo;

  static QueryBuilder<UserInfo> onlyActive(UserInfo q) {
    return q.where('status', 'active');
  }
}
```

## In JSON

- A relation with `eager: true` is always in `toJson()`.
- A relation loaded with `preload` is in `toJson()` of that query.
- The JSON key is the field name in snake_case: `user_info`.


---

# HasMany

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/database/model/relationship/has-many/

# HasMany

Use `HasMany` when one row of this table has many rows in another table.

For example, a user has many posts.
The other table keeps the foreign key (`post.user_id`).

## Define it

Add a field with `@HasMany(...)` to the model.
The field type is a list of the related model. Start it as an empty list.

```dart title="lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

import '../post/post.model.dart';

part 'user.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel()
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @Column()
  String? name;

  @HasMany(Post)
  List<Post> posts = <Post>[];
}
```

```dart title="lib/app/models/post/post.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

part 'post.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel()
class Post extends PostGenerator {
  @Column()
  int? userId; // column user_id

  @Column()
  String? title;

  @Column()
  String? status;
}
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` after you add a relationship.

## Load it

The relation is not loaded by default. Load it in one of these ways.
Use the field name (`'posts'`) as the relation name.

### `preload`

Use it when you load the models with a query.

```dart
User? user = await User().preload('posts').find(1);
print(user?.posts.length);

List<User> users = await User().preload('posts').get();
```

`preload` works with `find`, `get`, `all` and `getFirst`.
For a list of users, it runs one query for all of them.
A user without posts gets an empty list.

### `$getRelation`

Use it when you already have the model.

```dart
User? user = await User().find(1);
await user?.$getRelation('posts');
print(user?.posts.length);
```

### `related`

Use it when you need more conditions on the related rows.

```dart
User? user = await User().find(1);
List<Post> activePosts = await user
        ?.related<Post>('posts')
        ?.where('status', 'active')
        .orderBy('id', 'desc')
        .get() ??
    <Post>[];
```

It does not set `user.posts`.

### `eager`

Use it when every query of `User` should load the relation.

```dart
@HasMany(Post, eager: true)
List<Post> posts = <Post>[];
```

You do not call `preload`.

The load runs this SQL:

```sql
SELECT *, "user_id" as "_owner_id" FROM "post" WHERE "user_id" IN (@user_id_p0, ...)
```

`reload()` and a preload set the relation fields again, also when there is no related row. See [Relationships](../index.md#relationships).

## Filter by it

`whereHas()` keeps the users that have a post.
`whereDoesntHave()` keeps the users with no post.
It does not load the posts.

```dart
List<User> writers = await User().whereHas('posts', (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('status', 'active');
}).get();

List<User> noPosts = await User().whereDoesntHave('posts').get();
List<User> busy = await User().has('posts', '>=', 10).get();
```

See [Query by relations](../relation-queries.md).

## Options

| Option | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `foreignKey` | `{this model}_id`, like `user_id` | The column in the related table that points to this model. |
| `localKey` | the primary key of this model | The column in this table that `foreignKey` points to. |
| `onQuery` | none | A static function that changes the query. |
| `eager` | `false` | Load the relation on every query. |

The default `foreignKey` uses the class name in snake_case.
`User` gives `user_id`, also when the table is `users`.

### `foreignKey` and `localKey`

```dart
@HasMany(Book, foreignKey: 'author_code', localKey: 'code')
List<Book> books = <Book>[];
```

### `onQuery`

`onQuery` is a static function in the same model class.
It gets the query of the related model and returns it.
You can have two fields on the same model with different queries.

```dart
@DoxModel()
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @HasMany(Post)
  List<Post> posts = <Post>[];

  @HasMany(Post, onQuery: onlyActive)
  List<Post> activePosts = <Post>[];

  static QueryBuilder<Post> onlyActive(Post q) {
    return q.where('status', 'active').orderBy('id', 'desc');
  }
}
```

## In JSON

- A relation with `eager: true` is always in `toJson()`.
- A relation loaded with `preload` is in `toJson()` of that query.
- The JSON key is the field name in snake_case.


---

# BelongsTo

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/database/model/relationship/belongs-to/

# BelongsTo

Use `BelongsTo` when this table keeps the foreign key to another table.

For example, a comment belongs to a user.
The comment table has the column `user_id`.

`BelongsTo` is the other side of [HasOne](has-one.md) and [HasMany](has-many.md).

## Define it

Add a field with `@BelongsTo(...)` to the model. The field type is the related model, nullable.

```dart title="lib/app/models/comment/comment.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

import '../user/user.model.dart';

part 'comment.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel()
class Comment extends CommentGenerator {
  @Column()
  int? userId; // column user_id

  @Column()
  String? content;

  @BelongsTo(User)
  User? user;
}
```

```dart title="lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

part 'user.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel()
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @Column()
  String? name;

  @Column()
  String? status;
}
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` after you add a relationship.

## Load it

The relation is not loaded by default. Load it in one of these ways.
Use the field name (`'user'`) as the relation name.

### `preload`

Use it when you load the models with a query.

```dart
List<Comment> comments = await Comment().preload('user').all();
for (Comment comment in comments) {
  print(comment.user?.name);
}
```

`preload` works with `find`, `get`, `all` and `getFirst`.
It runs one query for all comments, not one query per comment.

### `$getRelation`

Use it when you already have the model.

```dart
Comment? comment = await Comment().find(1);
await comment?.$getRelation('user');
print(comment?.user?.name);
```

Do not call it in a loop over many models. Use `preload` for a list.

### `related`

Use it when you need more conditions on the related row.

```dart
Comment? comment = await Comment().find(1);
User? activeUser = await comment
    ?.related<User>('user')
    ?.where('status', 'active')
    .getFirst();
```

It does not set `comment.user`.

### `eager`

Use it when every query of `Comment` should load the relation.

```dart
@BelongsTo(User, eager: true)
User? user;
```

You do not call `preload`.

The load runs this SQL:

```sql
SELECT * FROM "user"
  WHERE "user"."id" IN (@userid_p0, ...)
```

Each user is read once, also when it has many comments.
Comments of the same user get the same `User` object.

`reload()` and a preload set the relation fields again, also when there is no related row. See [Relationships](../index.md#relationships).

## Filter by it

`whereHas()` keeps the comments by a user that matches.
It does not load the users.

```dart
List<Comment> comments = await Comment().whereHas('user', (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('name', 'Ann');
}).get();
```

See [Query by relations](../relation-queries.md).

## Options

| Option | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `foreignKey` | `{related model}_id`, like `user_id` | The column in this table that points to the related model. |
| `localKey` | the primary key of the related model | The column in the related table that `foreignKey` points to. |
| `onQuery` | none | A static function that changes the query. |
| `eager` | `false` | Load the relation on every query. |

The default `foreignKey` uses the class name of the related model in snake_case.
`User` gives `user_id`, also when the table is `users`.
The [`belongsToKeyFromRelation` flag](../../index.md#orm-flags) takes it from the relation name (`author_id`). The model generator does not pass the relation name yet, so set `foreignKey` when it is not the class name.

### `foreignKey` and `localKey`

```dart
@BelongsTo(User, foreignKey: 'author_id', localKey: 'id')
User? author;
```

### `onQuery`

`onQuery` is a static function in the same model class.
It gets the query of the related model and returns it.

```dart
@DoxModel()
class Comment extends CommentGenerator {
  @Column()
  int? userId;

  @BelongsTo(User, onQuery: onlyActive)
  User? activeUser;

  static QueryBuilder<User> onlyActive(User q) {
    return q.where('status', 'active');
  }
}
```

## In JSON

- A relation with `eager: true` is always in `toJson()`.
- A relation loaded with `preload` is in `toJson()` of that query.
- The JSON key is the field name in snake_case: `user`.


---

# ManyToMany

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/database/model/relationship/many-to-many/

# ManyToMany

Use `ManyToMany` when rows on both sides can have many rows on the other side.

For example, an artist has many songs, and a song has many artists.

The link is kept in a third table, the pivot table.
It has one foreign key to each side.

## Tables

| Table | Columns |
|---|---|
| `artist` | `id`, `name` |
| `song` | `id`, `title` |
| `artist_song` (pivot) | `id`, `artist_id`, `song_id` |

A migration for the pivot table:

```dart
await schema.create('artist_song', (Table table) {
  table.id();
  table.foreignId('artist_id').constrained('artist').cascadeOnDelete();
  table.foreignId('song_id').constrained('song').cascadeOnDelete();
});
```

## Define it

Add a field with `@ManyToMany(...)` to each model that needs it.
The field type is a list of the related model. Start it as an empty list.

```dart title="lib/app/models/artist/artist.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

import '../song/song.model.dart';

part 'artist.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel()
class Artist extends ArtistGenerator {
  @Column()
  String? name;

  @ManyToMany(Song)
  List<Song> songs = <Song>[];
}
```

```dart title="lib/app/models/song/song.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

import '../artist/artist.model.dart';

part 'song.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel()
class Song extends SongGenerator {
  @Column()
  String? title;

  @ManyToMany(Artist)
  List<Artist> artists = <Artist>[];
}
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` after you add a relationship.

## Load it

The relation is not loaded by default. Load it in one of these ways.
Use the field name (`'songs'`) as the relation name.

### `preload`

Use it when you load the models with a query.

```dart
Artist? artist = await Artist().preload('songs').find(1);
print(artist?.songs.length);

List<Song> songs = await Song().preload('artists').get();
```

`preload` works with `find`, `get`, `all` and `getFirst`.
For a list of models, it runs one query for all of them.
A model without links gets an empty list.

### `$getRelation`

Use it when you already have the model.

```dart
Artist? artist = await Artist().find(1);
await artist?.$getRelation('songs');
print(artist?.songs.length);
```

### `related`

Use it when you need more conditions on the related rows.

```dart
Artist? artist = await Artist().find(1);
List<Song> songs = await artist
        ?.related<Song>('songs')
        ?.orderBy('song.title')
        .get() ??
    <Song>[];
```

It does not set `artist.songs`.
The query joins the pivot table, so write `table.column` for column names.

### `eager`

Use it when every query of `Artist` should load the relation.

```dart
@ManyToMany(Song, eager: true)
List<Song> songs = <Song>[];
```

You do not call `preload`.
Do not set `eager: true` on both sides. Each side would load the other side again and again.

The load runs this SQL:

```sql
SELECT "song".*, "artist_song"."artist_id" as "_owner_id" FROM "song"
  LEFT JOIN "artist_song" on "artist_song"."song_id" = "song"."id"
  WHERE "artist_song"."artist_id" IN (@artist_songartist_id_p0, ...)
```

With `withPivot` or `withTimestamps`, it also selects those pivot columns, like `"artist_song"."role" as "_pivot_role"`.

`reload()` and a preload set the relation fields again, also when there is no related row. See [Relationships](../index.md#relationships).

## Read pivot columns

The pivot table can have more columns, like a `role`.
List them in `withPivot`.
Read them with `pivot` on each related model.

```dart
@ManyToMany(Song, withPivot: <String>['role'])
List<Song> songs = <Song>[];
```

```dart
Artist? artist = await Artist().preload('songs').find(1);
for (Song song in artist!.songs) {
  print(song.pivot['role']);
}
```

- `pivot` has the two pivot keys, like `artist_id` and `song_id`, when the rows are loaded by the relation:
  with `preload`, `$getRelation`, `eager` or `related('songs')!.get()`.
  They are read from the loaded rows, so a relation without `withPivot` runs no extra SQL.
- `withTimestamps: true` adds `created_at` and `updated_at` to `pivot`.
  `attach()`, `sync()` and `toggle()` then set them.
  `updateExistingPivot()` sets `updated_at`.
  The pivot table needs both columns (`table.timestamps()`).
- A model that was not loaded by a ManyToMany relation has an empty `pivot`.
- `toJson()` of a model loaded by a ManyToMany relation has a `pivot` key with these values. Dates are ISO text. Put `'pivot'` in `hidden` to leave it out. A model with its own `pivot` column keeps its column value in that key. Then the pivot values are only in the `pivot` getter in Dart, not in `toJson()`.

## Change the links

These methods add and remove rows in the pivot table.
The first argument is the relation name, like `'songs'`.
Save the model first. A model without an id throws a `StateError`.

The ids can be:

- one id: `1`
- a model: `song`
- a list of ids or models: `[1, 2, song]`
- a map of `id => pivot values`: `{1: {'role': 'singer'}, 2: {}}`

`null` means no ids. So `attach('songs', null)` and `detach('songs', null)` change nothing, and `sync('songs', null)` deletes every link, like `sync('songs', [])`.
Ids match with one rule:

- Two texts only match when the text is the same.
  So on a text key column, `'007'` and `'7'` are two ids.
  The ORM does not know the type of the key column, so `attach('songs', ['1', '01'])` adds two rows.
- When one id is a number (`int` or `double`), Dart reads the other one as a number.
  It trims the text, drops a `.0` end, and tries `int.tryParse` (`' 1'`, `'+1'`, `'01'`, `'1.0'`), then `double.tryParse` (`'1.'`, `'1e0'`).
  They match when the two numbers are the same.
  Rows of a number key column come back as numbers, so `sync('songs', ['01'])` keeps the row of song `1`.
- This is only how Dart matches ids. The databases read some texts in other ways.
  For example, `'0x1'` is `1` in Dart and on Postgres, `0` on MariaDB, and an error on MySQL.
  Postgres throws for `'1.0'`, `'1.'` and `'1e0'` on an integer column.
- A given text that only reads as a number at or past ±2^53, like `'1e20'` or `'9007199254740993.'`, is not exact.
  It throws an `ArgumentError` when it is matched to a number.
  `sync` checks every id before its first write.
- A stored value never throws. A value in the table that can not be read exactly does not match a number.
  So a long digit text in a text key column does not stop `sync`.
- A bool id is `1` or `0`, like the databases read it. So `sync('songs', true)` keeps the row of song `1`.
- A `BigInt` id is an `int` when it fits, else it throws an `ArgumentError`. Any other id type that is not an `int`, a `String`, a `bool`, a `double` or a model throws an `ArgumentError`.
- Each id finds its own stored row when it can. A row with the same text wins, so on a text key `1` finds `'1'`, not `'01'`.
  A stored row is matched once, so on a number key `toggle('songs', ['1', '01'])` detaches song `1` once.
- `detach` and `updateExistingPivot` send every given id.
  So on a text key, `detach('songs', [1, '01'])` deletes both rows.
- `sync` deletes a stored row only when none of the given ids matches it.
  So on a text key, `sync('songs', [1, '01'])` keeps the rows `'1'` and `'01'`.
- A new row is added once for ids that are the same by this rule, and the first id wins.
  So on a number key `attach('songs', [1, '01'])` adds one row. On a text key it adds only the row `1`.
- A whole double within ±2^53, like `2.0`, is sent as the int `2`.
  Any other double, like `1.5`, NaN, infinity or `1e20`, throws an `ArgumentError`.
- Text ids are sent to the database as they are.

A `null` id or a model that is not saved is skipped by `attach`, `detach`, `toggle`, `syncWithoutDetaching` and `updateExistingPivot`.
`sync` throws an `ArgumentError` for one, before it changes anything, because it would delete every other link.
Each id is used once: `[1, 1, '1']` adds one row.

A text key column can compare text without case.
This is the default in MySQL and MariaDB, and in SQLite with `COLLATE NOCASE`.
`COLLATE NOCASE` ignores case only. MariaDB can also ignore end spaces.
Dart does not know that. So `sync` and `toggle` also ask the database about each text id that Dart did not match.
Dox asks the database about all of these ids in one query (one query per 100 ids), with `WHERE key = id` for each id.
When it finds a stored row, that row counts as a match. With a stored `'ABC'`:

- `sync('songs', ['abc'])` keeps the row `'ABC'`. It adds no row and deletes nothing.
- `toggle('songs', ['abc'])` detaches the row `'ABC'`. It adds no row.
- The delete never removes a row that the database sees as a kept id.
- `detached` has only the ids whose row is really gone.

### `attach`

Adds a pivot row for each id.
The third argument has the pivot values for every new row.

```dart
await artist.attach('songs', 1);
await artist.attach('songs', <int>[2, 3], <String, dynamic>{'role': 'singer'});
await artist.attach('songs', <int, Map<String, dynamic>>{
  4: <String, dynamic>{'role': 'writer'},
});
```

`attach` does not check for a row that is already there.
Use `sync` or `syncWithoutDetaching` when the row may be there.

### `detach`

Deletes the pivot rows of the ids.
With no ids argument, it deletes every pivot row of the model.
`detach('songs', null)` deletes nothing.
It returns how many rows it deleted.
The songs stay in the `song` table.

```dart
await artist.detach('songs', <int>[1, 2]);
await artist.detach('songs');
```

### `sync`

Makes the pivot rows match the ids.

- It adds a row for each new id.
- It deletes the rows of the ids that are not in the list.
- It sets the pivot values of the rows that are already there, when a value changed. `updated` has those ids.

It returns a `PivotSyncResult` with the ids of each change.
A number id is an `int` in the result, also when you gave `'3'`.
A text that is not the plain text of an int, like `'03'` or `'007'`, stays text.

```dart
PivotSyncResult result = await artist.sync('songs', <int>[1, 2, 3]);
print(result.attached); // ids that got a new row
print(result.detached); // ids whose row was deleted
print(result.updated);  // ids whose pivot values changed
```

`syncWithoutDetaching` does the same, but it does not delete rows.

```dart
await artist.syncWithoutDetaching('songs', <int>[4]);
```

### `toggle`

Adds a row for each id that has none.
Deletes the row of each id that has one.
It returns a `PivotSyncResult` with `attached` and `detached`.

```dart
await artist.toggle('songs', <int>[1, 2]);
```

### `updateExistingPivot`

Sets pivot values on the rows of one id or a list of ids.
It returns how many rows changed.

```dart
await artist.updateExistingPivot('songs', 1, <String, dynamic>{'role': 'writer'});
```

## Filter by it

`whereHas()` keeps the artists that have a song.
It checks the pivot table `artist_song` for you.
It does not load the songs.

```dart
List<Artist> artists = await Artist().whereHas('songs', (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('title', 'Yesterday');
}).get();

List<Artist> noSongs = await Artist().whereDoesntHave('songs').get();
```

See [Query by relations](../relation-queries.md).

## Options

The examples are for `@ManyToMany(Song)` in the `Artist` model.

| Option | Default | Example value | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pivotTable` | the two model names in A-Z order, joined with `_` | `artist_song` | The pivot table. |
| `pivotForeignKey` | `{this model}_id` | `artist_id` | The pivot column that points to this model. |
| `pivotRelatedForeignKey` | `{related model}_id` | `song_id` | The pivot column that points to the related model. |
| `localKey` | the primary key of this model | `id` | The column in `artist` that `pivotForeignKey` points to. |
| `relatedKey` | the primary key of the related model | `id` | The column in `song` that `pivotRelatedForeignKey` points to. |
| `withPivot` | none | `['role']` | Extra pivot columns to read. See [Read pivot columns](#read-pivot-columns). |
| `withTimestamps` | `false` | `true` | Read and set `created_at` and `updated_at` in the pivot table. |
| `onQuery` | none | | A static function that changes the query. |
| `eager` | `false` | | Load the relation on every query. |

The defaults use the class names in snake_case, not the table names.
So `@DoxModel(table: 'artists')` does not change them.

- `Artist` and `Song` give `artist_song`.
- `Blog` and `Category` give `blog_category`.
- `BlogPost` and `Tag` give `blog_post_tag`.

### Set all keys

```dart
@ManyToMany(
  Song,
  pivotTable: 'artist_song',
  pivotForeignKey: 'artist_id',
  pivotRelatedForeignKey: 'song_id',
  localKey: 'id',
  relatedKey: 'id',
)
List<Song> songs = <Song>[];
```

### `onQuery`

`onQuery` is a static function in the same model class.
It gets the query of the related model and returns it.

```dart
@DoxModel()
class Artist extends ArtistGenerator {
  @ManyToMany(Song, onQuery: onlyPublished)
  List<Song> songs = <Song>[];

  static QueryBuilder<Song> onlyPublished(Song q) {
    return q.where('song.status', 'published');
  }
}
```

## In JSON

- A relation with `eager: true` is always in `toJson()`.
- A relation loaded with `preload` is in `toJson()` of that query.
- The JSON key is the field name in snake_case: `songs`.


---

# HasManyThrough

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/database/model/relationship/through/

# HasManyThrough

Use `HasManyThrough` to read rows that are two steps away.
A model in the middle links the two ends.
`HasOneThrough` is the same, but it gives one row.

For example, a country has many users, and a user has many posts.
A country has many posts through its users.

## Tables

| Table | Columns |
|---|---|
| `country` | `id`, `name` |
| `user` | `id`, `country_id` |
| `post` | `id`, `user_id`, `title` |

## Define it

Add the field to the first model.
The `through` option is the model in the middle.

```dart title="lib/app/models/country/country.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

import '../post/post.model.dart';
import '../user/user.model.dart';

part 'country.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel()
class Country extends CountryGenerator {
  @Column()
  String? name;

  @HasManyThrough(Post, through: User)
  List<Post> posts = <Post>[];

  @HasOneThrough(Post, through: User, onQuery: newest)
  Post? latestPost;

  static Model<Post> newest(Post q) {
    q.orderBy('post.id');
    return q;
  }
}
```

With `HasOneThrough`, when several rows match, the last row of the query wins.
So `newest` orders by `post.id` from low to high, and the highest id is the last row.

Run `dart run build_runner build` after you add a relationship.

## Load it

It loads like the other relations.

```dart
Country? country = await Country().preload('posts').find(1);
print(country?.posts.length);

List<Country> countries = await Country().withCount('posts').get();
List<Country> active = await Country().whereHas('posts').get();
```

`preload` runs one query for all countries.
`withCount`, `whereHas`, `whereDoesntHave` and `has` work too.
See [Counting relations](../counting-relations.md) and [Query by relations](../relation-queries.md).

Rows that are soft deleted are left out, in the middle table and in the far table.

## Options

| Option | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `foreignKey` | `{this model}_id`, like `country_id` | The column in the middle table that points to this model. |
| `localKey` | the primary key of this model | The column in this table that `foreignKey` points to. |
| `throughForeignKey` | `{middle model}_id`, like `user_id` | The column in the far table that points to the middle model. |
| `throughLocalKey` | the primary key of the middle model | The column in the middle table that `throughForeignKey` points to. |
| `onQuery` | none | A static function that changes the query. |
| `eager` | `false` | Load the relation on every query. |

```dart
@HasManyThrough(
  Post,
  through: User,
  foreignKey: 'home_country_id', // on user, points to the country
  localKey: 'id', // on country
  throughForeignKey: 'author_id', // on post, points to the user
  throughLocalKey: 'id', // on user
)
List<Post> posts = <Post>[];
```

## Write the table in a column name

The query joins the two tables.
So in `onQuery` and in a `whereHas` callback, write the table in front of the column.

```dart
List<Country> countries = await Country().whereHas('posts', (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('post.title', 'Hello');
}).get();
```

A column without the table, like `title`, can be in both tables.


---

# Polymorphic

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/database/model/relationship/polymorphic/

# Polymorphic

Use a polymorphic relation when one model can belong to more than one other model.

For example, a comment can belong to a photo or to a video.
The `comment` table does not have a `photo_id` and a `video_id`.
It has two columns:

- `commentable_id`: the id of the photo or the video.
- `commentable_type`: the type, like `photo` or `video`.

`commentable` is the morph name. You pick it.

## Tables

| Table | Columns |
|---|---|
| `photo` | `id`, `title` |
| `video` | `id`, `title` |
| `comment` | `id`, `body`, `commentable_id`, `commentable_type` |

`morphs()` adds both columns and an index:

```dart
await schema.create('comment', (Table table) {
  table.id();
  table.string('body');
  table.morphs('commentable');
  table.timestamps();
});
```

## The morph map

The morph map gives each model a type name.
The type name is the value in the `commentable_type` column.

Set it in the `setup()` of a [provider](../../../digging-deeper/providers.md).
Dox runs providers in every isolate, before the first request.
The map is kept per isolate, so setting it only in `main()` is not enough.
Then the other isolates store the class name, and `@MorphTo` throws there.

```dart
class MorphMapProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Model.morphMap(<String, Model<dynamic> Function()>{
      'photo': Photo.new,
      'video': Video.new,
    });
  }
}
```

A queue worker or a CLI command that reads these relations must call it too.

- `@MorphTo` needs it. It reads the type and makes the model from the map.
- Without a map, `@MorphMany` and `@MorphOne` store the class name, like `Photo`.
- Use a morph map in production. The class name changes when you rename the class, or when you build with `--obfuscate`. Then the old rows do not match.
- Do not change a type name later. The rows in the table keep the old name.
- `Model.morphMap(map, merge: false)` removes the names you set before.

Two helpers read the map:

```dart
String type = Model.morphTypeOf(Photo()); // 'photo'
Model<dynamic> model = Model.morphModel('video'); // a new Video()
```

## Define it

### `@MorphMany`

A photo has many comments.
The second argument is the morph name.

```dart title="lib/app/models/photo/photo.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

import '../comment/comment.model.dart';

part 'photo.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel()
class Photo extends PhotoGenerator {
  @Column()
  String? title;

  @MorphMany(Comment, 'commentable')
  List<Comment> comments = <Comment>[];
}
```

### `@MorphOne`

A photo has one cover image.
It works like `@MorphMany`, but the field is one model.

```dart
@MorphOne(Image, 'imageable')
Image? cover;
```

When there are many rows, it keeps the last row the query returns.
Add an `orderBy` in `onQuery` to pick the row, like with [HasOne](has-one.md).

### `@MorphTo`

A comment belongs to a photo or a video.
The field type is `Model<dynamic>?`.
The morph name is the field name in snake_case: `commentable`.
The `commentable_id` and `commentable_type` columns must be `@Column` fields, or the relation is always `null`.

```dart title="lib/app/models/comment/comment.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

part 'comment.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel()
class Comment extends CommentGenerator {
  @Column()
  String? body;

  @Column()
  int? commentableId;

  @Column()
  String? commentableType;

  @MorphTo()
  Model<dynamic>? commentable;
}
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` after you add a relationship.

## Save a row

There is no `associate()`. Set the two columns yourself.
Use `Model.morphTypeOf()` for the type, so it is the same as the morph map.

```dart
Comment comment = Comment()
  ..body = 'Nice'
  ..commentableId = photo.id
  ..commentableType = Model.morphTypeOf(photo);
await comment.save();
```

## Load it

Load it like the other relations: `preload`, `$getRelation`, `related` or `eager`.

```dart
Photo? photo = await Photo().preload('comments').find(1);
print(photo?.comments.length);

List<Comment> comments = await Comment().preload('commentable').get();
for (Comment c in comments) {
  if (c.commentable is Photo) {
    print((c.commentable as Photo).title);
  }
}
```

- `@MorphMany` and `@MorphOne` run one query for all models.
  It has `where commentable_type = 'photo'`.
- `@MorphTo` runs one query for each type in the list.
  A comment with a type that is not in the morph map throws a `StateError`.
  A comment with no type, or an empty type `''`, gets `null`.
- `related<Photo>('commentable')` on one comment gives the query of its photo.

`reload()` and a preload set the relation fields again, also when there is no related row. See [Relationships](../index.md#relationships).

## Filter by it

`whereHas()`, `whereDoesntHave()` and `withCount()` work with `@MorphMany` and `@MorphOne`.

```dart
List<Photo> photos = await Photo().whereHas('comments').get();
List<Video> videos = await Video().withCount('comments').get();
```

They do not work with `@MorphTo`. It throws an `UnsupportedError`.

## Options

### `@MorphMany` and `@MorphOne`

The examples are for `@MorphMany(Comment, 'commentable')` in the `Photo` model.

| Option | Default | Example value | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` (2nd argument) | | `commentable` | The morph name. |
| `typeColumn` | `{name}_type` | `commentable_type` | The type column in `comment`. |
| `idColumn` | `{name}_id` | `commentable_id` | The id column in `comment`. |
| `localKey` | the primary key of this model | `id` | The column in `photo` that `idColumn` points to. |
| `onQuery` | none | | A static function that changes the query. |
| `eager` | `false` | | Load the relation on every query. |

### `@MorphTo`

| Option | Default | Example value | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | the field name in snake_case | `commentable` | The morph name. |
| `typeColumn` | `{name}_type` | `commentable_type` | The type column in this table. |
| `idColumn` | `{name}_id` | `commentable_id` | The id column in this table. |
| `ownerKey` | the primary key of the related model | `id` | The column in the related table that `idColumn` points to. |
| `onQuery` | none | | A static function that changes the query of each type. It runs for every type, so it takes and returns `Model<dynamic>`. |
| `eager` | `false` | | Load the relation on every query. |

## In JSON

- A relation with `eager: true` is always in `toJson()`.
- A relation loaded with `preload` is in `toJson()` of that query.
- The JSON key is the field name in snake_case: `comments`, `commentable`.


---

# Authentication

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/security/authentication/

# Authentication

This page shows how to let users register, log in and log out, and how to protect routes.
Follow it from the top. At the end of each way, your app has working auth.

`dox_auth` gives you:

- a password login against your user table (bcrypt hashes)
- three ways to keep a user logged in: access tokens, JWT tokens and sessions
- `AuthMiddleware`, which protects a route and loads the user
- `req.auth`, the logged-in user in your controller
- a login throttle, and tools to revoke and renew tokens

`dox_auth` has no password reset, no email check, no "remember me" and no two-step login (2FA).
Your app builds these. The tools on this page help, for example the [two-step login recipe](#change-the-abilities-of-a-token).
Who may do what (roles, "may this user edit this post") is on the [Authorization](authorization.md) page.

## Which one do I need?

| Your app | Use | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| An API for a mobile app, a front end on another domain, or scripts | [Access tokens](#access-tokens) | You can revoke each token at any time, give it abilities, and renew it. The token is checked in a database table. |
| An API where other services must check the token with a key | [JWT](#jwt-tokens) | The token is signed. There is no token table. It works until it expires, unless you turn on revocation. |
| Web pages served by this app (forms, Inertia) | [Session](#session-login-for-web-pages) | The browser sends the session cookie. The client does nothing. |
| Web pages and an API in one app | [More than one guard](#more-than-one-guard) | A session guard for the pages, a token guard for the API. |

Not sure? For an API, use access tokens.

Two words used on this page:

- A **guard** is a named way to log in, like `api` or `web`. It says how the login is kept (access token, JWT or session) and which model holds the users.
- An **ability** is a name like `posts:read` on an access token. It says what the token may do.

## Set it up

These steps start from a new app made with `dox create my_app`.
It has a SQLite database, a `User` model and a `users` table with `name`, `email` and `password` columns.
Do these steps once, then follow one of the ways below.

### Install

```bash
dox add auth
```

It needs the ORM (`dox add orm`) and a `User` model in `lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart` (`dox make:model User -m`) first. A new app has both.
It does steps 1, 4 and 5 below.
It also writes the token table migration of [Access tokens](#access-tokens), so you do not need `dox auth:tokens-table` there. Run `dox migrate`.
Then do steps 2, 3 and 6 yourself.
It never overwrites a file, so it is safe to run twice.

### Set it up by hand

Do all the steps below when you do not use `dox add auth`.

### 1. Add the package

A new app does not have `dox_auth`. Add it:

```bash
dart pub add dox_auth
```

### 2. Check the user model

The password hash must never leave the server. Put it in `hidden`, so `toJson()` leaves it out.
The model of a new app already does this:

```dart title="lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

part 'user.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel(table: 'users', softDelete: true)
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @override
  List<String> get fillable => <String>['name', 'email', 'password'];

  @override
  List<String> get hidden => <String>['password'];

  @Column()
  String? name;

  @Column()
  String? email;

  @Column()
  String? password;
}
```

### 3. Add the input checks

These DTOs check the body of the register and login requests. Bad input gets `422`, and the controller does not run. See [Validation](../the-basic/validation.md).

```dart title="lib/app/dtos/auth/auth.dto.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart' hide Schema;

part 'auth.dto.g.dart';

/// The body of a register request.
@Dto()
class RegisterUser {
  @Trim()
  @Length(min: 1, max: 255)
  final String name;

  @Trim()
  @Lowercase()
  @Email()
  @Unique('users', column: 'email')
  final String email;

  /// bcrypt reads at most 72 bytes
  @Length(min: 8, max: 72)
  final String password;

  const RegisterUser({
    required this.name,
    required this.email,
    required this.password,
  });

  static const DtoSchema<RegisterUser> schema = $RegisterUserDto;
}

/// The body of a login request.
@Dto()
class LoginUser {
  @Trim()
  @Lowercase()
  @Email()
  final String email;

  final String password;

  const LoginUser({required this.email, required this.password});

  static const DtoSchema<LoginUser> schema = $LoginUserDto;
}
```

### 4. Add the auth config

The config lists the guards. Each guard has a driver (how the login is kept) and an `AuthProvider` (which model holds the users).
This config has one guard, `api`, with access tokens. The [JWT](#jwt-tokens) and [session](#session-login-for-web-pages) ways give their own version of this file.

```dart title="lib/config/auth.dart"
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

AuthConfig authConfig = AuthConfig(
  defaultGuard: 'api',
  guards: <String, AuthGuard>{
    'api': AuthGuard(
      driver: AccessTokenAuthDriver(expiresIn: const Duration(days: 30)),
      provider: AuthProvider(model: () => User()),
    ),
  },
);
```

`Auth()` and `AuthMiddleware()` use `defaultGuard`. All options are in the [reference](#reference).

### 5. Load the config when the app starts

This class gives the config to `dox_auth` when the app starts.
It is a `DoxProvider` (a class that Dox runs at startup). It is not the `AuthProvider` of step 4.

```dart title="lib/providers/auth_provider.dart"
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/auth.dart';

class AppAuthProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Auth.initialize(authConfig);
  }
}
```

You do not register it by hand. Dox finds every `DoxProvider`.

### 6. Run the code generator

It writes the DTO code and adds `AppAuthProvider` to `lib/generated/container.g.dart`.

```bash
dart run build_runner build
dart analyze
```

Do not start `dox s` yet. The first way below makes a migration first.

## Access tokens

An access token is an API token that you can revoke at any time.
It is like an AdonisJS access token.

- A token looks like `oat_12.<secret>`. `12` is the row id in the token table.
- The table keeps only a SHA-256 hash of the secret. You see the plain token once, when you make it.
- A token works until it expires or you revoke it.
- Each token has abilities. The default is `*` (all abilities).

The [setup](#set-it-up) above already added the `api` guard with `AccessTokenAuthDriver`.

### 1. Add the token table

```bash
dox auth:tokens-table --users-table=users
dox migrate
```

`dox auth:tokens-table` writes a migration in `db/migration`. `dox migrate` adds it to `db/migration/migrations.dart`, runs it, and makes the `auth_access_tokens` table.

The migration it writes looks like this:

```dart
// ignore_for_file: file_names
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';

/// The auth_access_tokens table of dox_auth.
class CreateAccessTokensTable extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await AccessTokenTables.up(schema, usersTable: 'users');
  }

  @override
  Future<void> down(Schema schema) async {
    await AccessTokenTables.down(schema);
  }
}
```

`--users-table=users` adds a foreign key with cascade delete. So when you delete a user, the tokens of the user are deleted too.
The command does not overwrite: when a `create_access_tokens_table` migration is already there, it prints so and stops.
For users with uuid or text ids, see [Users with uuid or text ids](#users-with-uuid-or-text-ids). All flags are in the [reference](#accesstokentablesup-and-dox-authtokens-table).

### 2. Write the auth controller

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/auth.controller.dart"
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/dtos/auth/auth.dto.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

@Inject()
class AuthController {
  /// POST /api/auth/register: make an account and give a token.
  Future<DoxResponse> register(RegisterUser body) async {
    User user = User()
      ..name = body.name
      ..email = body.email
      ..password = await Hash.makeAsync(body.password);
    await user.save();

    AccessToken token = await Auth().createAccessToken(user, name: 'login');
    return response(<String, dynamic>{
      'token': token.value,
      'user': user,
    }).statusCode(201);
  }

  /// POST /api/auth/login: check the email and password, give a token.
  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> login(DoxRequest req, LoginUser body) async {
    Auth auth = Auth(ip: req.ip());
    String? token = await auth.attempt(<String, dynamic>{
      'email': body.email,
      'password': body.password,
    });
    if (token == null) {
      throw UnAuthorizedException(message: 'Wrong email or password');
    }
    return <String, dynamic>{'token': token, 'user': auth.user<User>()};
  }

  /// GET /api/auth/me: the logged-in user.
  User? me(DoxRequest req) {
    return req.auth?.user<User>();
  }

  /// POST /api/auth/logout: the token of this request stops working.
  Future<Map<String, bool>> logout(DoxRequest req) async {
    await (req.auth as Auth).revokeToken(req);
    return <String, bool>{'logged_out': true};
  }
}
```

- `Hash.makeAsync` runs bcrypt in another isolate, so it does not block the server. See [Hashing](hashing.md).
- `attempt` finds the user by email and checks the password. It gives a new token with all abilities (`*`), or `null`. It runs bcrypt in another isolate too.
- `Auth(ip: req.ip())` gives the client ip to the [login throttle](#login-throttle).

### 3. Add the routes

`AuthMiddleware()` protects a route. A request with no good token stops with `401`.
A [rate limit](rate-limiting.md) on register and login slows down password guessing.

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/controllers/api.controller.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/controllers/auth.controller.dart';

class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/ping', (ApiController c) => c.pong);

    // for guests
    Route.post('/auth/register', <dynamic>[
      RateLimit(max: 5, name: 'register'),
      (AuthController c) => c.register,
    ]);
    Route.post('/auth/login', <dynamic>[
      RateLimit(max: 5, name: 'login'),
      (AuthController c) => c.login,
    ]);

    // for logged-in users
    Route.get('/auth/me', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(), (AuthController c) => c.me]);
    Route.post('/auth/logout', <dynamic>[
      AuthMiddleware(),
      (AuthController c) => c.logout,
    ]);
  }
}
```

Run the generator again, then start the app:

```bash
dart run build_runner build
dox s
```

### 4. Try it

The client sends the token in the `Authorization` header: `Authorization: Bearer oat_12.<secret>`.
The word `Bearer` can be in any case.
Run these in a second terminal. Where a step says "keep it in", copy the token from the answer into a shell variable.

```bash
# make an account
curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/auth/register -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Ada","email":"ada@example.com","password":"secret-pass"}'
# 201 {"token":"oat_1.c79C...","user":{"id":1,"name":"Ada","email":"ada@example.com",...}}

# a wrong password
curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"ada@example.com","password":"wrong-pass"}'
# 401 {"code":"unauthorized","message":"Wrong email or password"}

# log in, and keep the token in TOKEN
curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"ada@example.com","password":"secret-pass"}'
# 200 {"token":"oat_2.OTAG...","user":{"id":1,...}}
TOKEN='oat_2.OTAG...'

curl localhost:3000/api/auth/me -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# 200 {"id":1,"name":"Ada","email":"ada@example.com",...}

curl localhost:3000/api/auth/me
# 401 {"code":"unauthorized","message":"Authentication failed"}

# log out
curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/auth/logout -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# 200 {"logged_out":true}
curl localhost:3000/api/auth/me -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# 401 {"code":"unauthorized","message":"Authentication failed"}
```

The password is never in an answer, because it is in `hidden`.
The ids (`oat_1`, `oat_2`, ...) count up in your table, so yours may differ.

Your app has a working login. The next part adds script tokens, abilities and token renewal. You can skip it until you need it.

## More with access tokens

### Abilities

`createAccessToken(user, abilities: <String>['posts:read'])` gives a token that can do only these things.
The default is `<String>['*']`: all abilities. `attempt` always gives `*`.

Check an ability in the controller, after `AuthMiddleware`:

```dart
Auth auth = req.auth as Auth;
if (!auth.tokenCan('posts:write')) {
  throw ForbiddenHttpException();
}
auth.currentAccessToken; // the AccessToken of this request
```

- `tokenCan` is `true` when the token has the ability, or `*`.
- `tokenCan` is `false` when there is no access token. So a session or JWT login never passes it.
- A route with no `tokenCan` check takes every good token, whatever its abilities. Check an ability on each route that needs one.
- A token without the ability gets `403`. A request with no good token gets `401` from `AuthMiddleware`.

### Script tokens

Users can make extra tokens, for example for a script that only reads posts.
This controller lists, makes and revokes them. Each action needs the `tokens:manage` ability.
A login token has `*`, so it passes. A script token does not, so a leaked script token can not make new tokens.

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/token.controller.dart"
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

@Inject()
class TokenController {
  /// GET /api/tokens: all tokens of the user, newest first.
  Future<List<AccessToken>> index(DoxRequest req) async {
    Auth auth = _manager(req);
    return auth.accessTokens(auth.user<User>()!);
  }

  /// POST /api/tokens: a token for a script. It can only read posts.
  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> store(DoxRequest req) async {
    Auth auth = _manager(req);
    AccessToken token = await auth.createAccessToken(
      auth.user<User>()!,
      name: 'script',
      abilities: <String>['posts:read'],
      expiresIn: const Duration(days: 90),
    );
    return <String, dynamic>{'token': token.value};
  }

  /// DELETE /api/tokens/{id}: revoke one token of the user.
  Future<Map<String, bool>> destroy(DoxRequest req, int id) async {
    Auth auth = _manager(req);
    if (!await auth.revokeAccessToken(auth.user<User>()!, id)) {
      throw NotFoundHttpException();
    }
    return <String, bool>{'revoked': true};
  }

  /// The Auth of the request, when its token may manage tokens.
  Auth _manager(DoxRequest req) {
    Auth auth = req.auth as Auth;
    if (!auth.tokenCan('tokens:manage')) {
      throw ForbiddenHttpException();
    }
    return auth;
  }
}
```

A route that needs the `posts:read` ability:

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/post.controller.dart"
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

@Inject()
class PostController {
  /// GET /api/posts: needs a token with the posts:read ability.
  List<String> index(DoxRequest req) {
    if (!(req.auth as Auth).tokenCan('posts:read')) {
      throw ForbiddenHttpException();
    }
    return <String>['Hello'];
  }
}
```

In `lib/routes/api.dart`, add the imports at the top:

```dart
import 'package:my_app/app/http/controllers/post.controller.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/controllers/token.controller.dart';
```

And add the routes at the end of `register()`:

```dart
Route.get('/tokens', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(), (TokenController c) => c.index]);
Route.post('/tokens', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(), (TokenController c) => c.store]);
Route.delete('/tokens/{id}', <dynamic>[
  AuthMiddleware(),
  (TokenController c) => c.destroy,
]);
Route.get('/posts', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(), (PostController c) => c.index]);
```

Run `dart run build_runner build`. `dox s` restarts by itself.

`/auth/me` and `/auth/logout` have no ability check, so a script token can call them too. That is fine: it sees its own user, and its logout revokes only itself.

Try it. Log in first and keep the token in `TOKEN`, like above.

```bash
# make a script token, and keep it in SCRIPT_TOKEN
curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/tokens -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# 200 {"token":"oat_4.pwwK..."}
SCRIPT_TOKEN='oat_4.pwwK...'

curl localhost:3000/api/posts -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCRIPT_TOKEN"
# 200 ["Hello"]

# the script token may not manage tokens
curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/tokens -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCRIPT_TOKEN"
# 403 {"code":"forbidden","message":"Forbidden"}

# list the tokens, then revoke the script token (id 4)
curl localhost:3000/api/tokens -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# 200 [{"id":4,"name":"script","type":"api","abilities":["posts:read"],...},...]
curl -X DELETE localhost:3000/api/tokens/4 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# 200 {"revoked":true}
curl localhost:3000/api/posts -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCRIPT_TOKEN"
# 401 {"code":"unauthorized","message":"Authentication failed"}
```

### List and revoke tokens

```dart
await Auth().accessTokens(user);           // all tokens of the user, newest first, expired ones too
await Auth().revokeAccessToken(user, id);  // false when the user has no token with this id
await Auth().revokeAllAccessTokens(user);  // all tokens of the user, eg. after a password change
await Auth().revokeToken(req);             // the token of this request (a logout)
await Auth().pruneExpiredAccessTokens();   // delete expired tokens, eg. from a scheduled job
```

- A revoked token is deleted from the table, so it stops working at once.
- `token.toJson()` has no hash and no plain token, so you can send it to the client. `GET /api/tokens` above does this.
- On the `Auth` of `AuthMiddleware`, `(req.auth as Auth).revokeToken(req)` uses the token that was already checked. It does not check it again.
- Expired tokens stay in the table until you call `pruneExpiredAccessTokens()`. Run it from a [scheduled task](../digging-deeper/scheduler.md).

### Rotate a token

Rotate a token to renew it before it expires.
`rotateAccessToken` makes a new token in place of an old one.
The new token has the same user, name and abilities as the old one.

Add this method to `AuthController`:

```dart
/// POST /api/auth/refresh: a new token in place of the token of this
/// request. The old token stops working at once.
Future<Map<String, dynamic>> refresh(DoxRequest req) async {
  Auth auth = req.auth as Auth;
  if (!auth.tokenCan('tokens:manage')) {
    throw ForbiddenHttpException();
  }
  AccessToken next = await auth.rotateAccessToken(auth.currentAccessToken!);
  return <String, dynamic>{
    'token': next.value,
    'expires_at': next.expiresAt?.toIso8601String(),
  };
}
```

And this route at the end of `register()` in `lib/routes/api.dart`:

```dart
Route.post('/auth/refresh', <dynamic>[
  AuthMiddleware(),
  (AuthController c) => c.refresh,
]);
```

Run `dart run build_runner build`. The `tokens:manage` check keeps a script token from renewing itself.

Try it. Log in first and keep the token in `TOKEN`.

```bash
curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/auth/refresh -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# 200 {"token":"oat_6.-qAk...","expires_at":"2026-12-11T04:43:15.701944Z"}
NEW_TOKEN='oat_6.-qAk...'

curl localhost:3000/api/auth/me -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# 401 {"code":"unauthorized","message":"Authentication failed"}
curl localhost:3000/api/auth/me -H "Authorization: Bearer $NEW_TOKEN"
# 200 {"id":1,"name":"Ada",...}
```

`grace` is how long the old token still works. The default is zero: the old token ends at once, like above.
You need a grace only when one client sends requests in parallel. Then a request that is on the way with the old token does not fail.
Keep it short, a few seconds: `rotateAccessToken(token, grace: const Duration(seconds: 10))`.
If the old token ends sooner than `grace`, it keeps its own end.

The rules:

- A token can be rotated only once. A second rotate of the same token throws an `UnAuthorizedException` (`401`, `The access token was already rotated.`). This is also true in the grace time. Nothing is made.
- A revoked or expired token is refused the same way: `401` with `The access token is revoked or does not exist.` or `The access token is expired.`
- When two rotates of one token run at the same time, only one works.
- It runs in one transaction. When it fails, nothing is changed.
- `expiresIn:` sets how long the new token works. `null` (the default) gives the `expiresIn` of the driver. When that is `null` too, the new token has no end.
- `name:` gives the new token another name. `null` keeps the old name.
- A token of another guard, or a negative `grace`, throws an `ArgumentError`.

Safety notes:

- A longer `grace` gives a stolen old token more time. In that time it works on every route, also the token routes, so it can make new tokens. Only rotate refuses it. Keep `grace` short, or zero.
- Each rotate gives a full new life. So a client that rotates again and again stays logged in forever. A rotated token has a new `createdAt` and no link to the first token. To set a limit, keep the first login time yourself. For example, save it in a column, or in the token name with `rotateAccessToken(token, name: ...)`. Or ask for the password again after some time.

Rotate needs the `rotated_at` column. A table made by `dox auth:tokens-table` has it.

#### A token table without `rotated_at`

A token table without the `rotated_at` column works for everything except rotate.
`rotateAccessToken` then throws a `StateError` that names the column:

```text
Bad state: The table 'auth_access_tokens' has no rotated_at column. rotate() needs it. Add it in a new migration: ...
```

To add the column:

1. Stop `dox s` if it runs. It runs new migrations when it restarts. It would run the new, still empty file, and then the column is never added.
2. Make a migration:

    ```bash
    dox make:migration add_rotated_at_to_auth_access_tokens
    ```

3. Paste this into the new file in `db/migration` (its name starts with the date and time):

    ```dart
    // ignore_for_file: file_names
    import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';

    class AddRotatedAtToAuthAccessTokens extends Migration {
      @override
      Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
        await schema.table('auth_access_tokens', (Table t) {
          t.dateTimeTz('rotated_at').nullable();
        });
      }

      @override
      Future<void> down(Schema schema) async {
        await schema.table('auth_access_tokens', (Table t) {
          t.dropColumn('rotated_at');
        });
      }
    }
    ```

4. Run `dox migrate`, then start `dox s` again.

## JWT tokens

A JWT is a signed token. The server keeps no list of tokens.
The token works until it expires, unless you turn on [revocation](#revoke-tokens).
The user is still loaded from the database on each request, by the id in the token.

Do the [setup](#set-it-up) first. This way needs no token table.

### 1. Change the guard

```dart title="lib/config/auth.dart"
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

AuthConfig authConfig = AuthConfig(
  defaultGuard: 'api',
  guards: <String, AuthGuard>{
    'api': AuthGuard(
      driver: JwtAuthDriver(
        secret: SecretKey(env.appKey),
        expiresIn: const Duration(days: 7),
        // the token holds only the user id
        minimalPayload: true,
        // lets logout stop a token before it expires
        revocation: true,
      ),
      provider: AuthProvider(model: () => User()),
    ),
  },
);
```

- `secret` signs the tokens. `APP_KEY` is fine: it must be at least 32 bytes. A new app has it in `.env`. `dox key:generate` makes a new one.
- `expiresIn` is how long a token works. The default is one hour.
- `minimalPayload` and `revocation` are off by default. See [Small tokens](#small-tokens) and [Revoke tokens](#revoke-tokens).

### 2. Write the auth controller

```dart title="lib/app/http/controllers/auth.controller.dart"
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/dtos/auth/auth.dto.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

@Inject()
class AuthController {
  /// POST /api/auth/register: make an account and give a token.
  Future<DoxResponse> register(RegisterUser body) async {
    User user = User()
      ..name = body.name
      ..email = body.email
      ..password = await Hash.makeAsync(body.password);
    await user.save();

    String? token = Auth().login(user);
    return response(<String, dynamic>{
      'token': token,
      'user': user,
    }).statusCode(201);
  }

  /// POST /api/auth/login: check the email and password, give a token.
  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> login(DoxRequest req, LoginUser body) async {
    Auth auth = Auth(ip: req.ip());
    String? token = await auth.attempt(<String, dynamic>{
      'email': body.email,
      'password': body.password,
    });
    if (token == null) {
      throw UnAuthorizedException(message: 'Wrong email or password');
    }
    return <String, dynamic>{'token': token, 'user': auth.user<User>()};
  }

  /// GET /api/auth/me: the logged-in user.
  User? me(DoxRequest req) {
    return req.auth?.user<User>();
  }

  /// POST /api/auth/logout: the token of this request stops working.
  Future<Map<String, bool>> logout(DoxRequest req) async {
    await Auth().revokeToken(req);
    return <String, bool>{'logged_out': true};
  }
}
```

`Auth().login(user)` gives a token with no password check. `attempt` checks the password first.

### 3. Add the routes

```dart title="lib/routes/api.dart"
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/controllers/api.controller.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/http/controllers/auth.controller.dart';

class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/ping', (ApiController c) => c.pong);

    Route.post('/auth/register', <dynamic>[
      RateLimit(max: 5, name: 'register'),
      (AuthController c) => c.register,
    ]);
    Route.post('/auth/login', <dynamic>[
      RateLimit(max: 5, name: 'login'),
      (AuthController c) => c.login,
    ]);
    Route.get('/auth/me', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(), (AuthController c) => c.me]);
    Route.post('/auth/logout', <dynamic>[
      AuthMiddleware(),
      (AuthController c) => c.logout,
    ]);
  }
}
```

Run `dart run build_runner build`, then `dox s`.

### 4. Try it

```bash
curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/auth/register -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Ada","email":"ada@example.com","password":"secret-pass"}'
# 201 {"token":"eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...","user":{"id":1,"name":"Ada",...}}

# log in, and keep the token in TOKEN
curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"ada@example.com","password":"secret-pass"}'
# 200 {"token":"eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...","user":{"id":1,"name":"Ada",...}}
TOKEN='eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...'

curl localhost:3000/api/auth/me -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# 200 {"id":1,"name":"Ada","email":"ada@example.com",...}

curl -X POST localhost:3000/api/auth/logout -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# 200 {"logged_out":true}

curl localhost:3000/api/auth/me -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# 401 {"code":"unauthorized","message":"Authentication failed"}
```

If Ada already has an account from another way, `register` answers `422`. Then just log in.
For a longer JWT walkthrough, see the [JWT auth guide](../guides/jwt-auth.md).

### Small tokens

By default, a token holds the user (`toJson()`, `hidden` fields left out), plus the `iat`, `exp` and `jti` claims.
Anyone can read a JWT payload. It is signed, not secret.
`minimalPayload: true` is the safer choice. The token then holds only the user id (the `sub` claim).
Load the user with `req.auth?.user<User>()`, not from the token.
A front end that reads user fields from the token must then get the user from the API.

### Revoke tokens

By default, a token works until it expires. There is no server list of tokens.
Turn on revocation to stop a token before it expires:

```dart
JwtAuthDriver(
  secret: SecretKey(env.appKey),
  revocation: true,
  revocationStore: 'auth',
)
```

Each token has a random id (the `jti` claim).
With revocation on, the driver keeps revoked tokens in the app cache (`Cache()` of `dox_core`).
A revoked token stops working at once:

```dart
await Auth().revokeToken(req);     // revoke the bearer token of this request (a logout)
await Auth().revokeAllTokens(id);  // revoke all tokens of a user, eg. after a password change or a ban
await Auth().forgetUser(id);       // drop the user from `userCacheTtl`, eg. after a ban
```

- With revocation off, these three methods throw a `StateError`. So no one thinks a token is revoked when it is not.
- With revocation off, a token check never reads the cache.
- A revoked token stays on the deny-list only until it expires.
- `revokeAllTokens` keeps tokens made after the call. A token made in the same second as the call also still works, because `iat` is in whole seconds.
- A token with no `jti` claim can not go on the deny-list, so `revokeToken` does nothing for it. `revokeAllTokens` still stops it when it has an `iat` claim. Tokens from `JwtAuthDriver` have one.
- The `revokeAllTokens` time comes from the server clock. Keep server clocks in sync (NTP).
- Give auth its own [cache store](../digging-deeper/cache.md), and never flush it. For example, a `redis` store with its own prefix. Pick it with `revocationStore`. With no `revocationStore`, the default app store is used. A flush of this store (`Cache().flush()`), or a `memory` store with `max_size` that drops old keys, brings revoked tokens back until they expire.
- Cost: a token check reads this store on every request, also with `userCacheTtl`. It is one `many()` call: one round trip on `redis` and `memory`. On the `file` store (the default) it is 2 or 3 file reads per request. Use `memory` for one isolate, or `redis` for many isolates or servers. A `memory` store is seen by one isolate only.
- When the store can not be read, the token is checked with only the signature and `exp`, and a warning is printed once. So a cache outage does not log everyone out. But revoked tokens work until the store is back.

### Change the JWT secret

New tokens are always signed with `secret`.
A token is checked with `secret` first, then with each old secret.
Only a wrong signature moves on to the next secret. An expired token fails at once.

- **The secret is `APP_KEY`** (`SecretKey(env.appKey)`): follow [Change the key](encryption.md#change-the-key-key-rotation). The old keys in `AppConfig.previousKeys` are used. You need nothing more.
- **A separate JWT secret**: give the old one to the driver.

    ```dart
    JwtAuthDriver(
      secret: SecretKey(env.jwtSecret),
      previousSecrets: <JWTKey>[SecretKey(env.jwtOldSecret)],
    )
    ```

Remove the old secret once `expiresIn` has passed. Then every old token has expired anyway.
Do not keep a leaked secret: anyone who has it can make tokens.
To log out everyone at once, change the secret and keep no old secrets.

## Session login for web pages

For web pages, keep the login in the session instead of a token.
The browser sends the session cookie, so the client does nothing.
It needs `SessionMiddleware` and `CsrfMiddleware`. See [Session](../the-basic/session.md) and [CSRF protection](csrf.md).

Do the [setup](#set-it-up) first. This way needs no token table.
