# App config

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/reference/app-config/

# App config

Every field of `AppConfig`, with its type, its default and what it does.

`AppConfig` is the one object you give to `Dox().initialize()`. It lives in `lib/config/app.dart`.

Source: `packages/dox-core/lib/interfaces/app_config.dart`.

## Server

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `appKey` | `String` | required | Encrypts cookies (`req.cookie()`, `DoxCookie`) and signs local storage URLs. It must be exactly 32 characters. The app stops at start when it is empty, has another length, or is a public sample key. When `APP_ENV` is `development`, `local`, `test` or `testing`, this is only a warning. Make one with `dox key:generate`. |
| `serverPort` | `int` | `3000` | The port the HTTP server listens on. When the env has no `APP_PORT` but has `PORT`, Dox listens on `PORT` instead (Cloud Run, Fly, Render and Heroku set it). |
| `host` | `String?` | `null`: `APP_HOST`, else all interfaces | The network interface to listen on, like `127.0.0.1`. `null` reads the env var `APP_HOST`. With neither, Dox listens on all interfaces, IPv6 and IPv4 (`::`). |
| `totalIsolate` | `int?` | `Platform.numberOfProcessors` | Isolates (threads) that serve HTTP, all on the same port. On Windows the native server runs on one isolate. |
| `compress` | `bool` | `false` | gzip responses (`HttpServer.autoCompress`). Rust gzips on its own thread, not on the isolate. It still costs CPU on every response. Let a proxy do it when you have one. |
| `maxBodySize` | `int` | `10 * 1024 * 1024` (10 MB) | Biggest JSON or urlencoded body in bytes. Bigger gets `413`. |
| `maxMultipartSize` | `int` | `100 * 1024 * 1024` (100 MB) | Biggest `multipart/form-data` body (file uploads) in bytes. Bigger gets `413`. |
| `bodyTimeout` | `Duration` | `Duration(seconds: 120)` | A client that sends no body bytes for this long gets `408`. A slow but steady upload is fine. Native server only. |
| `idleTimeout` | `Duration` | `Duration(seconds: 30)` | A keep-alive connection with no new request for this long is closed. A request head must also arrive in this time. Behind a load balancer, set it longer than the balancer's idle timeout. See [Behind a load balancer](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#behind-a-load-balancer). |
| `maxConnections` | `int?` | `null` (no limit) | The most connections one isolate holds open at once. Must be 1 or more. 0 or less throws an `ArgumentError` when the server starts. When it is full, new clients wait in the OS listen queue until a connection closes. WebSocket connections and connections that are still closing count too. The queue holds up to 1024 clients, and the OS can make it smaller (`somaxconn`; 128 by default on macOS). When the queue is full, new clients wait and then time out. On Linux each new client goes to one isolate (`SO_REUSEPORT`), so it can wait for a full isolate even when others have room. The whole app holds up to `maxConnections * totalIsolate`, so keep that below `ulimit -n`. Native server only. |
| `shutdownTimeout` | `Duration` | `Duration(seconds: 8)` | On `SIGTERM` or `SIGINT`, how long open requests may run before Dox closes them. Keep it below the kill timeout of your platform. See [Graceful shutdown](../digging-deeper/deployment.md#graceful-shutdown). |
| `trustedProxies` | `List<String>` | `[]` | IPs or CIDR ranges of reverse proxies. Only when the direct client is in this list does Dox read `X-Forwarded-For` for `req.ip()` and `X-Forwarded-Proto` for `req.scheme()`. `['*']` trusts any direct client, and takes the right-most `X-Forwarded-For` hop (the one the proxy added) as the client. |

## Routing and request handling

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `container` | `void Function(IocContainer)?` | `null` | Fills the container: `registerContainer` from `lib/generated/container.g.dart`. Every isolate runs it. It also gives the routers, providers and model binders. See [Dependency injection](../the-basic/dependency-injection.md). |
| `routers` | `List<Router>` | `[]` | Routers to register first, in this order. Every other `Router` class comes from `container`. |
| `globalMiddleware` | `List<dynamic>` | `[]` | Middleware that runs on every route. A function or an `IDoxMiddleware`. |
| `dtos` | `List<DtoSchema<Object>>` | `[]` | Every DTO of the app: `dtos` from `lib/generated/dtos.g.dart`. Dox finds the DTO of a controller parameter and of `req.validate<T>()` with it. |
| `validationMessages` | `MessageResolver?` | `null` (English messages) | Messages for validation errors, for example in other languages. |
| `responseHandler` | `ResponseHandlerInterface?` | `null` | A class with `DoxResponse handle(DoxResponse res)`. It sees every response before it is sent. |
| `exceptionHandler` | `ExceptionHandler` | `ExceptionHandler()` | Reports every unhandled error and turns it into a response. The default logs the error with `Logger.warn` and the stack with `Logger.danger`. See [Error handling](../the-basic/errors.md). |
| `htmlErrors` | `bool` | `false` | Sends an HTML error page to a request that does not want JSON (see `DoxRequest.expectsJson()`). In `development` or `local` the page also shows the error text and the stack. JSON clients, validation errors and `ExceptionHandler.render` answers do not change. See [An HTML error page](../the-basic/errors.md#an-html-error-page). |
| `errorPage` | `String Function(int status, Object error, StackTrace stack, bool debug)` | `defaultErrorPage` | Makes the HTML of the page. `debug` is `true` in `development` or `local`. Escape every value you put in the page. Used only with `htmlErrors`. |
| `providers` | `List<DoxProvider>` | `[]` | Providers to run first, in this order. Every other `DoxProvider` class comes from `container`. Dox runs them in every isolate at start. |
| `webSocketAllowedOrigins` | `List<String>?` | `null` (no check) | Turns on the `Origin` check for every `Route.websocket` route. Only pages of the same host and the listed sites, like `https://app.example.com`, can open a socket. Other origins get `403`. `[]` means the same host only. `allowedOrigins` on a route wins over this. With `null`, any website can open a socket with the cookies of the user, and Dox prints one warning to stderr at start. |

## Sub configs

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cors` | `CORSConfig` | `CORSConfig()` | CORS headers. See [CORSConfig](#corsconfig). |
| `logger` | `LoggerConfig` | `LoggerConfig()` | The `Logger` output. See [LoggerConfig](#loggerconfig). |
| `cache` | `CacheConfig` | `file` store in `storage/cache`, plus a `memory` store | Cache stores for `Cache()`. See [CacheConfig](#cacheconfig). |
| `session` | `SessionConfig` | `cookie` driver, cookie `dox_session`, 2 hours | Settings for `SessionMiddleware`. See [Session](../the-basic/session.md#config). |
| `openApi` | `OpenApiConfig` | `OpenApiConfig()` | `/docs`, `/openapi.json` and `/openapi.yaml`. See [OpenApiConfig](#openapiconfig). |
| `flags` | `CoreFlags` | `CoreFlags()` (all off) | Opt-in core behaviors. See [Core flags](#core-flags). |

## Core flags

`CoreFlags` turns on opt-in behaviors. Every flag is off by default.
Turn on the ones you want:

```dart
AppConfig(
  appKey: env.appKey,
  flags: const CoreFlags(onlyPresent: true, cookieDefaults: true),
);
```

`CoreFlags.all()` turns on every flag:

```dart
AppConfig(appKey: env.appKey, flags: const CoreFlags.all());
```

| Flag | When it is on |
| --- | --- |
| `laravelErrors` | A `422` body is `{"message": "...", "errors": {"field": ["..."]}}`, with all messages of each field. The `message` is the first error, plus `(and N more errors)`. The OpenAPI `ValidationError` schema has this shape too. Off: `{"field": "first message"}`. |
| `onlyPresent` | `req.only([...])` leaves out keys that are not in the input. So `model.update(req.only([...]))` does not write `null` for a field the client did not send. Off: a missing key is in the map with `null`. |
| `cookieDefaults` | A `DoxCookie` with no `path` gets `Path=/`, and one with no `sameSite` gets `SameSite=Lax`. A value you set wins. `SameSite.none` needs `secure: true`, or browsers drop the cookie. A cookie set before with no `Path` on a sub-path (like `/auth`) is not removed by an `expire()` that sends `Path=/`. Expire it with its old `path`. Off: no `Path` and no `SameSite`. |
| `hasKeyOnly` | `req.has('x')` is `true` when the key is there, with any value (also `''` or null), like `req.exists('x')`. Dot keys work. Off: `''` and null give `false`. |
| `htmlStrings` | A string from a controller is sent as `text/html`. A content type you set wins, also one a middleware set on the response. Only the preset `text/plain; charset=utf-8` is changed, so a string with that type set by hand is sent as HTML too. To keep plain text, return `response(text).contentType(ContentType.text)`. Escape user input in the string. Off: `text/plain`. |
| `replaceHeaders` | `res.header(k, v)` replaces a value of the header that a middleware put on the response before. `Vary` and `Set-Cookie` are lists, so they still get one more value. Off: it adds a second value. `res.header(k, v, replace: true)` or `replace: false` picks for one call. |
| `decryptServerError` | A `DecryptException` gives `500` with `{"code": "server_error", "message": "Server Error"}`, and the `ExceptionHandler` reports it. Off: `400` `decrypt_failed`, not reported. `req.cookie()` still gives `null` for a bad cookie. |
| `envExpand` | `.env` values can use `${OTHER}`, and a `"..."` value reads `\n`, `\t`, `\"`, `\\` and `\$`. Also set `Env.flags = flags;` at the top of `main()` in `bin/server.dart` and in your tests, because `.env` is read before `AppConfig` exists. See [Use one value in another](../digging-deeper/env.md#use-one-value-in-another). Off: values are read as written. |
| `cacheCopies` | `Cache().store('x')`, `.tag()` and `.tags()` give a new `Cache`, and the first one does not change. Off: they change the same object and give it back. |

Each isolate builds its own `AppConfig`, so every isolate has the same flags.
Dox reads a flag when the code runs, with `Dox().flags`.

The lock flag of the cache is in [`CacheConfig`](#cacheconfig): `CacheFlags`.

## CORSConfig

Source: `packages/dox-core/lib/interfaces/app_config.dart`. Headers are set in `packages/dox-core/lib/http/http_cors_handler.dart`.

A value can be a `String` (`'*'` or a comma list) or a `List<String>`. A `null` value sends no header.

| Field | Type | Default | Header |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `bool` | `true` | Send CORS headers. A route can override it with its own `cors` setting. |
| `origin` | `dynamic` | `null` | `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`. One origin, `'*'`, or a list. With a list, Dox sends back only the request origin if it is in the list. |
| `methods` | `dynamic` | `null` | `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` |
| `headers` | `dynamic` | `null` | `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` |
| `exposeHeaders` | `dynamic` | `null` | `Access-Control-Expose-Headers` |
| `credentials` | `bool?` | `null` | `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` |
| `maxAge` | `num?` | `null` | `Access-Control-Max-Age` in seconds |

!!! note
    With the default `CORSConfig()` every value is `null`. So `enabled: true` alone sends no header. Set `origin` at least.

## LoggerConfig

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `String` | `''` | Written as `logger.name` in each JSON log line. Left out when empty. |
| `enabled` | `bool` | `false` | Turn the `Logger` on. When it is `false`, `LogMiddleware(enabled: true)` does not turn request logs on. |
| `prettyPrint` | `bool` | `false` | `true` prints colored text. `false` prints one JSON object per line (for log services). The line has `timestamp`, `status`, `message` and `logger.name`. Keys of a `Map` you log are added at the top level. Other data goes under `payload`. `LogMiddleware` follows this setting too. |
| `level` | `String` | `'info'` | The lowest level to print: `debug`, `info`, `warn` or `error`. `Logger.success` counts as `info`. `Logger.danger` counts as `error`. An unknown value prints every line. |

## CacheConfig

Source: `packages/dox-cache/lib/src/cache_config.dart`. Option keys: `packages/dox-cache/lib/src/constants/cache_constants.dart`.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultStore` | `String` | required | The store `Cache()` uses when no store is named. |
| `stores` | `Map<String, Map<String, dynamic>>` | required | Store name to options. Each store needs a `driver` option. |
| `flags` | `CacheFlags` | `CacheFlags()` (all off) | Opt-in cache behaviors. See below. |

`CacheFlags` has one flag. `CacheFlags.all()` turns it on.

| Flag | When it is on |
| --- | --- |
| `lockThrows` | `lock.block(timeout)` with no callback throws `LockTimeoutException` when the lock was not taken in time. Off: it gives `false`. Set `lock.throwOnTimeout` to pick for one lock. |

```dart
CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: 'redis',
  stores: stores,
  flags: const CacheFlags(lockThrows: true),
);
```

Options of each driver:

| Driver | Option | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| all | `driver` | `String` | required | `file`, `memory`, `redis` or `null` |
| all | `prefix` | `String` | `dox_cache:` | Text in front of every key. |
| `file` | `path` | `String` | `storage/cache` | Folder of the cache files. |
| `memory` | `max_size` | `int` | no limit | Most items in the map. |
| `redis` | `host` | `String` | `127.0.0.1` | Redis host. |
| `redis` | `port` | `int` | `6379` | Redis port. |
| `redis` | `username` | `String` | none | Redis user. |
| `redis` | `password` | `String` | none | Redis password. |
| `redis` | `db` | `int` | `0` | Redis database number. |
| `redis` | `tls` | `bool` | `false` | Use TLS. |
| `redis` | `pool_size` | `int` | `10` | Most connections per store. |

## StorageConfig

`StorageProvider` of the `dox_storage` package takes it. See [File storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md).
Source: `lib/src/dox/storage_config.dart` in [dartondox/dox-storage](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-storage).

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `defaultDisk` | `String` | `'local'` | The disk `Storage()` uses when no disk is named. |
| `disks` | `Map<String, Map<String, dynamic>>` | `{'local': {'driver': 'local', 'root': 'storage'}}` | Disk name to options. Each disk needs a `driver` option. |

Options of each driver:

| Driver | Option | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| all | `driver` | `String` | required | `local`, `s3` or `memory` |
| `local` | `root` | `String` | `storage` | Folder of the files. |
| `local` | `url` | `String` | none | Base of the public URLs, like `http://localhost:3000/files`. |
| `local` | `app_key` | `String` | `AppConfig.appKey` | Key that signs the URLs. |
| `local` | `visibility` | `String` | `public` | `public` or `private`. |
| `local` | `atomic_writes` | `bool` | `false` | Write to a temp file, then rename it. |
| `local` | `permissions` | `bool` or `Map` | off | Visibility is the file mode. See [File storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md#config). |
| `s3` | `bucket` | `String` | required | Bucket name. |
| `s3` | `region` | `String` | `us-east-1` | Region. |
| `s3` | `key` | `String` | required | Access key id. |
| `s3` | `secret` | `String` | required | Secret access key. |
| `s3` | `token` | `String` | none | Session token. |
| `s3` | `endpoint` | `String` | none | Custom endpoint (R2, MinIO, Spaces). |
| `s3` | `path_style` | `bool` | `false` | Use path style URLs. |
| `s3` | `url` | `String` | none | Base of the public URLs. |
| `s3` | `visibility` | `String` | `private` | `public` or `private`. |
| `s3` | `acl` | `bool` | `true` | The service supports ACLs. |
| `s3` | `batch_delete` | `bool` | `true` | The service supports batch delete. |

An unknown driver throws `ArgumentError('Storage disk "<name>" has unknown driver "<type>"')`.

## OpenApiConfig

Source: `packages/dox-core/lib/openapi/openapi_config.dart`.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `bool?` | `null` | Serve the docs routes. `null` means: on only when `APP_ENV` is `development` or `local`. An empty `APP_ENV` counts as production. |
| `info` | `Info` | `Info(title: 'Dox API', version: '1.0.0')` | Title and version of the API. |
| `servers` | `List<Server>` | `[]` | Base URLs of the API. |
| `securitySchemes` | `Map<String, SecurityScheme>` | `{}` | Ways to log in, like `{'bearerAuth': SecurityScheme.bearer()}`. |
| `securityByMiddleware` | `Map<String, List<Map<String, List<String>>>>` | `{}` | Security for routes that use a middleware class with this name. It wins over `@Security` on the class. A class name that ends with `AuthMiddleware` gets `bearerAuth` when it has neither. |
| `registry` | `OpenApiRegistry` | `OpenApiRegistry()` (empty) | What `dox_builder` found in the code. Pass `openApiRegistry` from `lib/generated/openapi.g.dart`. |
| `ui` | `DocsUi` | `DocsUi.scalar` | `scalar` or `swagger`. |
| `scalar` | `ScalarOptions` | `ScalarOptions()` | Options of the Scalar page. See below. |
| `pageTitle` | `String?` | `null` (uses `info.title`) | Title of the `/docs` page. |
| `include` | `List<String>` | `[]` (all routes) | Only routes with these paths are in the docs, like `['/api/*']`. A `*` at the end matches the rest of the path. |
| `exclude` | `List<String>` | `[]` | Routes with these paths are left out. Checked after `include`. |

`ScalarOptions` (`lib/src/docs_ui.dart` in [dartondox/dox-openapi](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-openapi)):

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `theme` | `ScalarTheme` | `ScalarTheme.default_` | One of `default_`, `alternate`, `moon`, `purple`, `solarized`, `bluePlanet`, `deepSpace`, `saturn`, `kepler`, `elysiajs`, `fastify`, `mars`, `laserwave`, `none`. |
| `darkMode` | `bool` | `false` | Start in dark mode. |
| `showDownloadButton` | `bool` | `true` | Show the download button for the OpenAPI document. |
| `proxyUrl` | `String?` | `null` | Send "Try it" requests through this proxy. |

## SocketIoConfig

`SocketIoProvider` of the `dox_socketio` package takes it. See [Socket.IO](../packages/socketio.md).
Source: `lib/src/dox/socket_io_config.dart` in [dartondox/dox-socketio](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-socketio).

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `bool` | `true` | Mount Socket.IO on the HTTP port at `/socket.io/`. |
| `options` | `ServerOptions` | `ServerOptions()` | Engine options. See below. |
| `namespaces` | `List<NamespaceHandler>` | `[]` | Namespaces to register, like `ChatNamespace()`. |
| `adapter` | `SocketAdapterFactory?` | `null` (in memory with one isolate, `IsolateAdapter` with many) | Makes the adapter in each isolate. Use a Redis adapter with many servers. |

`ServerOptions` (`lib/src/engine/server_options.dart` in dox-socketio). The defaults match the Node.js server.

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `String` | `/socket.io/` | URL path. Must end with `/`. |
| `pingInterval` | `Duration` | 25 s | Time between two server pings. |
| `pingTimeout` | `Duration` | 20 s | Time to wait for a pong before the session is closed. |
| `upgradeTimeout` | `Duration` | 10 s | Time a websocket upgrade may take. |
| `connectTimeout` | `Duration` | 45 s | Time a client has to join a namespace after the handshake. |
| `maxHttpBufferSize` | `int` | `1000000` | Biggest message in bytes a client may send. |
| `maxAttachments` | `int` | `10` | Most binary attachments in one packet. A packet with more closes that client. |
| `transports` | `List<String>` | `['polling', 'websocket']` | Allowed transports. |
| `allowUpgrades` | `bool` | `true` | Allow upgrades from polling to websocket. |
| `cors` | `CorsOptions?` | `null` (no CORS headers) | CORS for the long-polling requests. |

`CorsOptions`:

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `origins` | `List<String>` | `['*']` | Allowed origins. |
| `credentials` | `bool` | `false` | Send `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. |
| `methods` | `List<String>` | `['GET', 'POST']` | Allowed methods for preflight. |
| `allowedHeaders` | `List<String>?` | `null` (the requested headers) | Allowed request headers. |
| `maxAge` | `Duration?` | `null` | How long a browser may cache the preflight answer. |

## DatabaseConfig

The database is not a field of `AppConfig`. A provider calls `SqlQueryBuilder.initializeWithDatabaseConfig(databaseConfig)` in its `setup()`.
Source: `packages/dox-orm/lib/src/types/database_config.dart` and `connection_config.dart` in [dartondox/dox-orm](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-orm).

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `connection` | `String` | required | Name of the connection to use. A missing name throws `Exception('<name> not found')`. |
| `connections` | `Map<String, ConnectionConfig>` | required | Connection name to config. |

`ConnectionConfig`:

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `driver` | `Driver` | required | `Driver.postgres`, `Driver.mysql` (also MariaDB) or `Driver.sqlite`. |
| `host` | `String` | `'localhost'` | Database host. Not used by sqlite. |
| `port` | `int` | `0` | Database port. Not used by sqlite. |
| `user` | `String` | `''` | Database user. Not used by sqlite. |
| `password` | `String` | `''` | Database password. Not used by sqlite. |
| `database` | `String` | required | Database name. For sqlite: the file path, or `:memory:`. |
| `useSSL` | `bool` | `false` | Use TLS. Postgres: mode `require` (no certificate check), set `extra['sslMode']` to change it. MySQL: the certificate is checked. |
| `debug` | `bool` | required | Print every query with `printer`. |
| `printer` | `QueryPrinter?` | `null` | `ConsoleQueryPrinter()`, `PrettyQueryPrinter()`, `FileQueryPrinter(file: File('queries.log'))` or your own. `FileQueryPrinter(file: ..., buffered: true)` writes in the background, so a query does not wait for the disk. Then call `await printer.flush()` before `exit()`, or the last lines are lost. |
| `logRedact` | `List<String>` | `[]` | Names of values to hide in the query log. A value shows as `***` when its key ends with one of these names, in any case. `['password', 'token']` hides `password`, `users.password` and `remember_token`. Only the log changes. The query gets the real values. The list of the default connection counts for every query. The list of a named connection counts too, for the queries on that connection. |
| `slowQueryMs` | `int?` | `null` | Log each query that takes longer than this many milliseconds, with `printer`. `0` logs every query. `null` turns it off. It works with `debug` off. Values named in `logRedact` show as `***`. A failed query is not logged. |
| `read` | `List<Map<String, dynamic>>?` | `null` | Read replica hosts. Each map can change `host`, `port`, `user`, `password`, `database` and `extra`. See [Read replicas](../database/replicas.md). |
| `write` | `Map<String, dynamic>?` | `null` | Settings of the write host, in the same form as one `read` map. Only used with `read`. |
| `sticky` | `bool` | `false` | With `read`: after a write, the reads of the same request go to the write host. |
| `extra` | `Map<String, dynamic>` | `{}` | Driver options. See below. |
| `driverFactory` | `DBDriver Function(ConnectionConfig)?` | `null` | Your own driver class. It wins over every other setting. |

Keys of `extra`:

| Driver | Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| postgres, mysql | `maxConnectionCount` | `int` | `10` | Most open connections, for the whole process. |
| postgres, mysql | `threads` | `int` | `1` | Rust threads of the native driver. Only the first pool sets it. |
| postgres, mysql | `requestTimeout` | `Duration` | 300 s | The longest wait for one request (a free connection, the connect and the query). Over it, the request fails. |
| postgres, mysql | `maxConnectionAge` | `Duration` | none on Postgres, 12 hours on MySQL | Close a connection older than this, once it has no query. |
| postgres, mysql | `idleTimeout` | `Duration` | no limit on Postgres, 12 hours on MySQL | Close a free connection that is not used for this long. |
| mysql | `serverKill` | `bool` | `true` | Stop a cancelled or timed out query on the server with `KILL`. Set `false` behind a proxy like ProxySQL. |
| mysql, sqlite | `preparedStatementCacheSize` | `int` | `100` | Prepared statements kept per connection. |
| postgres | `sslMode` | `String` | `require` with `useSSL`, else `disable` | TLS mode: `disable`, `prefer`, `require` or `verify-full`. |
| postgres | `sslRootCert` | `String` | none | Path of a PEM file with the CA certificates to trust for `verify-full`. `sslrootcert` in `DATABASE_URL`. |
| postgres | `sslWarning` | `bool` | `true` | `false` hides the warning that Dox prints (once per isolate) when TLS mode is `require`. `sslWarning=false` in `DATABASE_URL` works too. |
| postgres | `timeZone` | `String` | `UTC` | Session time zone. |
| postgres | `applicationName` | `String` | none | Name of the app in `pg_stat_activity`. |
| mysql | `verifyCertificate` | `bool` | `true` | `false` skips the TLS certificate check. Only for a self-signed certificate in development. |
| sqlite | `busyTimeout` | `int` | `5000` | `PRAGMA busy_timeout` in milliseconds. |
| sqlite | `background` | `bool` | `false` | `true` (or `1`, `'true'`, `'1'`, so `?background=true` in `DATABASE_URL` works) runs the queries in a helper isolate, so a slow query does not block the request isolate. Each query costs one message hop. See [SQLite](../database/index.md#run-queries-in-a-helper-isolate). |

A time key takes a `Duration`, or a number of seconds. See [Pool settings](../database/index.md#pool-settings).

## AuthConfig

Auth is not a field of `AppConfig`. A provider calls `Auth.initialize(AuthConfig(...))` in its `setup()`.
Source: `lib/src/interfaces.dart` in [dartondox/dox-auth](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-auth).

| Class | Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AuthConfig` | `defaultGuard` | `String` | required | The guard `Auth()` uses when no guard is named. |
| `AuthConfig` | `guards` | `Map<String, AuthGuard>` | `{}` | Guard name to guard. |
| `AuthGuard` | `driver` | `AuthDriver` | required | How a token is made and checked, like `JwtAuthDriver(secret: SecretKey(...))`. |
| `AuthGuard` | `provider` | `AuthProvider` | required | Where users come from. |
| `AuthProvider` | `model` | `dynamic Function()` | required | Makes the user model, like `() => User()`. |
| `AuthProvider` | `identifierFields` | `List<String>` | `['email']` | Columns `attempt()` matches the login with. |
| `AuthProvider` | `passwordField` | `String` | `'password'` | Column with the bcrypt hash. |

## Full example

The config files of a new project. They read their values from `env`, the typed env class in `lib/config/env.dart` (see [Env reference](env.md)).

```dart title="lib/config/app.dart"
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/cache.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/cors.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/logger.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';
import 'package:my_app/generated/container.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  /// Changing the key makes old cookies and encrypted data unreadable.
  appKey: env.appKey,
  serverPort: env.appPort,
  totalIsolate: env.appTotalIsolate ?? Platform.numberOfProcessors,
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    LogMiddleware(enabled: env.appEnv != 'production'),
  ],
  container: registerContainer,
  cache: cache,
  cors: cors,
  logger: logger,
);
```

```dart title="lib/config/cache.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

CacheConfig cache = CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: env.cacheStore,
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},

    /// one map per isolate, fast, not shared
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 10000},
  },
);
```

```dart title="lib/config/logger.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

LoggerConfig logger = LoggerConfig(
  name: env.appName,
  enabled: true,
  level: env.logLevel,
  /// colored text is slow. JSON lines in production.
  // Env.appEnv, not appConfig.isDevelopment: appConfig is built from
  // this logger, so reading appConfig here would loop.
  prettyPrint: Env.appEnv == 'development',
);
```

```dart title="lib/config/database.dart"
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/app.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

/// Print every SQL query only in development.
bool _debug = appConfig.isDevelopment;

DatabaseConfig databaseConfig = DatabaseConfig(
  connection: env.dbConnection,
  connections: <String, ConnectionConfig>{
    'postgres': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.postgres,
      host: env.dbHost,
      port: env.dbPort ?? 5432,
      user: env.dbUsername,
      password: env.dbPassword,
      database: env.dbName,
      extra: <String, dynamic>{
        /// One pool for all isolates.
        'maxConnectionCount': 10,
        'maxConnectionAge': Duration(hours: 1),
      },
      debug: _debug,
      printer: PrettyQueryPrinter(),
    ),

    /// MySQL and MariaDB
    'mysql': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.mysql,
      host: env.dbHost,
      port: env.dbPort ?? 3306,
      user: env.dbUsername,
      password: env.dbPassword,
      database: env.dbName,
      extra: <String, dynamic>{'collation': 'utf8mb4_general_ci'},
      debug: _debug,
      printer: PrettyQueryPrinter(),
    ),

    /// `DB_NAME` is a file path, or `:memory:`.
    'sqlite': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.sqlite,
      database: env.dbName,
      debug: _debug,
      printer: PrettyQueryPrinter(),
    ),
  },
);
```

```dart title="lib/config/cors.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

CORSConfig cors = CORSConfig(
  enabled: false,
  // a list: Dox sends back the request origin only when it is in the list
  origin: <String>['http://localhost:3000'],
  methods: <String>['GET', 'HEAD', 'POST', 'PUT', 'PATCH', 'DELETE'],
  headers: <String>[
    'accept',
    'authorization',
    'content-type',
    'x-csrf-token',
    'x-xsrf-token',
    'x-requested-with',
  ],
  exposeHeaders: <String>[
    'cache-control',
    'content-language',
    'content-type',
    'expires',
    'last-modified',
    'pragma',
  ],
  credentials: true,
  maxAge: 90,
);
```

Do not use `origin: '*'` together with `credentials: true`.
With credentials the browser sends cookies, so it does not accept `*`, and the call fails.
Dox does not send back any origin in place of `*`, because that would let every site call the app with the user's cookies.
`'*'` is fine for a public API with `credentials: false` (or not set).

```dart title="lib/providers/orm_provider.dart"
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/database.dart';

/// Dox finds it by itself and runs it in every isolate.
/// No database? Delete this file.
class ORMProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  Future<void> setup() async {
    SqlQueryBuilder.initializeWithDatabaseConfig(databaseConfig);
  }

  @override
  Future<void> shutdown() async {
    await SqlQueryBuilder.close();
  }
}
```

A new project also has `lib/config/storage.dart`, `queue.dart` and `schedule.dart`, with a provider for each in `lib/providers/`. See [File storage](../digging-deeper/file-storage.md), [Queue](../digging-deeper/queue.md) and [Scheduler](../digging-deeper/scheduler.md).

A new project has no `openapi.dart`, `socketio.dart` or auth provider. You add them when you need them. See [OpenAPI](../packages/openapi.md), [Socket.IO](../packages/socketio.md) and [Authentication](../security/authentication.md).

# CLI

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/reference/cli/

# CLI

Every `dox` command, with its options and the files it writes.

The CLI lives in the [dox-cli](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-cli) repo. The paths below are in that repo. The commands come from `lib/src/command_registry.dart`. The file templates are Dart strings inside `lib/src/tools/`. The path of each template is given below.

How to install the CLI is on the [Dox CLI](../digging-deeper/dox-cli.md) page.

Rules that apply to every command:

- `dox` with no command prints ``Could not find a command. Run `dox help` for more information.`` and exits with code 1.
- An unknown command prints ``Could not find a command named "<name>". Run `dox help` for more information.``, and a hint about the `dox: commands:` key. It exits with code 1.
- A command that is not built in can come from a package or from the app. See [Package commands](../digging-deeper/package-commands.md).
- Too few or too many arguments prints `Invalid number of arguments for command "<name>".` with the expected count.
- A name you pass is turned into `snake_case` for the file and `PascalCase` for the class. `BlogPost` and `blog_post` give the same result.
- Many `make:*` commands also answer to a `create:*` name, like `create:model`. `dox help <command>` shows the aliases.
- A `make:*` command does not overwrite. When the file exists it prints `<name> already exists` and stops.

## Project

### `dox create`

```
dox create <project_name> [--version <version>]
```

Makes a new project from the [dox-sample](https://github.com/dartondox/dox-sample) repo.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--version <v>` (or `--v`) | A release tag of `dox-sample` to clone. Without it, the newest `dox-sample` release with the same major version as the CLI is used. |

What it does:

1. Turns the name into `snake_case`. Stops with `Folder name "<name>" already exist` when the folder is there.
2. Picks the release (see `--version` above) from the release list of `dartondox/dox-sample`.
3. Runs `git clone --depth 1 --branch v<version> https://github.com/dartondox/dox-sample.git <name>`.
4. Deletes the `.git` folder.
5. Replaces `dox_sample` with your project name in every text file, except files under `bin/dox`.
6. Copies `.env.example` to `.env` and writes a new random `APP_KEY` to it, like `dox key:generate`. It skips this step when `.env` is already there.
7. Prints the next steps: `cd <name>`, `dart pub get` and `dox serve`.

Needs `curl` and `git` on the `PATH`. When it can not find a release (no network), it prints `Could not find a template release for Dox <version>. Check your network, or pass --version.`

The new project already has `bin/server.dart`, `bin/migrate.dart`, `bin/seed.dart`, `bin/queue.dart` and `bin/schedule.dart`. So the migration, seed, queue and schedule commands below work in it right away.

Source: `lib/src/tools/create_project.dart`.

### `dox add`

```
dox add <package> [--dev] [options]
```

Adds a Dox package and sets it up. `orm` is short for `dox_orm`.
It runs `dart pub add`, then `dart pub get`, then the `<package>:install` command of the package with the options, like `dox add orm --driver=postgres`.
A package with no `<package>:install` command is only added.
See [Add a package](../getting-started/add-a-package.md).

Source: `lib/src/tools/add_package.dart`.

### `dox serve`

```
dox serve [--no-reload] [--ignore-build-runner]
dox s
dox server
```

Starts the dev server.

`dox serve --port=...` does not set the port. Dox ignores it and prints a warning. Set `APP_PORT` in `.env`, or run `APP_PORT=9000 dox serve`.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--no-reload` | Turn hot reload off. Every change restarts the server. |
| `--ignore-build-runner` | Do not start `dart run build_runner watch`. |

You can use both options together.

What it does:

1. Starts `dart run --resident bin/server.dart` and prints its output. The `--resident` flag keeps a background compiler that only recompiles changed files. So restarts are fast. `dox serve` stops that compiler when it exits.
2. Runs the server with the Dart VM service on a free port on `localhost`. Hot reload needs it. The server prints the VM service link at start. Open it in a browser to get DevTools: the debugger, the CPU profiler and memory snapshots. VS Code can also attach to the VM service address ("Dart: Attach to Dart Process").
3. When the server is up, starts `dart run build_runner watch` (unless the option is set).
4. Watches the project folder. It ignores `build/` and hidden folders like `.dart_tool/`. It waits until no file changed for 200 ms. With build_runner, a restart also waits for the generated files. A hot reload does not wait for build_runner.

What happens on a change:

| Changed | Result |
| --- | --- |
| A `.dart` file in `lib/app/` (not `.g.dart`) | Hot reload. The new code runs in the server at once, in about 0.1 to 0.2 seconds. |
| Routes, providers, config, `lib/generated/`, `bin/`, `db/` or a generated `.g.dart` file | The server restarts, because this code or data is built only at start. |
| A hot reload that fails, for example a compile error | The server restarts. |

Hot reload does not run code again that already ran once. For example, a changed static or global value keeps its old value until a restart. Use `--no-reload` if you do not want this.
With build_runner, one save gives one restart, after the generated files are written.

Source: `lib/src/tools/server_serve.dart`.

### `dox build`

```
dox build
```

AOT compiles the app for production into `build/bundle`. Use this in production, not `dart run`.

What it does:

1. When `pubspec.yaml` contains `build_runner`: runs `dart run build_runner build`. Stops with exit code 1 when it fails.
2. Runs `dart build cli --target bin/server.dart --output build`.
3. When `bin/queue.dart` or `bin/schedule.dart` exists: builds it the same way, to `build/bundle/bin/queue` and `build/bundle/bin/schedule`.
4. Deletes the old `build/bundle/db`, then copies `db/` to `build/bundle/db`. It leaves out SQLite files (`*.sqlite`, `*.sqlite3`, `*.db`, and their `-wal`, `-shm`, `-journal` and `.lock` files), so your local data does not go to production.
5. Copies `.env.example` to `build/bundle/.env.example`.
6. Prints `[Dox] Built build/bundle. Run it with: cd build/bundle && ./bin/server`.

Output:

| Path | What |
| --- | --- |
| `build/bundle/bin/server` | the native binary, no Dart SDK needed |
| `build/bundle/bin/queue` | the queue worker, when `bin/queue.dart` exists |
| `build/bundle/bin/schedule` | the scheduler, when `bin/schedule.dart` exists |
| `build/bundle/lib/` | native libraries from build hooks (SQLite, `dox_http_native`, ...) |
| `build/bundle/db/` | your migrations and seeders. SQLite files are not copied. |
| `build/bundle/.env.example` | copy it to `.env` or set real env vars |

`dart compile exe` can not build packages with build hooks, so the CLI uses `dart build cli`.

Source: `lib/src/tools/server_serve.dart` (`buildServer`).

### `dox build_runner:build` and `dox build_runner:watch`

```
dox build_runner:build
dox build_runner:watch
```

Run `dart run build_runner build` once, or `dart run build_runner watch`. No options.
`build_runner:build` prints only the first line of each output block of build_runner. Run `dart run build_runner build` yourself to see all of it.
The CLI does not pass `--delete-conflicting-outputs` (build_runner removed that flag).

### `dox key:generate`

```
dox key:generate [--show] [--force]
```

Makes a 32 character key (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, from `Random.secure()`) and writes it to `APP_KEY` in `.env`.
Prints `<key> : Key have been updated successfully in .env!`.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--show` | Print a new key and write nothing. |
| `--force` | Skip the question below. |

When `APP_ENV=production`, a new key logs every user out. In a terminal the command asks first. Without a terminal it prints a warning and runs. If you answer no, it prints `Stopped. APP_KEY was not changed.` and exits with code 1.

What it does with `.env`:

- Reads `.env` in the current folder. The file must exist, else the command fails with a file error.
- Replaces the value of `APP_KEY`. Every other line stays as it is, in the same order. This keeps comments, blank lines, quotes and values with more than one `=` (like `DATABASE_URL=postgres://u:p@h/db?a=b`).
- Adds `APP_KEY=<key>` as the first line when there is no `APP_KEY`.

Source: `lib/src/tools/generate_key.dart`.

### `dox env:generate`

```
dox env:generate
```

Writes `lib/config/env.dart`, the typed env class, from `.env.example`.

- Stops with `.env.example is missing.` (exit code 1) when there is no example file.
- Stops with `lib/config/env.dart is already there. Delete it to make it again.` (exit code 1) when the file exists.
- Prints ``Run `dart run build_runner build` to make env.g.dart.`` when done.

Rules for each key: a whole number (like `3000` or `-1`) gives `int get x => <value>;`, `true`/`false` give `bool get x => <value>;`, an empty value gives `String? get x;`, any other value gives `String get x;` (required, no default). `#` comment lines above a key become its doc comment. A key that does not map back from `camelCase` gets `@EnvKey('KEY')`.

Source: `lib/src/tools/env_tools.dart` (`EnvScaffold`).

### `dox env:check`

```
dox env:check
```

Loads `AppEnv` from `lib/config/env.dart` with the real environment and `.env`. Prints `The env is valid.` or an `EnvException` with every missing or bad key (exit code 1).

It writes a small script to `.dart_tool/dox/env_check.dart` and runs it with `dart run`. It needs `lib/config/env.dart` and a `name:` in `pubspec.yaml`.
Without `lib/config/env.dart` it prints ``lib/config/env.dart is missing. Run `dox env:generate` first.`` (exit code 1).

Source: `lib/src/tools/env_tools.dart` (`envCheck`).

### `dox openapi:generate`

```
dox openapi:generate [dir]
```

Runs `dart run bin/openapi.dart [dir]`. That file writes `openapi.json` and `openapi.yaml` into `dir` (default `storage/openapi`).
A new project has no `bin/openapi.dart`. You add it yourself, see [OpenAPI](../packages/openapi.md).
When the file is not there, the command prints `bin/openapi.dart is missing.` and the code to put in it (exit code 1).

Source: `lib/src/tools/openapi_generate.dart`.

### `dox update`

```
dox update
```

Installs the newest CLI with the same major version as the one you have.
It reads the version list from pub.dev (retracted versions are skipped), then runs `dart pub global activate dox <version>`.
Needs `curl` on the `PATH`.

Source: `lib/src/tools/update_dox.dart`.

### `dox version`

```
dox version
dox v
dox -v
dox --version
```

Prints `Dox version: <version>`. Aliases: `--version`, `-version`, `v`, `-v`, `--v`.

### `dox help`

```
dox help [command]
dox --help
dox -h
```

Aliases: `--help`, `-h`. Without a command: lists every command by category. With a command: prints its usage, description, category, aliases and argument count.

## Create files

### `dox make:controller`

```
dox make:controller <name> [-r|--resource] [--api] [--model=<model>]
```

Alias: `create:controller`. Some other `make:*` commands have a `create:*` alias too. The Command list table at the end shows which.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `-r` or `--resource` | A resource controller with `index`, `create`, `store`, `show`, `edit`, `update`, `destroy`. |
| `--api` | A resource controller without `create` and `edit`, the two form pages. `Route.resource` makes no route for them. |
| `--model=<model>` or `--model <model>` | A resource controller that uses the model. It imports `package:<app>/app/models/<model>/<model>.model.dart`. `index` returns all rows, and `store` creates a row from `req.body`. `show`, `edit`, `update` and `destroy` take the model as a parameter, so [route model binding](../the-basic/dependency-injection.md#route-model-binding) loads it by the `{id}`. |

`--api` and `--model` work together. Each one makes a resource controller, also without `-r`.
With `--model`, the CLI prints a warning when the model file does not exist yet.
Any other option prints `Unknown option <x> for make:controller.` (exit code 1), and no file is made.

A trailing `Controller` in the name is removed: `UserController` and `User` give the same file.

| Form | Writes | Template |
| --- | --- | --- |
| plain | `lib/app/http/controllers/<name>.controller.dart` | `_getSample` in `lib/src/tools/create_controller.dart` |
| `-r`, `--api`, `--model` | `lib/app/http/controllers/<name>.controller.dart` | `_getResourceSample` in the same file |

The class has `@Inject()`, so the container makes it. A comment shows the route to add, like `Route.get('path', (BlogController c) => c.index);`. A resource controller gets `Route.resource('path', BlogController);`.
After the file is made, the CLI tells you to run `dart run build_runner build`. That adds the controller to `lib/generated/container.g.dart`.

### `dox make:middleware`

```
dox make:middleware <name>
```

Writes `lib/app/http/middleware/<name>.middleware.dart`: a class `<Name>Middleware implements IDoxMiddleware` with a `handle(IDoxRequest req)` that returns `req`.
A trailing `Middleware` in the name is removed.

Template: `_getSample` in `lib/src/tools/create_middleware.dart`.

### `dox make:dto`

```
dox make:dto <name>
```

Writes `lib/app/dtos/<name>/<name>.dto.dart`: a `@Dto()` class with one `name` field and `part '<name>.dto.g.dart';`.
The class name has no `Dto` at the end: `dox make:dto CreateBlog` gives the class `CreateBlog` in `lib/app/dtos/create_blog/create_blog.dto.dart`.
A trailing `Dto` in the name is removed. Prints ``Run `dox build_runner:build` to make <name>/<name>.dto.g.dart.``

Template: `_getSample` in `lib/src/tools/create_dto.dart`.

### `dox make:serializer`

```
dox make:serializer <name>
```

Writes `lib/app/serializers/<name>.serializer.dart`: a class `<Name>Serializer extends Serializer<<Name>>`. It imports the model with `package:<app>/app/models/<name>/<name>.model.dart`.
A trailing `Serializer` in the name is removed.

Template: `_getSample` in `lib/src/tools/create_serializer.dart`.

### `dox make:provider`

```
dox make:provider <name>
```

Writes `lib/providers/<name>_provider.dart`: a class `<Name>Provider extends DoxProvider` with an empty `setup()` and an optional `shutdown()`.
A trailing `Provider` in the name is removed: `dox make:provider Cache` gives `CacheProvider` in `lib/providers/cache_provider.dart`.
Prints ``Run `dox build_runner:build` to add it to the container.`` Dox finds the provider after that. See [Providers](../digging-deeper/providers.md).

Template: `createProvider` in `lib/src/tools/make_files.dart`.

### `dox make:command`

```
dox make:command <name>
```

Writes `lib/app/commands/<name>_command.dart`: a class `<Name>Command extends Command`. Its name is `app:<name>`, and `_` in the name becomes `-`. So `dox make:command send_report` makes the command `app:send-report`.
A trailing `Command` in the name is removed.

It also does two more things:

- It adds the class to the `commands` list in `lib/app/commands/commands.dart`. It makes that file when it is missing.
- It adds `commands: package:<app>/app/commands/commands.dart` under `dox:` in `pubspec.yaml`, when that key is not set.

Then it prints ``Run `dart pub get`, then `dox app:send-report`.``

It makes all the changes or none. When `pubspec.yaml` or `commands.dart` is not in the shape it expects, it prints what to add by hand, exits with code 1 and writes nothing. When `dox: commands:` already points to another library, it does the same.

See [Package commands](../digging-deeper/package-commands.md#add-a-command-to-your-app).

Template: `createCommand` in `lib/src/tools/make_files.dart`.

### `dox make:mail`

```
dox make:mail <name> [--no-view]
```

| Form | Writes |
| --- | --- |
| plain | `lib/app/mail/<name>_mail.dart` and the view `resources/views/emails/<name>.dox.html` |
| `--no-view` | `lib/app/mail/<name>_mail.dart` only, with a plain text body |

The class is `<Name>Mail extends Mailable`. It takes the recipient `Address` in its constructor. A comment shows how to send it and how to queue it. A trailing `Mail` in the name is removed.
With the view, the mail has `view` set to `emails/<name>` and a `data` map with `name`. With `--no-view`, it has a `text` getter.
It makes both files or none.

After it writes the files, it prints a hint for each package that `pubspec.yaml` does not have yet: `dox_mailer`, and `dox_view` when there is a view.
With a view, it also prints that the default view settings work (`resources/views`), and that you only add a `ViewProvider` with a `ViewConfig` to change them.

See [Mail](../digging-deeper/mail.md#mailables).

Template: `createMail` in `lib/src/tools/make_files.dart`.

### `dox make:view`

```
dox make:view <name>
```

Writes `resources/views/<name>.dox.html` with a small sample: `<h1>Hello, {{ name }}</h1>`.
A name with `/` makes a folder: `dox make:view emails/welcome` writes `resources/views/emails/welcome.dox.html`.
Each part of the name becomes `snake_case`: `Pages/About` gives `resources/views/pages/about.dox.html`.

See [Views](../the-basic/views.md).

Template: `createView` in `lib/src/tools/make_files.dart`.

### `dox make:test`

```
dox make:test <name> [--unit]
```

| Form | Writes |
| --- | --- |
| plain | `test/<name>_test.dart` that starts the app with `DoxTestClient` and checks `GET /ping` for status 200. Change the path to match your route. |
| `--unit` | `test/<name>_test.dart` with a plain `package:test` test. It does not start the app. |

A trailing `Test` in the name is removed.

See [Testing](../digging-deeper/testing.md).

Template: `createTest` in `lib/src/tools/make_files.dart`.

### `dox make:model`

```
dox make:model <name> [-m] [-c] [-r] [-f] [-s] [-a] [--api]
dox create:model <name> [-m] [-c] [-r] [-f] [-s] [-a] [--api]
```

Writes `lib/app/models/<name>/<name>.model.dart`: a `@DoxModel(table: '<plural snake name>')` class with `part '<name>.model.g.dart';`. `BlogPost` gives `blog_posts`. The class has an empty `fillable` list. Add your columns to it.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `-m` or `--migration` | Also make a `create_<table>_table` migration. |
| `-c` or `--controller` | Also make a plain controller, `<name>.controller.dart`. |
| `-r` or `--resource` | Also make a resource controller that uses the model. |
| `--api` | Also make a resource controller without `create` and `edit`, that uses the model. |
| `-f` or `--factory` | Also make a factory, `db/factories/<name>.factory.dart`. |
| `-s` or `--seed` | Also make a seeder, `db/seeders/<name>.seeder.dart`. |
| `-a` or `--all` | Also make the migration, the factory, the seeder and a resource controller. |

You can join short options: `-mcr` is the same as `-m -c -r`. With `-c` and `-r` together, the controller is a resource controller.

Each extra file is the same as the one from the single command:

| Command | Same file as |
| --- | --- |
| `dox make:model Post -m` | `dox make:migration create_posts_table` |
| `dox make:model Post -c` | `dox make:controller Post` |
| `dox make:model Post -r` | `dox make:controller Post -r --model=Post` |
| `dox make:model Post --api` | `dox make:controller Post --api --model=Post` |
| `dox make:model Post -f` | `dox make:factory Post` |
| `dox make:model Post -s` | `dox make:seeder Post` |

When the model file exists, the command prints `<Name> model already exists` and makes no other file.
When one of the other files exists, that file is skipped, the same as with its own command.
Any other option prints `Unknown option <x> for make:model.` (exit code 1), and no file is made.

Template: `_getSample` in `lib/src/tools/create_model.dart`.

### `dox make:migration`

```
dox make:migration <name> [--sql]
dox create:migration <name> [--sql]
```

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--sql` | Make a `.sql` file with `-- up` and `-- down` sections instead of a Dart class. |

Writes `db/migration/<yyyy>_<mm>_<dd>_<hhmmss>_<name>.dart` (or `.sql`). Characters that are not letters, digits or `_` are removed from the name. A second argument other than `--sql` is ignored.

Migrations run sorted by file name. So the new file always sorts after every file already in `db/migration`. When the current time is not later than the newest file (for example, two migrations in the same second), it uses the newest time plus 1 second.

For a Dart migration it also:

- writes `db/migration/migrations.dart`, the registry of every Dart migration in the folder, sorted by name. A file with no class that `extends Migration` is skipped with a warning;
- writes `bin/migrate.dart` when it is missing, and prints `bin/migrate.dart created.`

The Dart template depends on the name:

| Name | `up()` | `down()` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `create_<table>_table` | `schema.create('<table>', ...)` with `id()` and `timestamps()` | `schema.dropIfExists('<table>')` |
| `<x>_to_<table>_table` (also `from`, `in`, `on`) | `schema.table('<table>', ...)` | `schema.table('<table>', ...)` |
| anything else | a comment | a comment |

Templates: `dartMigrationSource`, `migrateEntrySource` and `_sampleSql` in `lib/src/tools/create_migration.dart`.

## Routes

### `dox route:list`

```
dox route:list [--json]
```

Prints every route of the app: method, path, name, handler and middleware. Run it in the app folder.

```
METHOD  PATH           NAME  HANDLER             MIDDLEWARE
GET     /api/ping            ApiController.pong  LogMiddleware
GET     /ping                WebController.pong  LogMiddleware
GET     /docs                serve
GET     /openapi.json        serve
GET     /openapi.yaml        serve

5 routes
```

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--json` | Print the same data as one JSON list. |

```bash
dox route:list --json
```

```json
[{"method":"GET","path":"/api/ping","name":null,"handler":"ApiController.pong","middleware":["LogMiddleware"]}]
```

Each item has `method`, `path`, `name`, `handler` and `middleware`. The example shows the first route only.

How to read the table:

- A controller route shows `Controller.method`. A function shows its name, or `Closure` when it has none.
- Fallback routes have the method `FALLBACK`. Handlers added with `Route.mount` have the method `MOUNT`.
- A `Route.websocket` route shows `WebSocket` as its handler.
- A route with a domain shows the domain in front of the path.

It does not start the server. It writes a small script to `.dart_tool/dox/route_list.dart` and runs it. The script loads the routes of your routers with `Dox().loadRoutes()`.

Providers do not run. A route that a provider adds in `setup()` is not in the list. The Socket.IO mount is one example.

Your `dox_core` must have `Dox().loadRoutes()`.

Errors go to stderr, so `--json` output stays clean for scripts. Without a Dox app in the folder, or with an unknown option, the command exits with code 1.

Source: `lib/src/tools/route_list.dart`.

## Migrations

All `migration:*` commands work the same way:

1. When `bin/migrate.dart` exists: write the registry again, then run `dart run bin/migrate.dart <command> [args]`. Your app code runs, so Dart migrations work.
2. When there is no `bin/migrate.dart` but `db/migration` has Dart files: write `bin/migrate.dart` (the same text as `make:migration` writes, and print `bin/migrate.dart created.`), then go on like step 1. This happens after a package command like `dox queue:table` wrote the first Dart migration.
3. Else: run the `.sql` migrations with `Migrator()` from `dox_migration` in the CLI process.

The database comes from `DATABASE_URL` when it is set. Else it comes from `DB_CONNECTION`, `DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT`, `DB_USERNAME`, `DB_PASSWORD` and `DB_DATABASE` (or `DB_NAME`). See [Environment variables](env.md).
A failed run prints the error and sets exit code 1.

| Command | Aliases | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dox migration:run` | `dox migrate` | Run the migrations that did not run yet. |
| `dox migration:rollback [--step=<count>] [--batch=<number>] [--force]` | `dox migrate:rollback` | Undo the last batch, the last `<count>` migrations, or only batch `<number>`. `--step 2` and `--batch 3` work too. Give `--step` or `--batch`, not both. Any other option prints `Invalid option <x>, use --step=<count>, --batch=<number> or --force` (exit code 1). |
| `dox migration:reset` | `dox migrate:reset` | Undo every migration. |
| `dox migration:refresh` | `dox migrate:refresh` | Undo every migration, then run them all again. |
| `dox migration:fresh` | `dox migrate:fresh` | Drop every table, then run all migrations. |
| `dox migration:status` | `dox migrate:status` | Print which migrations ran, and their batch. |

`--seed` after `migration:run`, `migration:refresh` or `migration:fresh` runs `dox db:seed` when the migrations end well.

`--force` after `migration:rollback`, `migration:reset`, `migration:refresh` or `migration:fresh` skips the question they ask when `APP_ENV=production` and stdin is a terminal. Without a terminal they print a warning and run.

`bin/migrate.dart` takes the same commands: `dart run bin/migrate.dart <run|rollback [--step=n|--batch=n]|reset|refresh|fresh|status>`. With no command it runs `run`.

## Factories and seeders

| Command | Aliases | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dox make:factory <model>` | `dox create:factory` | Make `db/factories/<model>.factory.dart`. It imports the model with the package name of `pubspec.yaml`. |
| `dox make:seeder <name>` | `dox create:seeder` | Make `db/seeders/<name>.seeder.dart`. It writes `db/seeders/seeders.dart` again, and makes `bin/seed.dart` when it is missing. |
| `dox db:seed [--class=<name>]` | | Write `db/seeders/seeders.dart` again, then run `dart run bin/seed.dart [--class=<name>]`. Default seeder: `DatabaseSeeder`. `--class <name>` (with a space) works too. When `bin/seed.dart` is missing, it prints `bin/seed.dart is missing.` (exit code 1). |

Templates: `createFactory` in `lib/src/tools/create_factory.dart`, and `createSeeder` and `seedEntrySource` in `lib/src/tools/create_seeder.dart`.

## Queue

These commands run the app script `bin/queue.dart` with `dart run`. A new project already has it. It uses the `dox_queue` package.
Input, output and errors go straight to your terminal. `Ctrl+C` (SIGINT) and SIGTERM are sent on to the script, so a worker can finish its job and stop. The exit code of the script is the exit code of `dox`.
When `bin/queue.dart` is missing, the command prints how to set it up and exits with code 1.

| Command | Runs | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dox make:job <name>` | | Make `lib/app/jobs/<name>.job.dart` with a `@Job()` class that extends `DoxJob`. A trailing `Job` in the name is removed. Make `bin/queue.dart` when it is missing. Print a hint to add `dox_queue` to `pubspec.yaml` when it is not there, and to run `dox build_runner:build` (it makes `lib/generated/jobs.g.dart`). |
| `dox queue:work [flags]` | `bin/queue.dart work [flags]` | Run the worker. |
| `dox queue:failed` | `bin/queue.dart failed` | List the failed jobs. |
| `dox queue:retry <id\|all>` | `bin/queue.dart retry <id\|all>` | Put one failed job, or all of them, back on the queue. |
| `dox queue:forget <id>` | `bin/queue.dart forget <id>` | Delete one failed job. |
| `dox queue:flush` | `bin/queue.dart flush` | Delete all failed jobs. |
| `dox queue:clear [queue]` | `bin/queue.dart clear [queue]` | Delete the jobs of a queue. The default queue is `default`. |
| `dox queue:restart` | `bin/queue.dart restart` | Make the running workers stop after their current jobs. The workers must share the cache store. |
| `dox queue:prune-failed [--hours=N]` | `bin/queue.dart prune-failed [--hours=N]` | Delete failed jobs older than N hours. The default is 24. |
| `dox queue:table` | | A [package command](../digging-deeper/package-commands.md) of `dox_queue_database`. Make `db/migration/<time>_create_queue_tables.dart`, which calls `QueueTables.up`, `QueueTables.upBatches` and the matching `down` methods. When a `create_queue_tables` migration is already there, it prints so and exits with code 1. |
| `dox auth:tokens-table` | | A [package command](../digging-deeper/package-commands.md) of `dox_auth`. Make a migration for the `auth_access_tokens` table. When a `create_access_tokens_table` migration is already there, it prints so and exits with code 1. |

Flags of `queue:work`, passed on as they are:

| Flag | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--queue=a,b` | `default` | The queues to read, the first one first. |
| `--concurrency=N` | `1` | How many jobs run at the same time in this process. |
| `--once` | off | Run one job, then stop. |
| `--tries=N` | `1` | How many times a job may run before it is marked as failed. A job can set its own `tries`. |
| `--timeout=S` | `60` | Seconds a job may run. |
| `--sleep=S` | `3` | Seconds to wait when the queues are empty. |
| `--stop-when-empty` | off | Stop when the queues are empty. |
| `--timeout-grace=S` | none | After a timeout, wait up to `S` seconds for the old run to end before the next try. |

An unknown flag or command prints the usage and exits with code 64.

Flags of `auth:tokens-table`. They set the same options of `AccessTokenTables.up`:

| Flag | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--uuid` | The users have uuid ids. Set `uuidIds: true` on `AccessTokenAuthDriver` too. |
| `--string-ids` | The users have text ids. Set `stringIds: true` on `AccessTokenAuthDriver` too. Do not use it with `--uuid`. |
| `--users-table=<table>` | Add a foreign key from `tokenable_id` to this table, with cascade delete. |
| `--users-key=<column>` | The column of `--users-table` for the foreign key. Default: `id`. It does nothing without `--users-table`. |

The `bin/queue.dart` of a new project (`<app>` is the `name` in `pubspec.yaml`). The jobs come from `queueConfig` in `lib/config/queue.dart`:

```dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_queue/dox_queue.dart';
import 'package:<app>/config/app.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  exitCode = await QueueWorker(app: appConfig).run(args);
}
```

Templates: `createJob` and `queueEntrySource` in `lib/src/tools/create_job.dart`.

## Schedule

These commands run the app script `bin/schedule.dart` with `dart run`. A new project already has it. They pass the signals, the terminal and the exit code the same way as the queue commands.
When `bin/schedule.dart` is missing, the command prints how to set it up and exits with code 1.

| Command | Runs | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dox schedule:work` | `bin/schedule.dart work` | Run the scheduler and keep it running. |
| `dox schedule:run` | `bin/schedule.dart run` | Run the tasks that are due now, once. |
| `dox schedule:list` | `bin/schedule.dart list` | List the scheduled tasks. |
| `dox schedule:test <name>` | `bin/schedule.dart test <name>` | Run one task now. |
| `dox schedule:clear-cache` | `bin/schedule.dart clear-cache` | Remove the `withoutOverlapping()` locks that a crash left behind. Do not run it while a task really runs. |

You add tasks in `lib/config/schedule.dart`. These are the two files of a new project:

```dart title="lib/config/schedule.dart"
import 'package:dox_scheduler/dox_scheduler.dart';

ScheduleConfig scheduleConfig = const ScheduleConfig();

void schedule(Schedule s) {
  // s.call('cleanup', cleanup).dailyAt('02:00');
}
```

```dart title="bin/schedule.dart"
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_scheduler/dox_scheduler.dart';
import 'package:<app>/config/app.dart';
import 'package:<app>/config/schedule.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  exitCode = await SchedulerRunner(
    schedule: schedule,
    app: appConfig,
    config: scheduleConfig,
  ).run(args);
}
```

See [Scheduler](../digging-deeper/scheduler.md) for the task methods. See [Queue](../digging-deeper/queue.md) for jobs.

# Environment variables

Source: https://dartondox.dev/latest/reference/env/

# Environment variables

Every env var the framework and its packages read.

How to read your own keys with the typed env class is on the [Environment Variables](../digging-deeper/env.md) page.

The code reads env vars in three ways:

- `Env.get()` and `EnvReader` (`dox_core`): a real environment variable wins over the `.env` file.
- `Platform.environment` straight: only the real environment, `.env` is not read.
- `dox_migration` has its own `loadEnv()`: it reads `.env` and the real environment. A real environment variable wins. It reads plain lines like `Env.get()` does (`export`, comments, quotes). It has no `${VAR}` expansion and does not read `.env.testing`.

## Read by the framework

If `APP_ENV` is not set or empty, Dox treats the app as production: `/docs` is off and error details are hidden. Set `APP_ENV=development` in your `.env` and in CI.

| Variable | Who reads it | Default | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `APP_ENV` | `dox_core`, `dox_auth`, `dox_view` | empty | Any value except `development`, `local`, `test` or `testing` (also empty) makes a bad `APP_KEY` a startup error: missing, not exactly 32 characters, or a public sample key. The same rule applies to a JWT secret shorter than 32 bytes (`dox_auth`). In `development`, `local`, `test` and `testing` both are only a warning. `development` or `local` also: show error details in `500` responses and in health check answers, turn the `/docs` routes on when `openApi.enabled` is `null`, and turn the template cache of `dox_view` off. `testing` as a real environment variable also loads `.env.testing` (see below). Read with `Env.get`. | `APP_ENV=production` |
| `APP_NAME` | `dox_core` (`Cache`) | not set | The default `prefix` of a `redis` cache store: `My Shop` gives `my_shop_cache:`. So two apps on one Redis do not share keys. | `APP_NAME="My Shop"` |
| `APP_URL` | `dox_core` (`Route.signedUrl`) | not set | The scheme and host in front of an absolute [signed URL](../security/signed-urls.md). | `APP_URL=https://example.com` |
| `PORT` | `dox_core` (`DoxServer.portFor()`) | not set | The port to listen on, when `APP_PORT` is not set. Cloud Run, Fly, Render and Heroku set it. `APP_PORT` wins when both are set. Read with `Env.get`. | `PORT=8080` |
| `APP_HOST` | `dox_core` (`DoxServer.hostFor()`) | not set (all interfaces, `::`) | The host to listen on. `127.0.0.1` keeps the app off the network, for an app behind a proxy on the same machine. `AppConfig.host` wins over it. Read with `Env.get`. | `APP_HOST=127.0.0.1` |
| `DATABASE_URL` | `dox_orm` (`DatabaseConfig.url`), `dox_migration` | not set | A database url. When it is set, it wins over `DB_CONNECTION` and the other `DB_*` keys. The app reads it through `env.databaseUrl` (the line `url: env.databaseUrl` in `lib/config/database.dart`), from `.env` or the shell. The shell wins. An app without that line reads it only from the shell. See [Database url](../database/index.md#database_url). | `DATABASE_URL=postgres://app:secret@db:5432/blog?sslmode=require` |
| `DB_CONNECTION` | `dox_migration` (`DbConnection.config()`) | sqlite | `sqlite`, `postgres` or `mysql`. Any other value is an error. | `DB_CONNECTION=postgres` |
| `DB_HOST` | `dox_migration` | `localhost` | Database host. A path that starts with `/` is a Unix socket: the folder for Postgres, the socket file for MySQL. | `DB_HOST=127.0.0.1` |
| `DB_PORT` | `dox_migration` | `5432` (postgres), `3306` (mysql) | Database port. | `DB_PORT=5432` |
| `DB_USERNAME` | `dox_migration` | `postgres` (postgres), `root` (mysql) | Database user. | `DB_USERNAME=app` |
| `DB_PASSWORD` | `dox_migration` | `postgres` (postgres), empty (mysql) | Database password. | `DB_PASSWORD=secret` |
| `DB_DATABASE` | `dox_migration` | falls back to `DB_NAME`, then `dox` | Database name. For sqlite: the file path. | `DB_DATABASE=dox` |
| `DB_NAME` | `dox_migration` | `dox` | Same as `DB_DATABASE`. `DB_DATABASE` wins when both are set. | `DB_NAME=dox` |
| `HOME` / `USERPROFILE` | build hooks of `dox_http_native`, `dox_postgres_native`, `dox_mysql_native` | empty | Used to find `~/.cargo/bin/cargo` when the library must be built from source. | set by the OS |
| `DART_VM_OPTIONS` | the Dart VM | not set | Flags for the VM. The AOT binary from `dox build` reads it. Dox never sets VM flags for you. See [Performance](../digging-deeper/performance.md#dart-vm-flags). | `DART_VM_OPTIONS=--new_gen_semi_max_size=64` |

## Read by a new project

A new project (`dox create`) reads these keys through its typed env class, `lib/config/env.dart`. The framework itself does not read them. In code, use the getter: `env.appPort`.

| Variable | Getter | Type | Default | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `APP_NAME` | `appName` | `String` | `dox` | `LoggerConfig.name`. |
| `APP_ENV` | `appEnv` | `String` | `production` | `development`, `staging` or `production`. `appConfig.isDevelopment` is `true` for `development`. It turns on `prettyPrint` of the logger and the query log of the database. Any value except `production` turns on `LogMiddleware` in the new project (one log line per request, if the logger is enabled). Also read by the framework (see above). |
| `APP_PORT` | `appPort` | `int` | `3000` | `AppConfig.serverPort`. When `APP_PORT` is not set, Dox listens on `PORT` if the env has it. |
| `APP_KEY` | `appKey` | `String` | required | `AppConfig.appKey`. It must be exactly 32 characters. Run `dox key:generate` for one. The app stops at start when it is missing, has another length, or is a public sample key (only a warning in `development`, `local`, `test` and `testing`). |
| `APP_TOTAL_ISOLATE` | `appTotalIsolate` | `int?` | not set: one per CPU core | `AppConfig.totalIsolate`. |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | `logLevel` | `String` | `info` | `LoggerConfig.level`. |
| `CACHE_STORE` | `cacheStore` | `String` | `file` | `CacheConfig.defaultStore`. A new project has the stores `file` and `memory` in `lib/config/cache.dart`. Add a `redis` store there before you use it. |
| `STORAGE_DISK` | `storageDisk` | `String` | `local` | `StorageConfig.defaultDisk`. A new project has the disk `local` in `lib/config/storage.dart`. Add an `s3` or `memory` disk there before you use it. |
| `DB_CONNECTION` | `dbConnection` | `String` | `sqlite` | `DatabaseConfig.connection`: `sqlite`, `postgres` or `mysql`. |
| `DB_NAME` | `dbName` | `String` | `db/dox.sqlite` | The database name. For SQLite: the file path. |
| `DB_HOST` | `dbHost` | `String` | `localhost` | Database host. |
| `DB_PORT` | `dbPort` | `int?` | not set: `5432` for Postgres, `3306` for MySQL | Database port. |
| `DB_USERNAME` | `dbUsername` | `String` | `postgres` | Database user. |
| `DB_PASSWORD` | `dbPassword` | `String` | empty | Database password. |

To add a key, add a getter to `AppEnv` and run `dart run build_runner build`. See [Environments](../guides/environments.md#2-add-a-key).

The `.env.example` of a new project:

```ini title=".env.example"
APP_NAME=dox
APP_ENV=development
APP_PORT=3000
APP_KEY=

CACHE_STORE=file
STORAGE_DISK=local

# SQLite needs no setup. The file is created at the first start.
DB_CONNECTION=sqlite
DB_NAME=db/dox.sqlite

# Postgres or MySQL: set DB_CONNECTION=postgres or mysql and fill these in.
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=5432
DB_USERNAME=postgres
DB_PASSWORD=postgres
```

## How `.env` is parsed

`Env.parse()` in `packages/dox-core/lib/env/env.dart`:

- One `KEY=value` per line. The key is trimmed. A line that starts with `#` is a comment.
- The value is everything after the first `=`. A second `=` is kept.
- `#` after a space starts a comment: `KEY=abc # note` gives `abc`. `KEY=abc#def` stays `abc#def`.
- A value in quotes (`"`, `'` or `` ` ``) is kept as it is, also a `#`. The quotes are removed.
- An empty value (`KEY=`), a value with only spaces, or the text `null`, counts as missing. So `Env.get` gives the default.
- `export KEY=value` is read like `KEY=value`.
- With `CoreFlags.envExpand`, `${OTHER}` and `"..."` escapes work. See [Use one value in another](../digging-deeper/env.md#use-one-value-in-another).
- The file is read once per isolate, from the current working directory.
- In tests (`dart test`, or `APP_ENV=testing` as a real environment variable), Dox also reads `.env.testing` next to `.env`. Its keys win over the keys of `.env`. A real environment variable still wins over both.

`dox_migration` has its own simpler parser. It removes every quote character and does not strip `# note` comments. It does not read `.env.testing`. Keep comments on their own line.
